q: Redis 对自己的定位最准确的是？
options: 磁盘上的关系型数据库，靠表和外键组织数据
内存中的「数据结构存储」(data structure store)
面向批量扫描的列式分析引擎，不追求单条低延迟
跨机器切分文件块的分布式文件系统
why: Redis 是用 C 写的内存数据结构存储：数据全在内存里，暴露字符串、哈希、有序集合这些你写代码时就熟悉的结构。
why_en: Redis is an in-memory data structure store written in C, exposing familiar structures like strings, hashes, and sorted sets.
options_en: A disk-based relational database organized around tables and foreign keys
An in-memory data structure store
A columnar analytics engine built for batch scans, not single-record speed
A distributed file system that splits files into blocks across machines
q_en: What best describes how Redis positions itself?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 数据全在内存里、没有表和外键，这是关系型数据库的定位，不是 Redis。
对：内存里放字符串、哈希、有序集合这些数据结构，这才是 Redis 的定位。
错：Redis 追求单条低延迟随机访问，不是批量扫描的列式分析引擎。
错：Redis 存的是内存数据结构，不是切分文件块的分布式文件系统。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis keeps everything in memory with no tables or foreign keys — that fits a relational database, not Redis.
Right: it holds structures like strings, hashes, and sorted sets in memory — that's Redis's actual positioning.
Wrong: Redis is built for low-latency single-record access, not batch-scan columnar analytics.
Wrong: Redis stores in-memory data structures, not file blocks split across machines.

q: Redis 执行命令的并发模型是？
options: 每个连接一个线程
多线程 + 行级锁
单线程逐条执行命令
协程池并行执行
why: Redis 在单线程上一次执行一条命令，天然原子、不需要锁；新版本把 I/O 等旁路工作交给其他线程，但心智模型仍是「一次一条、按序执行」。
why_en: Redis executes commands one at a time on a single thread, so every command is atomic without locks even though newer versions offload I/O to helper threads.
options_en: One thread per connection
Multi-threaded with row-level locks
Single-threaded, executing commands one at a time
A coroutine pool running commands in parallel
q_en: What is Redis's concurrency model for executing commands?
optionExplanations: 错：连接数一多，一连接一线程会让上下文切换和锁开销爆炸，Redis 没这么设计。
错：行级锁是关系型数据库的并发模型，Redis 命令执行层没有锁。
对：命令在单线程上按顺序逐条执行，天然原子，不用锁协调。
错：Redis 不用协程池并行跑命令，执行器本身仍是单线程串行。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: one thread per connection would blow up context-switch and lock overhead at scale — not how Redis works.
Wrong: row-level locking is a relational-database concurrency model; Redis's executor has no locks.
Right: commands run one at a time on a single thread, so they're atomic without any lock coordination.
Wrong: Redis doesn't fan commands out across a coroutine pool — the executor stays single-threaded and serial.

scenario: 一台机器有 8 个 CPU core，你听说 Redis「单线程」，又看到新版 Redis 有 I/O threads。题目问的是：单线程到底限制在哪里？
scenario_en: A machine has 8 CPU cores. You hear that Redis is single-threaded, but newer Redis versions also mention I/O threads. The question is: where exactly is the single-threaded boundary?
q: 关于 Redis 单线程设计，哪些说法正确？（多选）
options: 命令执行不需要任何锁
对这么简单的操作，单核很少成为瓶颈
新版本把 I/O 和后台工作卸载到其他线程
命令会被拆开在多核上并行执行
why: Redis 单线程主要指命令执行器串行触碰数据结构，因此不需要数据库式行锁。多核能跑旁路工作，但不会拆分单条 SET/INCR。
why_en: Redis single-threaded mostly means the command executor touches data structures serially, so it does not need database-style row locks. Extra cores can run side work, but one SET/INCR is not split apart.
codeSample:
event_loop:
  cmd = next_ready_command()
  execute_command(cmd)     # GET/SET/INCR touch Redis data here
  enqueue_reply(cmd)

# Helper threads may read sockets, parse protocol, or write replies.
# They do not run the same key's SET/INCR body in parallel.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C1["client commands"] --> IO["I/O threads: read/write sockets"]
  IO --> Q["command queue"]
  Q --> E["main command executor"]
  E --> D["Redis data structures"]
  E --> Q2["reply queue"]
  Q2 --> IO
  Core["extra CPU cores"] -.can run.-> IO
  Core -.can run.-> BG["AOF/RDB/background work"]
  Core -.not split.-> E

termDefinitions.meaning: CPU core：硬件执行单元；多核机器能同时跑多个线程或进程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU core is a hardware execution unit; a multi-core machine can run multiple threads or processes at the same time.

termDefinitions.meaning: thread：进程里的软件执行流；一个线程某一刻通常跑在一个 core 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thread is a software execution flow inside a process; at a moment it usually runs on one CPU core.

termDefinitions.meaning: command executor：真正执行 GET/SET/INCR 并读写 Redis 数据结构的主路径；Redis 的单线程主要说的是这里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The command executor is the main path that runs GET/SET/INCR and touches Redis data structures; Redis's single-threaded model mainly refers to this path.

termDefinitions.meaning: I/O thread：辅助收发 socket、写响应、解析协议的线程；它提升网络 I/O 吞吐，但不把一条命令的数据修改拆成并行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An I/O thread helps with socket reads, response writes, or protocol parsing; it improves network I/O throughput but does not split one command's data mutation into parallel execution.

options_en: Command execution needs no locks at all
For operations this simple, a single core is rarely the bottleneck
Newer versions offload I/O and background work to other threads
Commands get split up and run in parallel across multiple cores
q_en: Which statements about Redis's single-threaded design are correct? (multi-select)
optionExplanations: 对：Redis 每次只让一条命令碰数据，两条命令不可能同时改同一个 value，所以天然不用锁。
对：单条命令只占微秒级 CPU，8 核里的 1 个核基本够用，很少先撑爆。
对：新版本把慢的 I/O、过期扫描等旁路工作挪给额外线程，减轻主线程负担。
错：单条 SET/INCR 不会被拆成多个子任务分给多核，执行器仍是一条命令一次处理完。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the executor touches data structures serially, so no two commands can race on the same value — no locks needed.
Right: a single command only costs microseconds of CPU, so one core out of eight is rarely the bottleneck.
Right: newer versions offload side work like slow I/O and expiry scans to extra threads, easing the main thread.
Wrong: a single SET/INCR is never split into sub-tasks across cores — the executor finishes it as one command.

q: 补全 Redis 的两种持久化模式：
text: {{RDB}} 定期做快照，崩溃会丢掉最后一次快照之后的所有写入；{{AOF}} 逐条记录写命令，默认每 {{1}} 秒 fsync 一次。
why: RDB 靠周期快照、AOF 靠追加日志；两者的默认配置都不给「提交即落盘」的保证。
why_en: RDB takes periodic snapshots while AOF logs every write and fsyncs once per second by default.

termDefinitions.meaning: RDB（Redis Database）：某一时刻整个数据集的二进制快照文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RDB is a point-in-time binary snapshot of the entire Redis dataset.

termDefinitions.meaning: AOF（Append Only File）：把每条写命令追加写入的日志文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF is Append Only File, a log that records every write command as it happens.

termDefinitions.meaning: fsync：强制把操作系统缓冲区里的数据真正刷到磁盘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: fsync forces buffered data to actually be written to disk.

q_en: Fill in Redis's two persistence modes:

q: 只用 RDB 快照做持久化，进程崩溃时的后果是？
options: 丢失自上次快照以来的全部写入
最多丢 1 秒写入
不丢任何数据
数据文件永久损坏
why: RDB 是周期性快照：崩溃时两次快照之间的写入全部蒸发。这是 Redis 用持久性换速度的取舍之一。
why_en: With RDB snapshots alone, a crash loses every write since the last snapshot.
options_en: Loses every write since the last snapshot
Loses at most one second of writes
Loses no data at all
The data file becomes permanently corrupted
q_en: If you persist with RDB snapshots alone, what happens to data when the process crashes?
optionExplanations: 对：RDB 是周期性全量快照，两次快照之间的写入没落盘，崩溃就全没了。
错：约 1 秒丢失窗口是 AOF 默认 fsync 策略的特征，不是纯 RDB 的行为。
错：纯内存 + 定期快照必然有丢失窗口，不可能保证零丢失。
错：崩溃丢的是没落盘的写入，不会把已经写好的快照文件本身弄坏。
optionExplanations_en: Right: RDB is a periodic full snapshot, so writes between two snapshots never hit disk and vanish on crash.
Wrong: a ~1s loss window is what AOF's default fsync policy gives you, not plain RDB.
Wrong: pure in-memory plus periodic snapshots always has a loss window — zero loss isn't possible this way.
Wrong: a crash loses writes that never made it to disk; it doesn't corrupt the snapshot file that already exists.

q: 这个 fsync 频率的量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 关键写入要么接受约 1 秒的丢失窗口，要么改成每写 fsync 或换真正持久化的实现
默认配置和关系型数据库一样是提交即落盘
丢失窗口只取决于网络延迟，与 fsync 频率无关
只要打开了 AOF 就等于零丢失，不需要额外设计
why: 每秒 fsync 划出一个约 1 秒的丢失窗口：能接受就用默认配置换速度，不能接受就改每写 fsync 或换 MemoryDB 这类真正持久化的实现。
why_en: The once-per-second fsync policy leaves a roughly one-second loss window, so critical writes need per-write fsync or a truly durable store instead of the defaults.
scenario: AOF 默认策略是每秒 fsync 一次；你要为「已确认写入」写一份诚实的持久性说明给业务方。
options_en: Critical writes must either accept a roughly one-second loss window, fsync on every write, or use a truly durable option
The defaults give the same commit-is-on-disk guarantee as a relational database
The loss window depends only on network latency, not fsync frequency
Turning on AOF alone means zero data loss with no extra design needed

termDefinitions.meaning: AOF（Append Only File）：逐条记录写命令的日志文件，按策略定期 fsync。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF is Append Only File, a write log that fsyncs to disk on a configurable schedule.

termDefinitions.meaning: fsync：把系统缓冲区里的数据真正刷到磁盘的动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: fsync is the operation that actually flushes buffered writes to disk.

q_en: Which design conclusion does this fsync frequency best support?
scenario_en: AOF's default policy fsyncs once per second, and you need to give the business side an honest durability statement about "acknowledged writes."
optionExplanations: 对：默认每秒落盘一次，中间的写入有约 1 秒的风险敞口；能忍就留默认，忍不了就上更频繁的落盘或换持久化方案。
错：关系型数据库默认提交即落盘，Redis 默认 AOF 是每秒 fsync，二者的持久性承诺不一样。
错：丢失窗口由落盘频率决定，网络延迟只影响你多快看到结果，不影响这份数据有没有落盘。
错：打开 AOF 默认仍是每秒 fsync，窗口内的写入照样可能丢，不是零丢失。
optionExplanations_en: Right: fsync-per-second leaves a ~1s loss window — accept it on defaults, or move to fsync-per-write or a truly durable store.
Wrong: a relational database commits to disk by default; Redis's default AOF only fsyncs once a second — different promises.
Wrong: the loss window comes from how often data hits disk, not network latency — that only affects how fast you see the result.
Wrong: AOF's default is still fsync-per-second, so writes inside that window can still be lost — not zero loss.

q: 与关系型数据库默认的「提交即在磁盘上」相比，Redis 默认持久化的立场是？
options: 保证一样强，都是提交即落盘
更强，因为 RDB+AOF 双保险
取决于客户端驱动版本
刻意放弃这个保证来换速度
why: Redis 团队有意用较弱的持久化换性能：默认配置下已确认写入存在丢失窗口，这是产品立场而不是 bug。
why_en: Redis deliberately trades away the commit-is-on-disk guarantee that relational databases give by default in exchange for speed.
options_en: Just as strong: both guarantee commit-is-on-disk
Stronger, because RDB and AOF are used together
It depends on which client driver you use
Deliberately gives up that guarantee in exchange for speed
tradeoff: Redis 默认配置的速度 vs 关系型数据库默认的落盘保证

termDefinitions.meaning: 提交即落盘：事务返回成功时数据已经写入磁盘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Commit-is-on-disk means the data is already on disk by the time the transaction reports success.

termDefinitions.meaning: RDB 是 Redis 的周期性二进制快照，恢复快，但会丢掉上次快照后的写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RDB is Redis's periodic binary snapshot; it restores quickly but can lose writes since the last snapshot.

termDefinitions.meaning: AOF 是顺序追加写命令的日志，默认每秒刷盘，所以仍有短暂丢失窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF is an append-only write log; by default it fsyncs once per second, so a short loss window remains.

q_en: Compared to a relational database's default commit-is-on-disk guarantee, what stance does Redis's default persistence take?
optionExplanations: 错：关系型数据库默认提交即落盘，Redis 默认（哪怕开 AOF）也只是每秒 fsync，不是同等强度。
错：RDB+AOF 一起开也改变不了默认 fsync 频率，仍有丢失窗口，谈不上更强。
错：持久性承诺由服务端配置决定，客户端驱动版本改变不了 Redis 落盘的时机。
对：这是团队主动做的取舍——用弱一点的持久性换更快的写入，默认下已确认的写还是可能在故障时飞走。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a relational database commits to disk by default; Redis's default (even with AOF on) only fsyncs once a second.
Wrong: running RDB and AOF together doesn't change the default fsync frequency — there's still a loss window.
Wrong: durability is a server-side setting; the client driver version can't change when Redis flushes to disk.
Right: the Redis team deliberately trades weaker durability for speed — a confirmed write can still be lost by design.

scenario: 你想要 Redis 的数据结构和接口，但它不只是缓存：已确认写入必须持久，failover 后也不能丢。
q: 最合适的选择是？
options: 开源 Redis 默认配置：最快，但确认写可能仍有丢失窗口
Redis RDB+AOF：更安全，但仍取决于 fsync 策略
AWS MemoryDB：Redis-compatible，写入进 Multi-AZ log 后再确认
Memcached：纯缓存，节点故障或重启就丢
why: MemoryDB 是 Redis-compatible 持久主库：写入进 Multi-AZ log 后才确认。别全用它；可重建缓存用 Redis/ElastiCache 更便宜更快。
why_en: MemoryDB is a Redis-compatible durable primary database, but Redis or ElastiCache is usually better when the data is only a rebuildable cache.
whenOtherWins: 若只是可重建缓存，Redis/ElastiCache/Memcached 更轻；AWS 新项目还要评估带持久性的 ElastiCache。
options_en: Stock Redis defaults: fastest, but acknowledged writes may still have a loss window.
Redis RDB plus AOF: safer, but still depends on the fsync policy.
AWS MemoryDB: Redis-compatible, confirms writes after the Multi-AZ log.
Memcached: pure cache; data is lost on restart or node failure.
tradeoff: 持久主数据库 vs 纯缓存/弱持久 Redis
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Application"] -->|Redis command| P["MemoryDB primary"]
  P -->|durable before ACK| L["Multi-AZ transaction log"]
  P --> R["read replica"]
  A -->|strong read| P
  A -.eventual read.-> R

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS MemoryDB：兼容 Redis/Valkey API 的内存主数据库，成功写入会进入 Multi-AZ log。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS MemoryDB is a Redis/Valkey-compatible in-memory primary database that durably logs successful writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读 primary 可以拿到最新成功写入，适合需要强一致的读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary read returns the latest successful writes and is used when strong consistency matters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读副本可以分担读流量，但副本同步可能有短暂延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replica reads can scale read traffic, but replicas may lag behind the primary.

termDefinitions.meaning: Memcached：纯内存、无持久化的键值缓存，重启即丢数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memcached is a pure in-memory key-value cache with no persistence, so data is gone on restart.

q_en: Given this requirement, what's the best choice?
scenario_en: You want Redis's data structures and API, but it can't just be a cache: acknowledged writes must be durable and must survive failover.
optionExplanations: 对可再生数据够用：开源默认最快，但确认写仍可能在丢失窗口内蒸发，不满足本题「不能丢」的要求。
折中方案：RDB+AOF 能把窗口缩到约 1 秒，仍取决于 fsync 策略，达不到本题要的 failover 也不丢。
对：MemoryDB 会先把写入落进跨可用区的事务日志才回确认，所以就算 failover 也保得住数据，正合「确认写必须持久」的要求。
只做缓存才选它：Memcached 没有持久化，节点故障或重启数据直接消失，完全不适合本题。
optionExplanations_en: Fine when data is disposable: open-source defaults are fastest, but a confirmed write can still vanish in the loss window — fails this case's 'must not lose it' bar.
A middle ground: RDB+AOF shrinks the window to roughly a second, but it still rides on the fsync policy — not durable enough for 'no loss even on failover'.
Right: MemoryDB writes go into a Multi-AZ transaction log before it acks, so a failover still keeps the data — exactly what 'confirmed writes must persist' needs.
Only for pure caching: Memcached has no persistence, so a node failure or restart wipes the data — wrong fit here.

q: Redis 逻辑模型最准确的描述是？
options: 每个字符串 key 指向一个 value，数据结构就住在 value 里
表、行和列组成的关系模型，靠外键做跨表关联
嵌套的文档树，字段可以任意深度嵌套（如 MongoDB）
节点和边组成的图，边可以带权重和属性
why: Redis 的底座是 KV：你创建一个 sorted set，其实是把它作为某个 key 的 value 存起来；所有高级结构都长在 value 上。
why_en: Everything in Redis is a value stored at a string key, and the data structure lives inside that value.
options_en: Every string key points to a value, and the data structure lives inside that value
A relational model of tables, rows, and columns linked by foreign keys
A nested document tree where fields can nest to any depth, like MongoDB
A graph of nodes and weighted, attributed edges
q_en: What best describes Redis's logical data model?
optionExplanations: 对：Redis 底座是 KV，任何高级结构（比如有序集合）本质上都是挂在某个 key 下面的 value。
错：表、行、列和外键跨表关联是关系型数据库的模型，Redis 没有表和外键。
错：Redis 的 hash 是扁平字段，不是可以任意深度嵌套的文档树，那是 MongoDB 的模型。
错：Redis 没有原生的带权边的图结构，节点和边组成的图不是它的逻辑模型。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Redis's foundation is key-value — creating a sorted set just stores it as the value under some key.
Wrong: tables, rows, columns, and foreign-key joins describe a relational database; Redis has no tables or foreign keys.
Wrong: a Redis hash is flat fields, not an arbitrarily nested document tree — that's MongoDB's model.
Wrong: Redis has no native weighted-edge graph structure; nodes and edges aren't its logical model.

q: 以下哪些是 Redis 的原生数据结构或能力？（多选）
options: Sorted Set（有序集合 / 优先队列）
Stream（追加日志）
地理空间索引
跨 key 的 JOIN 查询
why: 字符串、哈希、列表、集合、有序集合、流、地理索引都是原生结构；Redis 没有 join 这类跨 key 查询能力。
why_en: Redis natively offers strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, and geospatial indexes, but it has no joins.
options_en: Sorted set, a ranked structure usable as a priority queue
Stream, an append-only log
Geospatial index
Cross-key JOIN queries
q_en: Which of these are native Redis data structures or capabilities? (multi-select)
optionExplanations: 对：有序集合是原生结构，天然当优先队列或排行榜用。
对：Stream 是原生追加日志结构，配合消费组能当工作队列用。
对：地理空间索引是原生能力，GEOADD/GEOSEARCH 直接支持按半径查询。
错：Redis 没有跨 key 的 JOIN，关联查询要么应用层拼、要么把数据建模到同一个结构里。
optionExplanations_en: Right: sorted sets are a native structure, naturally usable as a priority queue or leaderboard.
Right: Stream is a native append-only log structure; paired with consumer groups it works as a job queue.
Right: geospatial indexing is native — GEOADD/GEOSEARCH directly support radius queries.
Wrong: Redis has no cross-key JOIN; relating data means stitching it in the app or modeling it into one structure.

scenario: 你已经会普通 cache-aside：先 GET 缓存，miss 再查 DB 并 SET 回 Redis。现在面试官追问 Redis 8/Redis Stack 那些更专门的数据类型：Bloom filter、JSON、Time series 到底长什么样、什么时候用。
scenario_en: You already know normal cache-aside: GET the cache first, read the database on miss, then SET Redis. Now the interviewer asks what the more specialized Redis 8 / Redis Stack data types actually look like: Bloom filters, JSON, and time series, and when you would use them.
q: Bloom filter、JSON、时序这类能力在 Redis 8 里的状态是？
options: 已并入核心（老版本要靠 Redis Stack 模块）
必须自己用 Lua 脚本从零实现这些数据结构
只在收费的商业版 Redis Enterprise 里才提供
Redis 完全不支持这些能力，也没有第三方替代
why: Redis 8 文档把 JSON、Bloom 等概率结构、Time series 列为 Open Source 数据类型；老版本常靠 Redis Stack/模块。记住：BF 查集合，JSON 改嵌套，TS 查时间线。
why_en: In Redis 8, JSON, Bloom-style probabilistic structures, and time series are Open Source data types; older versions often needed Redis Stack modules.
whenOtherWins: 普通 GET/SET、Hash、Sorted Set 足够时别上专门类型；集合巨大、需局部 JSON 更新、指标按时间查时才用。
options_en: Merged into core (older versions needed the Redis Stack modules)
You have to implement these data structures yourself from scratch in Lua
Only available in the paid Redis Enterprise commercial edition
Redis does not support these capabilities at all, with no third-party alternative
tradeoff: 专门数据类型表达力强、命令直接 vs 普通 String/Hash/Sorted Set 更通用更简单
codeSample:
# Bloom: 0 = absent, 1 = may exist.
BF.RESERVE usernames:bf 0.001 1000000
BF.ADD usernames:bf alice
BF.EXISTS usernames:bf alice
# JSON: update one nested path.
JSON.SET user:42 $ '{"usage":{"apiCalls":0}}'
JSON.NUMINCRBY user:42 $.usage.apiCalls 1
# Time series: append and read samples.
TS.ADD api:latency:p95 * 183
TS.RANGE api:latency:p95 - +

flowchart LR
  A["Question: what shape is the data?"] --> B["Huge membership set"]
  A --> C["Nested object"]
  A --> D["Timestamped metric"]
  B --> BF["Bloom: BF.EXISTS"]
  C --> J["JSON: JSON.GET path"]
  D --> TS["Time series: TS.RANGE"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 布隆过滤器：用很少内存判断「一个元素一定不存在，或可能存在」的概率型结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic structure that tells you an element definitely does not exist, or might exist, using very little memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: false positive：布隆过滤器可能把没见过的元素误判为可能存在；但返回不存在时可以相信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive means a Bloom filter may say an unseen item might exist, but a negative answer is reliable.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis JSON：在 Redis 里存 JSON 文档，并用 JSONPath 路径读取、修改嵌套字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis JSON stores JSON documents in Redis and lets you read or modify nested fields with JSONPath-like paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Time series：按时间戳追加数值样本，适合指标、传感器、延迟曲线等时间序列数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Time series appends timestamped numeric samples, useful for metrics, sensors, and latency curves.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Stack：老版本用来附加 JSON、时序、概率结构等能力的模块集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Stack was the module bundle older Redis versions used to add JSON, time series, and probabilistic structures.

q_en: What is the status of capabilities like Bloom filters, JSON, and time series in Redis 8?
optionExplanations: 对：官方现在把 JSON、像 Bloom 这样的近似算法结构、还有按时间序列存的类型，都算进开源版本自带的能力里了。
错：这些是内置数据类型，直接调 BF.ADD/JSON.SET/TS.ADD 就有，不需要自己用 Lua 重造。
错：Redis 8 把它们并进了开源核心，不是只锁在收费的 Enterprise 版本里。
错：这些能力过去要装 Stack 模块才有，现在版本已经把它们收进主线，不是完全没有。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Redis 8's docs list JSON, probabilistic structures (Bloom included), and time series as built-in Open Source types.
Wrong: these are built-in types — BF.ADD/JSON.SET/TS.ADD just work, no need to rebuild them from scratch in Lua.
Wrong: Redis 8 folded them into the open-source core; they're not locked behind paid Enterprise only.
Wrong: older versions needed Redis Stack/modules for these; Redis 8 ships them built in — not unsupported.

scenario: 你在 redis-cli 里敲 SET name alice。客户端真正发到 Redis TCP 连接上的不是 HTTP 请求，而是一段 RESP 编码。
scenario_en: You type SET name alice in redis-cli. The client does not send an HTTP request to Redis; it sends RESP-encoded bytes over a TCP connection.
q: Redis 线上协议 RESP 的特点是？
options: 二进制列式编码
命令和参数几乎按你敲的样子在网络上传输
基于 HTTP/2 的 gRPC 协议
必须通过 ORM 框架才能访问
why: RESP 是 Redis 客户端和服务器在 TCP 上说话的线格式：简单、快解析、基本可读，且不是 HTTP/gRPC。
why_en: RESP is the wire format Redis clients and servers speak over TCP: simple, fast to parse, mostly readable, and not HTTP/gRPC.
options_en: A binary columnar encoding
Commands and arguments travel over the wire almost exactly as you type them
A gRPC protocol layered on HTTP/2
You must go through an ORM framework to access it
codeSample:
# What you type:
SET name alice

# What the client sends over TCP as RESP:
*3\r\n
$3\r\nSET\r\n
$4\r\nname\r\n
$5\r\nalice\r\n

# Redis reply:
+OK\r\n
diagram:
flowchart LR
  CLI["redis-cli: SET name alice"] --> Enc["RESP encode"]
  Enc --> TCP["TCP socket"]
  TCP --> R["Redis server"]
  R --> Dec["parse array of bulk strings"]
  Dec --> Exec["execute SET"]
  Exec --> Resp["+OK CRLF"]

termDefinitions.meaning: RESP（REdis Serialization Protocol）：Redis 客户端和服务器之间的 wire protocol，用前缀和长度把命令、参数、返回值编码成字节流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RESP, or REdis Serialization Protocol, is the wire protocol between Redis clients and servers, using prefixes and lengths to encode commands, arguments, and replies as bytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: wire protocol：程序在网络连接上实际传输的字节格式；这里常被中文说成线上协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A wire protocol is the byte format programs actually send over a network connection; this is what 'online protocol' refers to here.

termDefinitions.meaning: bulk string：RESP 里带长度前缀的字符串，例如 $5\r\nhello\r\n；可安全传二进制内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bulk string is a length-prefixed RESP string, such as $5\r\nhello\r\n, and can safely carry binary data.

termDefinitions.meaning: CRLF：\r\n，RESP 用它分隔协议片段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRLF means \r\n, the separator RESP uses between protocol parts.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP/2：支持多路复用的第二代 HTTP 协议，Redis 并不用它做线上协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the second major HTTP version with multiplexing, and it is not the protocol Redis speaks.

termDefinitions.meaning: gRPC：基于 HTTP/2 和 Protobuf 的远程调用框架，与 RESP 无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a remote-procedure-call framework built on HTTP/2 and Protobuf, unrelated to Redis's RESP protocol.

termDefinitions.meaning: ORM（对象关系映射）：把数据库行映射成程序对象的框架，Redis 访问不需要它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ORM, or Object-Relational Mapping, maps database rows to program objects, and Redis access does not require one.

q_en: What characterizes Redis's wire protocol, RESP?
optionExplanations: 错：RESP 是简单可读的文本型行协议，不是面向批量扫描的二进制列式编码。
对：RESP 是简单快解析的线格式，客户端发的命令和参数基本按你敲的样子传输。
错：RESP 走的是普通 TCP 连接，不基于 HTTP/2，也不是 gRPC。
错：redis-cli 或任意客户端库直接用 RESP 说话，不需要经过 ORM 框架。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: RESP is a simple, readable line protocol, not a binary columnar encoding built for batch scans.
Right: RESP is a simple, fast-to-parse wire format — the command and arguments travel roughly as you typed them.
Wrong: RESP runs over a plain TCP connection; it isn't built on HTTP/2 and isn't gRPC.
Wrong: redis-cli or any client library speaks RESP directly — no ORM framework required.

scenario: 用 Redis Set 存每个用户的好友 ID，请求要快速判断「A 是否在 B 的好友集合里」。
q: 该用哪条命令？
options: SMEMBERS friends:B 然后应用里遍历
SCARD friends:B
SISMEMBER friends:B A
SADD friends:B A
why: 要问「A 在不在 B 的 Set 里」，直接用 SISMEMBER。SMEMBERS 是拉全量，SCARD 是数数量，SADD 是写入成员。
why_en: To ask whether A is in B's set, use SISMEMBER. SMEMBERS fetches all members, SCARD counts members, and SADD writes a member.
whenOtherWins: 真要一次性展示全部好友时才用 SMEMBERS；集合很大时改用 SSCAN 分批拉取。
codeSample:
SADD friends:B A          # add A as B's friend
SISMEMBER friends:B A     # 1 = A is in B's friend set
SISMEMBER friends:B C     # 0 = C is not in B's friend set
SCARD friends:B           # count B's friends
SMEMBERS friends:B        # list all friends; avoid for just checking one ID
options_en: SMEMBERS friends:B then loop through it in application code
SCARD friends:B
SISMEMBER friends:B A
SADD friends:B A
tradeoff: 服务端 O(1) 成员判断 vs 拉全量到客户端再遍历

termDefinitions.meaning: SISMEMBER：在服务端 O(1) 判断某个元素是否在集合里，不用把整个集合传回客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SISMEMBER checks set membership on the server in constant time without transferring the whole set.

termDefinitions.meaning: SMEMBERS：返回集合里全部元素，集合很大时既慢又费带宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SMEMBERS returns every member of a set, which is slow and bandwidth-heavy for large sets.

termDefinitions.meaning: SCARD：只返回集合里元素的数量，不返回具体元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCARD returns only the count of members in a set, not the members themselves.

termDefinitions.meaning: SADD：把一个或多个成员加入集合；它是写命令，不是用来检查关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SADD adds one or more members to a set; it is a write command, not a relationship check.

q_en: Which command should you use?
scenario_en: You store each user's friend IDs in a Redis Set, and a request needs to quickly check whether A is in B's friend set.
optionExplanations: 错：SMEMBERS 拉全量成员回应用层遍历，集合大了既慢又浪费带宽，不是判断单个成员在不在。
错：SCARD 只返回集合的成员数量，回答不了「A 在不在」这个问题。
对：SISMEMBER 直接问「这个成员在不在集合里」，O(1) 返回布尔结果，正是本题要的判断。
错：SADD 是往集合里写入成员，不是查询，用它反而会把 A 错误地加进好友集合。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: SMEMBERS pulls the whole set for the app to loop over — slow and wasteful on a big set, and not a membership check.
Wrong: SCARD only returns how many members the set has — it can't answer whether A is in it.
Right: SISMEMBER directly asks 'is this member in the set', returning a boolean in O(1) — exactly this check.
Wrong: SADD writes a member into the set rather than querying it — using it here would wrongly add A as a friend.

q: 这个「槽数量在集群运行期间固定」的设计，最支持哪个判断？
options: 扩缩容 = 重新分配槽归属哪个节点，而不是重新对所有 key 哈希
每加一个节点，哈希函数本身都要跟着重新调整算法
槽的总数必须精确等于集群里的节点数量
槽总数会随着集群规模自动增加或减少
why: Redis 先算 slot = CRC16(key) % 16384，再查 slot->node 表。扩容只迁移槽归属和槽内 key；key 到 slot 的结果不随节点数变化而重哈希。
why_en: Redis first maps a key to CRC16(key) % 16384, then looks up the slot owner; scaling moves slot ownership, not the key-to-slot formula.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  K["key = order:99"] --> H["CRC16(key) % 16384"]
  H --> S["slot = 13000"]

  subgraph Before["Before adding node D"]
    A1["Node A owns slots 0-5460"]
    B1["Node B owns slots 5461-10922"]
    C1["Node C owns slots 10923-16383"]
  end

  S -->|lookup slot map| C1

  subgraph After["After adding node D"]
    A2["Node A owns slots 0-4095"]
    B2["Node B owns slots 4096-8191"]
    C2["Node C owns slots 8192-12287"]
    D2["Node D owns slots 12288-16383"]
  end

  S -.same slot, new owner.-> D2
  C1 -.move slot 13000 and its keys.-> D2
scenario: Redis Cluster 把整个 key 空间预先切成 16384 个哈希槽。加/减节点时，key->slot 的算法不变，变化的是 slot->node 的归属表。
options_en: Scaling means reassigning which node owns which slots, not rehashing every key
Adding a node forces you to re-tune the hash function's algorithm itself
The total slot count must exactly equal the number of nodes in the cluster
The total slot count automatically grows or shrinks as the cluster resizes
codeSample:
slot = CRC16("order:99") % 16384

# Before scale-out
slot_map[13000] = "node C"

# After adding node D
slot_map[13000] = "node D"
tradeoff: 固定槽位让扩缩容只迁移部分槽 vs 单个槽仍只能归属一个主节点

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希槽：Redis Cluster 把 key 空间切成的固定分片单位，每个槽归属一个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash slot is a fixed sharding unit that Redis Cluster splits the key space into, with each slot owned by one node.

termDefinitions.meaning: slot map：记录每个哈希槽当前归属哪个节点的映射表，客户端和节点都靠它把请求路由到正确节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slot map records which node currently owns each hash slot, and clients use it to route requests to the right node.

termDefinitions.meaning: CRC16：Redis Cluster 用来把 key 算到 0..16383 号槽位的哈希函数基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRC16 is the hash function basis Redis Cluster uses to map keys into slots 0 through 16383.

termDefinitions.meaning: 16384=2^14,两个原因:①节点间 gossip 心跳里要带「自己拥有哪些槽」的位图,16384 位=2KB,够小能频繁发(若用 65536 位就是 8KB、太占带宽);②Redis Cluster 上限约 1000 个 master,16384/1000≈每节点 16 槽,够细能均匀分。跟吞吐(ops/sec)无关——那是「为什么要分片」,槽数是「怎么分」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 16384 = 2^14, for two reasons: (1) gossip heartbeats carry each node owned-slots bitmap; 16384 bits = 2 KB, small enough to send often (65536 bits would be 8 KB, too much bandwidth); (2) Redis Cluster tops out around 1000 masters, so 16384/1000 ≈ 16 slots per node — fine enough to spread evenly. It has nothing to do with throughput (ops/sec): that is WHY you shard, the slot count is HOW you shard.

q_en: Which conclusion does the fixed slot count during cluster operation best support?
scenario_en: Redis Cluster pre-splits the entire key space into a fixed number of hash slots; adding or removing nodes only reassigns which node owns which slots, without rehashing.
optionExplanations: 对：slot=CRC16(key)%16384 算法不变，扩容只搬槽的归属表和槽内 key，不用给全部 key 重新哈希。
错：哈希函数固定为 CRC16(key)%16384，加节点变的是 slot→node 归属表，不是哈希算法本身。
错：16384 个槽可以分给任意数量节点，一个节点能持有多个槽，槽数不等于节点数。
错：槽总数在集群运行期间固定为 16384，不会随节点增减而变化，变的只是归属。
optionExplanations_en: Right: slot = CRC16(key) % 16384 never changes; scaling just moves slot ownership and the keys in those slots, not a full rehash.
Wrong: the hash function stays fixed; adding a node changes the slot-to-node ownership table, not the hash itself.
Wrong: the 16384 slots can be split across any number of nodes — one node can own many slots, so slot count isn't node count.
Wrong: the total slot count stays fixed at 16384 while the cluster runs; only ownership shifts as nodes change.

q: Redis Cluster 客户端如何找到 key 所在的节点？
options: 随便连一个节点，由它读懂请求内容后代为转发
每次操作前先询问一个独立的外部配置中心服务
客户端本地缓存 slot→node 映射，从 key 算出槽后直连目标节点
把每个请求广播到集群里所有节点，取第一个响应
why: 客户端把槽位表当电话簿：从 key 算槽、查本地映射、第一跳就打到正确节点；Redis 节点不会替你转发请求。
why_en: Clients cache the slot-to-node map, compute the slot from the key, and connect directly to the owning node because Redis will not forward requests.
options_en: Connect to any node and have it read the request and forward it on your behalf
Ask a separate external configuration-center service before every operation
Cache the slot-to-node map locally, compute the slot from the key, and connect directly to the owning node
Broadcast every request to all nodes in the cluster and take the first response
q_en: How does a Redis Cluster client find the node that owns a key?
optionExplanations: 错：打错门的时候节点只是回一句「去那边找」，并不会帮你把请求转过去。
错：客户端不需要每次操作前都去问一个外部配置中心，槽位表就缓存在客户端本地。
对：客户端本地缓存 slot→node 映射，从 key 算出槽后直接打到目标节点，像查电话簿。
错：广播到全部节点等第一个响应既浪费又不可靠，Redis 客户端不这么设计。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a Redis node never forwards your request for you — hit the wrong one and you just get MOVED back.
Wrong: the client doesn't ask an external config service before every operation — the slot table is cached locally.
Right: the client caches a local slot-to-node map, computes the slot from the key, and connects straight to the right node.
Wrong: broadcasting to every node and taking the first reply is wasteful and unreliable — not how Redis clients work.

q: 客户端把请求发给了不再持有该槽的节点，会发生什么？
options: 节点读出目标 key 归属后代为转发到正确节点
请求会排队缓存，等待槽迁移彻底完成
返回 MOVED 指向正确节点，客户端刷新本地槽位表后重发
节点直接报错并主动断开这个客户端的连接
why: 节点回 MOVED 告诉你槽的新主人，客户端据此刷新映射（如 CLUSTER SHARDS）再重发；节点自己绝不转发。
why_en: The node replies with MOVED pointing at the right owner, and the client refreshes its cached slot map and retries.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant A as 节点A(旧主人)
    participant B as 节点B(新主人)
    C->>A: GET user:9
    A-->>C: MOVED 1234 B
    C->>C: 刷新 slot→node 映射
    C->>B: GET user:9
    B-->>C: value
options_en: The node figures out the right owner and forwards the request there for you
The request queues and waits until the slot migration fully finishes
It replies MOVED pointing at the right node, and the client refreshes its slot map and retries
It errors out immediately and actively drops that client's connection

termDefinitions.meaning: MOVED：节点告诉客户端「这个槽现在归谁」的重定向回复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MOVED is the redirect reply a node sends telling the client which node now owns that slot.

q_en: What happens when a client sends a request to a node that no longer owns that slot?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 节点不会替客户端做转发，它只回一个指向正确节点的提示，转发由客户端自己做。
错：节点不会把请求挂起等迁移完成，它立刻返回结果，让客户端决定下一步。
对：节点用 MOVED 指个方向，客户端拿这个提示更新自己缓存的槽位信息，再重新把命令发一次。
错：打错门是槽位路由的正常情况，节点不会因此报错断开连接，只是告诉你去哪找。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a Redis node never proxies the request for you — it just returns a hint to the right node.
Wrong: the node doesn't queue the request waiting for migration to finish — it replies immediately.
Right: the node replies MOVED pointing to the correct node; the client refreshes its slot map and resends.
Wrong: hitting the wrong node is normal slot routing — it doesn't error out and disconnect, just tells you where to go.

q: 集群里每个节点如何知道完整的槽位分布？
options: 只有主节点知道完整槽位分布
节点之间用 gossip 协议互换集群状态
依赖外部的 ZooKeeper 协调服务
每次由客户端主动告知节点
why: 节点之间通过 gossip 传播集群状态，所以任何节点都掌握全量槽位表，也才能对打错门的请求回出 MOVED。
why_en: Nodes share cluster state via a gossip protocol, so every node knows the full slot map.
options_en: Only the primary nodes know the full slot layout
Nodes exchange cluster state with each other via a gossip protocol
It relies on an external ZooKeeper coordination service
Clients tell nodes about the slot layout each time

termDefinitions.meaning: gossip 协议：节点之间随机两两交换状态，最终让全体节点收敛到一致视图的通信方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gossip protocol has nodes randomly exchange state with each other so the whole cluster eventually converges on one consistent view.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper：一个独立的分布式协调服务，Redis Cluster 并不依赖它同步槽位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a separate distributed coordination service that Redis Cluster does not rely on to sync its slot map.

q_en: How does every node in the cluster learn the full slot layout?
optionExplanations: 错：任何一个节点（包括副本）都掌握全量槽位表，不是只有主节点才知道。
对：节点之间靠 gossip 协议互相传播集群状态，因此任何节点都掌握全量槽位分布。
错：Redis Cluster 自己靠 gossip 维护成员和槽位状态，不依赖外部的 ZooKeeper。
错：槽位分布是节点之间自己传播出来的，不是靠客户端每次主动告知。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: every node, including replicas, holds the full slot table — it isn't limited to primaries.
Right: nodes propagate cluster state to each other via a gossip protocol, so every node ends up with the full slot map.
Wrong: Redis Cluster maintains membership and slot state itself via gossip — it doesn't depend on ZooKeeper.
Wrong: slot distribution spreads node-to-node on its own; it isn't the client's job to announce it each time.

q: 给 Redis Cluster 加一个新节点后会发生什么？
options: 新节点只接收新写入，旧数据不动
全量数据重新洗牌一遍
必须停机才能完成迁移
一部分槽（连同其中的 key）迁移到新节点
why: 扩容 = 槽迁移：一部分 slot 连同里面的 key 移到新节点，客户端靠 MOVED 和刷新映射自动跟上。
why_en: Adding a node migrates a share of the hash slots and their keys to it while clients follow along via MOVED redirects.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Add node"] --> B["Move slots"]
  B --> C["MIGRATE keys"]
  C --> D["Update slot map"]
options_en: The new node only receives new writes; existing data stays put
All the data gets reshuffled from scratch
The cluster must go offline to migrate
A share of the slots, along with their keys, migrates to the new node
q_en: What happens after you add a new node to a Redis Cluster?
optionExplanations: 错：新节点要真正分担负载，就得从别的节点接管一部分槽，不会只收新写入。
错：迁移只动被重新分配的那部分槽和其中的 key，不是把全量数据都洗一遍。
错：槽迁移是在线完成的，客户端靠 MOVED/ASK 和刷新映射跟上，不需要整体停机。
对：加节点意味着挑一部分槽搬家，槽里的 key 跟着一起走，客户端发现打偏了会自动纠正路由。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: for a new node to actually take load, it has to take over some slots — it can't just start with new writes.
Wrong: migration only moves the reassigned slots and the keys in them, not the entire dataset.
Wrong: slot migration happens online; clients keep up via MOVED/ASK — no full-cluster downtime needed.
Right: scaling moves some slots, and the keys inside them, to the new node; clients catch up via MOVED and a refreshed map.

scenario: 客户端向 Redis primary 写 SET order:123 paid。这个 primary 后面挂着两个 replica，用来异步复制和 failover。题目问的是：客户端什么时候收到 OK？
scenario_en: A client writes SET order:123 paid to a Redis primary. Two replicas follow that primary for replication and failover. The question is: when does the client receive OK?
q: Redis 主从复制的确认时序是？
options: 主节点在副本收到写入之前就向客户端确认（异步复制）
必须多数副本确认才向客户端返回
主副本同步双写完成后才确认
客户端直接把写入发给副本
why: Redis 默认主先执行并回 OK，复制流随后给 replica；低延迟，但 failover 可能丢尾部已确认写。Cassandra/Dynamo 常用 W+R>N 的 quorum；Redis 默认不是这套。
why_en: By default, Redis executes on the primary and returns OK before replicas process the write, then sends the replication stream afterward. This keeps latency low but can lose the last acknowledged writes on failover. Cassandra/Dynamo commonly use W+R>N quorums; default Redis does not.
options_en: The primary acknowledges the client before replicas have seen the write (async replication)
It must wait for a majority of replicas to acknowledge before returning
It confirms only after synchronously writing to both primary and replica
Clients write directly to the replicas
tradeoff: 写入低延迟 vs failover 时可能丢最后一批已确认写入

rows: 等 W 个副本 ACK

codeSample:
SET order:123 paid
# Default Redis: primary can reply OK before replicas process it.

SET order:124 paid
WAIT 1 1000
# Client asks Redis to wait up to 1s for 1 replica ACK.
# This reduces risk, but it is not a full CP/quorum commit.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant P as Redis primary
  participant R as Replica
  C->>P: SET order:123 paid
  P-->>C: OK before replica applies it
  P-->>R: async replication stream
  Note over P,R: if P dies first, promoted replica may miss this write

termDefinitions.meaning: 异步复制：主节点先应答客户端，副本之后才追上这次写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asynchronous replication means the primary acknowledges the client first and replicas catch up afterward.

termDefinitions.meaning: WAIT：Redis 命令，让客户端等待前面的写入被指定数量副本确认；它降低丢写概率，但不等于强一致多数派提交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WAIT makes the client wait until a given number of replicas acknowledge previous writes; it reduces loss risk but is not a strong-consistency quorum commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum：在 Cassandra/Dynamo 这类系统里，N 是副本数，写等 W 个 ACK，读等 R 个响应；W+R>N 时读写集合必然相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In Cassandra/Dynamo-style systems, N is replica count, W is write acknowledgments, and R is read responses; W+R>N makes read and write sets overlap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同步复制：写入要等副本或日志也确认后才回客户端，延迟更高但丢已确认写的概率更低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Synchronous replication waits for replicas or a durable log before acknowledging the client, trading latency for lower acknowledged-write loss.

q_en: What is the acknowledgment timing in Redis primary-replica replication?
optionExplanations: 对：Redis 默认主先执行并立刻回 OK，复制流随后才异步送给 replica，延迟低但有丢尾风险。
错：等多数副本点头才算数是 quorum 写法，那是 Dynamo 风格系统的常见做法，不是 Redis 默认这一套。
错：主副同步双写完成才确认会拖高延迟，Redis 默认走的是异步复制，不等副本。
错：客户端只连主节点写入，复制流是主节点单向推给副本，客户端不会直接写副本。
optionExplanations_en: Right: by default the primary executes and replies OK immediately; the write reaches the replica asynchronously afterward.
Wrong: waiting for a majority of replicas to ack is quorum writing (like Cassandra/Dynamo's W+R>N) — not Redis's default.
Wrong: waiting for the replica to apply the write too would add latency; Redis defaults to async replication instead.
Wrong: the client only writes to the primary; replication pushes one-way from primary to replica, not from the client.

scenario: primary 执行 SET order:123 paid 并已经给客户端回 OK，但复制流还没送到 replica；primary 立刻宕机，replica 被提升成新主。
q: 主节点崩溃、副本被提升后，最典型的数据后果是？
options: 副本数据反而比主节点还新
崩溃前最后一段已确认写入凭空消失
数据绝不会丢失，一定能恢复
槽位分布表被损坏
why: Redis 默认异步复制：OK 只说明 primary 执行过，不代表 replica 已收到。主在复制尾部传完前死掉，新主只能保留自己见过的数据。
why_en: Redis replication is async by default: OK means the primary applied the write, not that replicas received it. If the primary dies before sending the tail, the promoted replica only has the data it saw.
codeSample:
T1 client -> primary: SET order:123 paid
T2 primary -> client: OK
T3 primary --X--> replica: replication stream not delivered yet
T4 primary crashes
T5 replica promoted to new primary
T6 GET order:123 -> nil   # the acknowledged write is gone
options_en: The replica ends up newer than the primary was
The last stretch of acknowledged writes before the crash simply vanishes
No data is ever lost; it always recovers
The slot distribution table gets corrupted
tradeoff: 异步复制低延迟 vs failover 可能丢尾部已确认写
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant P as Primary
  participant R as Replica
  C->>P: SET order:123 paid
  P-->>C: OK
  P-xR: async replication not delivered
  Note over P: crashes
  R->>R: promoted to primary
  C->>R: GET order:123
  R-->>C: nil

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端已经收到 OK 的写入；在 Redis 默认复制里，这只代表主节点执行过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write for which the client already received OK; in default Redis replication, that only means the primary applied it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点已执行、但副本还没应用到同一位置之间的时间窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The window where the primary has applied writes that the replica has not applied yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点故障后，把某个副本提升为新主节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Promoting a replica to become the new primary after the old primary fails.

q_en: After the primary crashes and a replica is promoted, what is the most typical data consequence?
scenario_en: The primary applies SET order:123 paid and already returns OK to the client, but the replication stream has not reached the replica. The primary crashes immediately and the replica is promoted.
optionExplanations: 错：异步复制下副本的数据只会比主节点旧或持平，不会反而更新。
对：OK 只说明主节点执行过，不代表复制流已送到副本；主在传完前挂了，新主只保留自己见过的数据。
错：异步复制正是「不保证零丢失」的取舍点，说绝不丢失和场景描述矛盾。
错：这次事故丢的是数据本身，跟槽位归属表是否损坏无关，槽位分布不受影响。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: under async replication, a replica's data can only be older than or equal to the primary's, never newer.
Right: OK only means the primary executed the write, not that replication reached the replica; if it dies first, the new primary keeps only what it saw.
Wrong: async replication is exactly the trade-off that gives up zero-loss guarantees — that contradicts the scenario.
Wrong: what's lost here is the data itself, not the slot ownership table — slot distribution is unaffected.

q: 对比大多数数据库，Redis Cluster 的设计哲学是？
options: 自动帮你解决扩展性问题
内置跨节点查询优化器
只给你原语，扩展性问题由你自己靠 key 设计解决
提供强一致的跨节点分布式事务
why: Redis 集群刻意简单：它期望一个请求的数据都在单个节点上，「怎么组织 key，就是怎么扩展 Redis」。
why_en: Redis Cluster hands you primitives instead of solving scaling for you, so structuring your keys is how you scale Redis.
options_en: It automatically solves scalability problems for you
It has a built-in cross-node query optimizer
It hands you primitives and leaves scaling to how you design your keys
It provides strongly consistent cross-node distributed transactions
q_en: Compared to most databases, what is Redis Cluster's design philosophy?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 集群不会替你自动解决扩展性，key 怎么组织仍要你自己设计。
错：Redis 没有跨节点的查询优化器帮你规划执行路径，这是关系型数据库的能力。
对：Redis 假定一次请求用到的数据都挤在一个节点里，key 该怎么设计，直接决定了这套系统能怎么撑大。
错：Redis Cluster 不提供强一致的跨节点分布式事务，MULTI 必须在一个槽内完成。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis Cluster doesn't automatically solve scaling for you — how you organize keys is still on you.
Wrong: Redis has no cross-node query optimizer planning execution paths — that's a relational-database capability.
Right: Redis expects one request's data to live on a single node — 'how you organize keys is how you scale Redis'.
Wrong: Redis Cluster doesn't offer strongly consistent cross-node transactions; MULTI must stay inside one slot.

scenario: user:123 的帖子列表和点赞集合是两个 key，要在一个 MULTI 事务里一起修改。
q: 正确做法是？
options: 放弃集群模式，把整个部署缩回成本更低的单节点 Redis
用 hash tag：key 里用花括号包住哈希部分，如 {user:123}:posts
把这次修改拆成两个独立事务分别提交，接受中间态可见
在客户端代码里再加一把分布式锁做双重保护
why: Redis Cluster 的 MULTI 必须在一个槽/主节点上执行；共享 hash tag 可强制相关 key 同槽。
why_en: In Redis Cluster, a MULTI transaction must run in one slot on one primary; a shared hash tag forces related keys into that slot.
whenOtherWins: 若业务能接受最终一致，拆成独立事件可分散负载；别把无关 key 硬绑同槽。
codeSample:
# Bad for one MULTI in Cluster: likely different slots.
MULTI
  LPUSH user:123:posts post:9
  SADD user:123:likes post:9
EXEC
# -> CROSSSLOT risk

# Good: same hash tag, same slot.
MULTI
  LPUSH {user:123}:posts post:9
  SADD {user:123}:likes post:9
EXEC
options_en: Give up cluster mode entirely and shrink the deployment back to a cheaper single Redis node
Use a hash tag: wrap the hashed part of the key in braces, like {user:123}:posts
Split the change into two separate transactions committed independently, accepting a visible intermediate state
Add another client-side distributed lock on top as a second layer of protection
tradeoff: 同槽换来跨 key 原子事务 vs 硬绑同槽带来的负载倾斜风险
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["need one MULTI"] --> B{"same slot?"}
  B -->|yes: hash tag user123| C["EXEC on one primary"]
  B -->|no| D["CROSSSLOT"]
  E["can tolerate middle state"] --> F["split events"]

termDefinitions.meaning: hash tag：key 里花括号 {} 包住的部分，只有它参与哈希计算，用来让多个 key 强制同槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash tag is the braces-enclosed part of a key that alone gets hashed, used to force several keys onto the same slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: MULTI：开启一个 Redis 事务，把后续命令排队到一起原子执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MULTI starts a Redis transaction, queuing the following commands to execute atomically together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个相关 key 只更新了一个时，读请求看到的短暂不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A brief state where one related key is updated but the other is not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多 key 操作触碰不同槽时的错误；加锁不能改变槽位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The error returned when one multi-key operation touches different slots; a lock does not change slots.

q_en: What's the correct approach?
scenario_en: user:123's post list and like set are two keys that must change together inside one MULTI transaction.
optionExplanations: 规模足够小时可行：放弃集群换单节点能绕开跨槽限制，但代价是放弃了水平扩展，不是本题要的答案。
对：花括号包住共同的哈希部分（如 {user:123}）强制让相关 key 落进同一个槽，MULTI 才能在单节点原子执行。
错：拆成两个事务会让中间态被其他请求看到（帖子列表已改、点赞还没改），破坏了「一起修改」的要求。
错：分布式锁挡不住跨槽——两个 key 依然分属不同主节点，MULTI 本身在 Cluster 里还是会报 CROSSSLOT。
optionExplanations_en: Workable only at small scale: dropping back to a single node sidesteps cross-slot limits, but gives up horizontal scaling — not the fit here.
Right: wrapping the shared part in braces (e.g. {user:123}) forces the related keys onto the same slot, so MULTI can run atomically on one node.
Wrong: splitting into two transactions lets others see the in-between state (posts updated, likes not yet) — breaks the 'change together' requirement.
Wrong: a distributed lock doesn't fix cross-slot routing — the two keys still belong to different primaries, so MULTI still throws CROSSSLOT.

q: 这个吞吐量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 先用单节点撑住这个量级，明显超过它再考虑分片
无论峰值多少都应默认直接上 Redis Cluster 分片
这个量级下必须换成异步批处理框架写入
单节点吞吐和磁盘型数据库同量级，可直接互换选型
why: 单节点约十万写/秒的量级，意味着分片是应对明显超出这个量级的峰值，而不是默认动作。
why_en: A single node handling on the order of a hundred thousand writes per second means sharding is for peaks that clearly exceed it, not a default first move.
scenario: 系统预计单个 Redis 主节点要扛住每秒十万量级的写入峰值。
options_en: Let one node absorb this order of magnitude first, and shard only once you clearly exceed it
Default to Redis Cluster sharding regardless of the actual peak
This throughput forces you to route writes through an async batch framework instead
Single-node throughput matches disk-based databases, so they are interchangeable
q_en: Which design conclusion does this throughput order of magnitude best support?
scenario_en: The system expects a single Redis primary to absorb write peaks on the order of a hundred thousand per second.
optionExplanations: 对：单机大约十万级写/秒已经够用了，只有峰值远超这个数才值得上分片，不是碰到规模就该做的默认动作。
错：没到瓶颈就默认分片会白白背上跨槽、hash tag、运维复杂度这些成本，不是这个量级该做的事。
错：这个吞吐量级正是 Redis 单节点内存操作能扛住的范围，不需要换成异步批处理框架。
错：Redis 是内存操作，磁盘型数据库受随机 I/O 限制，两者吞吐量级并不同量级，不能直接互换选型。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a single node handles roughly this hundred-thousand-writes/sec range fine; sharding is for peaks clearly beyond that.
Wrong: sharding by default before hitting a real bottleneck adds cross-slot routing, hash tags, and ops overhead for nothing.
Wrong: this throughput is squarely within what a single in-memory Redis node can handle — no need for async batch processing.
Wrong: Redis is in-memory while disk-based databases are bound by random I/O — not the same order of magnitude at all.

termDefinitions.term: 集群总吞吐≈节点数×单节点
termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 水平扩:16384 个槽分给 N 个节点,每节点管 ~1/N 的 key/流量,所以总吞吐≈N×单节点(~10~20万/秒);1000 节点≈1~2 亿/秒。前提是负载均匀——单个 hot key 拆不开(只住一个节点),那一个 key 的量上不去
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster scales horizontally: 16384 slots split across N nodes, each handling ~1/N of keys/traffic, so aggregate throughput ≈ N × single-node (~100k-200k/s); 1000 nodes ≈ 100M-200M/s. This assumes even load — a single hot key cannot be split (lives on one node) and does not scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 槽=key 的「桶」。Redis 预先把 key 空间切成 16384 个固定桶:key→CRC16(key)%16384→落进某一个槽→该槽归某个节点。所以是 key→槽→节点。好处:加减节点只搬「槽(连同里面的 key)」,不用给所有 key 重新哈希。16384=2^14(14 是指数,不是 14 个槽);每个节点用一个「16384 位的位图」报自己拥有哪些槽,一位一个槽,16384÷8=2048 字节=2KB
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slot is a bucket for keys. Redis pre-splits the keyspace into 16384 fixed buckets: key→CRC16(key)%16384→one slot→owned by a node (key→slot→node). Adding/removing nodes just moves slots (with their keys), no rehash. 16384=2^14 (14 is the exponent); each node reports owned slots as a 16384-bit bitmap, one bit per slot, 16384/8=2048 bytes=2KB.

q: 这个耗时量级最支持哪条设计判断？
options: 命令本身很少是瓶颈，优化重点应放在减少网络往返（pipeline/MGET）
命令执行本身是主要瓶颈，要用 Lua 脚本替换所有命令
微秒级执行意味着可以放心做同步跨机房调用
既然命令很快，热点 key 就不需要任何缓解手段
why: 命令本身只花微秒，真正决定观感延迟的是网络往返次数，这正是 pipeline/MGET 划算的原因。
why_en: Since a command itself costs only microseconds, the number of network round trips dominates perceived latency, which is why pipelining and MGET pay off.
scenario: 一条 Redis 命令在服务器上的执行只有微秒级开销，网络往返才是你看到的亚毫秒延迟的主因。
options_en: The command itself is rarely the bottleneck, so optimize by cutting round trips with pipelining or MGET
Command execution is the main bottleneck, so replace every command with a Lua script
Microsecond execution means synchronous cross-region calls are safe
Since commands are fast, hot keys need no mitigation at all
q_en: Which design conclusion does this latency order of magnitude best support?
scenario_en: A single Redis command costs only microseconds to execute on the server; network round trips are the main source of the sub-millisecond latency you actually observe.
optionExplanations: 对：单条命令快到可以忽略不计，拖慢体感速度的其实是来回跑网络的次数，合并请求批量发送才是省时间的关键。
错：命令执行只占微秒级，把它换成 Lua 脚本省不下多少时间，真正的瓶颈是网络往返次数。
错：命令快不等于网络快，跨机房的物理传播延迟不会因为服务端执行快就消失，同步跨机房调用仍然贵。
错：单条命令快，不代表某个 key 被打爆时不会成为单点瓶颈，热点 key 仍需要额外缓解手段。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the command itself only costs microseconds; round trips dominate perceived latency — why pipelining/MGET pay off.
Wrong: execution is already microsecond-scale, so swapping it for a Lua script saves little — the real cost is round trips.
Wrong: a fast command doesn't mean a fast network — cross-region propagation delay doesn't vanish just because it's quick.
Wrong: a fast single command doesn't stop one key from becoming a single-node bottleneck under heavy load.

scenario: 页面要展示 100 条订单及买家名：先 1 次查订单列表，再对每条订单各查 1 次买家资料，总共 101 次查询。这就是 N+1。
q: 「N+1 查询」打在 SQL 上是灾难，打在 Redis 上却勉强可行，为什么？
options: 每条命令只花服务器微秒级，还能用 pipeline 或 MGET 把多次往返合成一次
Redis 会在服务端自动检测并合并相似的重复查询
Redis 内置一个查询优化器，会帮你规划执行路径
因为这种场景下业务数据量一定很小，可以忽略
why: N+1 是 1 次列表 + N 次详情。SQL 每次 SELECT 有规划/索引成本；Redis 命令轻，可用 MGET/pipeline 合并往返。
why_en: N+1 means one list query plus N detail queries. SQL pays planning and index costs per SELECT; Redis commands are lighter, and MGET or pipelining batches round trips.
codeSample:
# N+1 shape: 1 list query + N detail queries.
orders = sql("SELECT id, buyer_id FROM orders LIMIT 100")
for order in orders:
  buyer = sql("SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?", order.buyer_id)
# 101 SQL calls: bad. Prefer JOIN or WHERE id IN (...).

# Redis version: still N logical reads, but batch the trip.
postIds = redis.lrange("feed:user:42", 0, 99)
posts = redis.mget(postIds.map(id => "post:" + id))
# Or pipeline many GET/HGET commands and wait once.
options_en: Each command costs the server only microseconds, and pipelining or MGET collapses many round trips into one
Redis automatically detects and merges similar repeated queries on the server
Redis has a built-in query optimizer that plans the execution path for you
Because in this scenario the data volume is guaranteed to be negligible
tradeoff: SQL N+1 查询成本高 vs Redis 点查轻但仍要批量化
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["1 list query"] --> B["100 ids"]
  B --> C["100 detail queries"]
  C --> D["101 total calls"]
  E["Better SQL"] --> F["JOIN / IN"]
  G["Better Redis"] --> H["MGET / pipeline"]

termDefinitions.meaning: N+1 查询：先查出 N 条主记录，再为每条记录各查一次关联详情，总查询数变成 1+N。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The N-plus-one pattern fetches N main records, then runs one extra lookup per record, creating 1+N total queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多条命令一次性发送，只等一次网络往返。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Send many commands at once and wait for one network round trip.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求批量读取多个 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fetch multiple keys in one request.

q_en: Why is the N-plus-one query pattern disastrous on SQL but tolerable on Redis?
scenario_en: A page displays 100 orders with buyer names: one query fetches the order list, then one buyer lookup runs per order, for 101 total queries. That is N+1.
optionExplanations: 对：这里的 N+1 是 1 次列表加 N 次逐条查询；SQL 每条都要过一遍规划器，Redis 命令便宜得多，把它们攒成一次往返就行。
错：服务端不会替你悄悄把相似请求并成一次，想少跑几趟网络得应用自己批量发命令。
错：Redis 没有查询优化器帮你规划路径，这道题能扛住是因为命令便宜，不是因为有优化器。
错：这个场景能扛住是因为单命令成本低，跟业务数据量大小没有必然关系，数据量大同样可行。
optionExplanations_en: Right: N+1 is 1 list call + N detail calls; SQL pays a planning cost per SELECT while Redis commands are cheap, so MGET/pipeline merge the round trips.
Wrong: Redis doesn't auto-detect and merge similar queries server-side — merging round trips is something the app does with MGET/pipeline.
Wrong: Redis has no query optimizer planning a path for you; this holds up because each command is cheap, not because of an optimizer.
Wrong: this scales fine because a single command is cheap, not because the business data has to be small.

scenario: 你执行 SET session:42 abc EX 10。10 秒后再次 GET session:42。题目问的是：Redis 为什么不会把 abc 这个过期值返回给你？
scenario_en: You run SET session:42 abc EX 10. Ten seconds later, you call GET session:42 again. The question is: why does Redis not return the expired value abc?
q: Redis 对设置了 TTL 的 key 给出的保证是？
options: TTL 到点会立刻从内存里清除
TTL 只对 string 类型的 key 生效
过期后仍可能读到几秒内的旧值
过期之后绝不会再读到这个 key 的值
why: 保证是「过期后逻辑读不到」：访问路径先查过期时间，过期就删并返回不存在。没人访问的过期 key 由后台抽样清理，所以内存回收可能晚一点。
why_en: Redis checks expiry before returning a key; if it is timed out, the command deletes it and returns missing. Background expiration cleans up expired keys that nobody touches.
options_en: It is purged from memory the instant the TTL hits zero
TTL only works on keys of type string
You might still read a stale value for a few seconds after expiry
You will never read this key's value again once its TTL has expired
codeSample:
SET session:42 abc EX 10
# After 10s, the read path behaves like this:
get(key):
  if has_ttl(key) and now_ms() >= expire_at_ms[key]:
    delete(key)        # passive expiration
    return nil
  return value[key]

# Separately, Redis samples TTL keys in the background.
# That active cleanup frees memory for keys nobody reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL（Time To Live）：key 在被判定过期前还能存活多久的倒计时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL, or Time To Live, is the countdown before a key is considered expired.

termDefinitions.meaning: passive expiration：客户端访问 key 时，Redis 发现它已过期，就先删除再返回不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Passive expiration means Redis checks a key during access, deletes it if it is expired, and returns it as missing.

termDefinitions.meaning: active expiration：Redis 后台周期性抽样带 TTL 的 key，把已经过期但没人访问的 key 清掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Active expiration means Redis periodically samples keys with TTLs and deletes expired keys that nobody accessed.

termDefinitions.meaning: expire_at：Redis 记录的绝对过期时间；读路径用当前时间和它比较，决定 key 是否已过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: expire_at is the absolute expiration timestamp Redis compares with the current time to decide whether a key is expired.

q_en: What guarantee does Redis give for a key with a TTL set?
optionExplanations: 错：没人访问的过期 key 靠后台抽样清理，内存回收可能晚一点，不是到点立刻从内存消失。
错：TTL 对任意类型的 key 都生效，不局限于 string，hash/set/zset 一样能设过期。
错：访问路径会先检查过期时间，过期就当不存在处理，不会把旧值返回给你。
对：承诺的是「一过期逻辑上就读不到」——每次访问都会先核对是不是已经到期，到了就当它不存在。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an expired key nobody touches is cleaned up by a background sampling sweep, so memory reclaim can lag a bit.
Wrong: TTL applies to keys of any type, not just strings — hashes, sets, and sorted sets can lapse too.
Wrong: the access path checks the expiry time first and treats a lapsed key as gone — it won't hand back the stale value.
Right: the guarantee is 'logically unreadable once lapsed' — the access path checks first, deletes, and returns not-found.

q: 不配置淘汰策略时，Redis 内存写满后的默认行为是？
options: 自动按 LRU 规则淘汰旧 key
自动删除最早写入的那个 key
拒绝接受新的写入请求
把冷数据换出到磁盘上存放
why: 反直觉：默认策略是内存满直接拒写。把 Redis 当缓存必须显式配置 allkeys-lru 这类淘汰策略。
why_en: Out of the box Redis rejects writes once memory is full, so a cache must explicitly configure an eviction policy like allkeys-lru.
options_en: It automatically evicts keys using an LRU rule
It automatically deletes the oldest-written key
It rejects new write requests
It swaps cold data out to disk
q_en: With no eviction policy configured, what is Redis's default behavior once memory fills up?
optionExplanations: 错：想要按最近最少用来淘汰，得手动配上相应策略才会生效，默认状态下不会自己这么做。
错：按写入时间淘汰最早的 key 不是 Redis 的默认策略，默认根本不会主动删任何 key。
对：听起来反直觉但确实如此——什么都不配的话，内存一满就直接拒写，想当缓存用就得自己去开一个淘汰策略。
错：Redis 没有把冷数据换出到磁盘这种分层存储机制，数据要么在内存里要么被淘汰。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: LRU eviction only happens if you explicitly configure a policy like allkeys-lru — it isn't the default.
Wrong: deleting the oldest-written key isn't the default either — by default Redis won't proactively delete anything.
Right: counterintuitive but true — the default is noeviction, so a full memory just rejects new writes; using Redis as a cache needs an explicit policy.
Wrong: Redis has no tiered mechanism that swaps cold data out to disk — data is either in memory or evicted.

scenario: Redis 纯做缓存：所有 key 都是数据库数据的可再生副本，内存满时希望自动腾出空间。
q: 应配置哪种淘汰策略？
options: allkeys-lru：对全部 key 做近似 LRU 淘汰
noeviction（默认，满了就拒写）
手动写定时任务 DEL 旧 key
把所有 key 的 TTL 都调得很短
why: 纯缓存里任何 key 都可以安全丢弃，allkeys-lru 让 Redis 淘汰最久未用的 key 来腾内存。
why_en: For a pure cache, allkeys-lru lets Redis evict the least recently used keys to make room since everything is reloadable.
whenOtherWins: 同一实例里混了不能丢的数据时，用 volatile-* 只淘汰带 TTL 的 key，或干脆把缓存和状态拆成两个实例。
options_en: allkeys-lru: apply approximate LRU eviction across all keys
noeviction (the default, which rejects writes once full)
Write a scheduled job that manually DELs old keys
Set a very short TTL on every key
tradeoff: 自动淘汰腾内存 vs 人工维护淘汰逻辑
q_en: Which eviction policy should you configure?
scenario_en: Redis is used purely as a cache: every key is a rebuildable copy of database data, and you want memory to free itself automatically once full.
optionExplanations: 对：这里每个 key 都能从数据库重新算出来，丢了不心疼，配上按最近最少用自动腾内存的策略正好。
只在容不得丢任何 key 时选：noeviction（默认）会在内存满时直接拒写，纯缓存场景下这只会让服务提前报错，没必要。
手写定时任务能做但要自己判断冷热、处理并发删除竞态，比内建的 LRU 采样淘汰更啰嗦，不是本题的最简方案。
短 TTL 能缓解但不是淘汰策略本身——它只是让数据更快过期，内存满时该拒写还是拒写，没有真正解决淘汰问题。
optionExplanations_en: Right: every key is a reproducible copy of DB data, safe to drop — allkeys-lru auto-evicts the least-recently-used key to free memory.
Only pick this when losing any key is unacceptable: noeviction (the default) just rejects writes once full — for a pure cache that just errors out for nothing.
A cron DEL loop can work, but you'd have to track hot/cold yourself and handle deletion races — more effort than built-in LRU sampling.
Short TTLs help but aren't an eviction policy — they just make data lapse sooner; once memory is full it still rejects writes.

scenario: Redis 内存到达 maxmemory，需要腾出一个 key。它不想为所有 key 维护一条精确 LRU 链表，因为每次 GET/SET 都移动链表会增加内存和 CPU 开销。
q: Redis 的 LRU 淘汰在实现上的特点是？
options: 精确维护一条全局访问顺序链表
严格按 key 的插入顺序淘汰
完全随机挑选 key 淘汰
抽样若干 key 做近似 LRU，不追踪精确顺序
why: Redis 给 key 记录最近访问时间；要淘汰时随机抽几个 key，挑其中最久没访问的删。抽样数越大越接近真 LRU，但 CPU 更高。
why_en: Redis stores recent-access metadata per key. On eviction, it samples a few keys and removes the stalest one in that sample. More samples approximate true LRU better but cost more CPU.
codeSample:
# Config idea
maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
maxmemory-samples 5

# Eviction idea when memory is full
evict_one_key():
  sample = random_keys(count=5)
  victim = max_by(sample, key => now - key.last_access_time)
  DEL victim

# Not guaranteed to be the global oldest key.
# It is the oldest among the sampled candidates.
options_en: It precisely maintains one global access-order linked list
It strictly evicts in insertion order
It picks keys to evict completely at random
It samples a handful of keys to approximate LRU without tracking exact order
tradeoff: 精确 LRU 更准但维护重 vs 采样 LRU 低成本且足够接近
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["memory full"] --> B["sample 5 keys"]
  B --> C["compare idle time"]
  C --> D["evict stalest sample"]
  E["hot key touched"] --> F["idle time reset"]

termDefinitions.meaning: LRU（最近最少使用）：优先淘汰最久没被访问的 key 的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU, or Least Recently Used, is a policy that evicts whichever key has gone the longest without being accessed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不找全局最老 key，而是在随机样本里找最老 key；多次淘汰后效果接近 LRU。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Instead of finding the globally oldest key, approximate LRU finds the oldest key in a random sample; repeated evictions behave close to LRU.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 配置项，控制每次淘汰前抽几个候选 key；默认常见值是 5，调大更准但更耗 CPU。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis setting that controls how many candidate keys to sample per eviction; higher values are more accurate but use more CPU.

q_en: What's distinctive about how Redis implements LRU eviction?
scenario_en: Redis has reached maxmemory and needs to free one key. It does not want to maintain an exact global LRU linked list because moving list nodes on every GET or SET costs memory and CPU.
optionExplanations: 错：维护一条全局精确 LRU 链表意味着每次 GET/SET 都要移动链表，Redis 为了省 CPU/内存不这么做。
错：按插入顺序淘汰是 FIFO，Redis 记的是最近访问时间，不是写入时间。
错：完全随机不看访问时间，会淘汰刚用过的热 key，Redis 至少会参考最近访问时间。
对：每个 key 会带一个最近访问的时间戳，真要腾地方时就随机抽一撮候选、挑其中最久没碰过的下手，抽的越多越准。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: maintaining one exact global LRU list means moving it on every GET/SET — Redis skips that to save CPU and memory.
Wrong: evicting by insertion order is FIFO; Redis tracks recency of access, not write time.
Wrong: fully random ignores access recency and could evict a key just used — Redis at least weighs recent access.
Right: Redis timestamps each key's last access, samples a few candidates on eviction, and drops the least-recently-used among them.

q: TTL 过期和淘汰策略（eviction）分别解决什么问题？
options: 两者本质上都是在解决同一个内存不足的问题
TTL 管数据新鲜度（staleness），eviction 管内存满了删谁
TTL 管的是内存占用，eviction 管的是数据新鲜度
两者语义完全等价，配置一个就能替代另一个
why: 过期处理 staleness，淘汰处理 memory pressure——面试里把这两个混为一谈是常见丢分点。
why_en: Expiration handles staleness while eviction handles memory pressure; they solve different problems.
options_en: Both are fundamentally solving the same out-of-memory problem
TTL handles staleness, while eviction handles what to delete when memory is full
TTL governs memory usage, while eviction governs data freshness
The two are fully equivalent in semantics, and configuring one can replace the other
tradeoff: 新鲜度控制（TTL）vs 内存压力控制（eviction）
q_en: What problem does TTL expiration solve versus what problem does eviction solve?
optionExplanations: 错：过期处理的是数据新不新鲜，淘汰处理的是内存够不够用，是两个不同的问题，混为一谈是常见丢分点。
对：TTL 处理的是这份数据还新不新鲜，eviction 处理的是内存不够用时该删谁，两件事要分开配置。
错：说反了——TTL 管新鲜度，不是内存占用；eviction 才是应对内存满的机制。
错：两者语义不等价，配了 TTL 不代表内存满时就有淘汰空间，配了淘汰策略也不能让数据保持新鲜。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: expiry is about whether a value is still fresh, eviction is about whether memory is full — conflating them is a common slip.
Right: TTL handles staleness (is this value still fresh), eviction handles memory pressure (who gets deleted when full).
Wrong: that's reversed — TTL governs freshness, not memory footprint; eviction is the mechanism for a full memory.
Wrong: they aren't interchangeable — a TTL doesn't create eviction headroom, and an eviction policy doesn't keep data fresh.

scenario: Ticketmaster 式抢座：多台应用服务器并发处理同一张票，同一时刻只允许一个进程操作，且锁要能在持有者崩溃后自动释放。
q: 获取锁的正确命令是？
options: SETNX lock:concert:343 1（不带过期时间）
SET lock:concert:343 my-token NX EX 30
先 GET 判断不存在再 SET
INCR lock:concert:343
why: NX 保证只有 key 不存在时才写入成功（即抢到锁），EX 30 让崩溃的持有者最多占 30 秒，随机 token 是稍后安全释放的凭证。
why_en: SET with NX and EX atomically creates the lock only if absent and adds an expiry so a crashed holder cannot keep it forever.
whenOtherWins: 若被保护的数据就在数据库里，SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 行锁或条件 UPDATE 往往能直接取代分布式锁，更简单也更安全。
codeSample:
SET lock:concert:343 my-token NX EX 30
# OK  -> 抢到锁
# nil -> 已被占用，等待后重试
options_en: SETNX lock:concert:343 1 (no expiry set)
SET lock:concert:343 my-token NX EX 30
GET to check absence, then SET separately
INCR lock:concert:343
tradeoff: 原子获取 + 自动过期 vs 无过期时间的锁永远占用风险

termDefinitions.meaning: NX：SET 命令的标志，只有 key 不存在时才写入成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NX is a SET flag meaning the write only succeeds if the key does not already exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: EX：SET 命令的标志，给这次写入的 key 设置以秒为单位的过期时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EX is a SET flag that attaches a expiry, in seconds, to the key being written.

termDefinitions.meaning: SETNX：老式的「不存在才写入」命令，不能同时带过期时间，已被 SET ... NX EX 取代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SETNX is the older set-if-absent command that cannot attach an expiry in the same call, superseded by SET with NX and EX.

q_en: What is the correct command to acquire the lock?
scenario_en: Ticketmaster-style seat grabbing: many application servers process the same ticket concurrently, only one process may act on it at a time, and the lock must auto-release if its holder crashes.
optionExplanations: 错：SETNX 本身能抢锁，但不带过期时间——持有者一崩溃，锁就永远没人能释放。
对：NX 这个条件保证「没人占着这个 key 才能写进去」，也就是抢锁本身；EX 30 则保证持有者崩了最多占 30 秒就自动放手。
错：先 GET 再 SET 是两条独立命令，中间可能被别的进程插队同时判断「不存在」，锁失去互斥性。
错：INCR 只会把计数器加一，不是「仅当不存在才写入」的判断，做不了互斥抢锁。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: SETNX alone can grab the lock, but without a TTL — if the holder crashes, nobody can ever release it.
Right: NX ensures the write only succeeds when the key doesn't exist yet, and EX 30 auto-releases a crashed holder after 30s.
Wrong: GET-then-SET is two separate commands — another process can slip in and also see 'not exists', breaking mutual exclusion.
Wrong: INCR just increments a counter; it isn't a 'write only if absent' check, so it can't do mutually exclusive locking.

q: SET 命令里 NX 标志的语义是？
options: 仅当 key 不存在时写入才成功
写入后立即设为过期
跳过复制直接向客户端返回
无条件强制覆盖已有的值
why: NX = not exists：key 已存在则失败返回 nil。这一个原子判断本身就是「抢锁」动作。
why_en: NX makes the SET succeed only if the key does not already exist, which is the atomic lock acquisition.
options_en: The write only succeeds if the key does not already exist
The write is immediately marked as expired
It skips replication and returns to the client right away
It unconditionally overwrites whatever value is already there
codeSample:
SET lock:a token NX
# OK  -> key 不存在，写入成功
# nil -> key 已存在，写入失败
q_en: What does the NX flag on the SET command mean?
optionExplanations: 对：这个标志的字面意思是「不存在才写」——key 已经有了就直接失败返回 nil，这个原子检查本身就是抢锁的动作。
错：写入后立即过期是 PX 0/EX 0 之类的过期设置，跟 NX 这个存在性判断是两码事。
错：NX 不影响复制流程，写入照样会正常复制给副本，它只是控制「要不要写」的条件。
错：无条件强制覆盖是没有任何 flag 的普通 SET，NX 恰恰是加了「不存在才写」的限制，跟强制覆盖相反。
optionExplanations_en: Right: NX means not-exists — if the key already exists the write fails with nil; that atomic check is the 'grab the lock' action.
Wrong: lapsing immediately after write is what EX 0/PX 0 would do — unrelated to NX's existence check.
Wrong: NX doesn't skip replication; the write still replicates normally — it only gates whether the write happens.
Wrong: unconditional overwrite is a plain SET with no flag; NX does the opposite, adding a 'write only if absent' condition.

q: 给锁 key 加 EX 30 过期时间，防的是哪种事故？
options: 别人恶意偷走这把锁
服务器之间的时钟回拨
网络发生分区
持有者崩溃后锁永远不会被释放
why: 没有过期时间，崩溃的进程会永久持锁把所有人挡在外面；EX 让锁最多被占一个 TTL 的时长。
why_en: The expiry ensures a crashed lock holder cannot keep the lock forever.
options_en: Someone maliciously stealing the lock
Clock drift between servers
A network partition
A crashed holder keeping the lock forever
q_en: What failure does adding an EX 30 expiry to the lock key prevent?
optionExplanations: 错：EX 挡不住恶意偷锁——没有过期时间时锁反而更容易被永久占死，跟「被偷」是两回事。
错：时钟回拨影响的是 TTL 判断的精确性，不是 EX 这个机制本身要解决的问题。
错：网络分区会让客户端连不上 Redis，跟锁会不会被永久占用是不同的故障场景。
对：要是压根不设过期时间，进程一崩，这把锁就再也没人能拿到了；EX 把这个占用时长封了顶。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: EX doesn't defend against a malicious lock theft — without a TTL the lock is more likely to be held forever.
Wrong: clock skew affects how precisely the TTL is judged, not the problem EX itself is meant to solve.
Wrong: a network partition just means the client can't reach Redis — a different failure mode entirely.
Right: without a TTL, a crashed process would hold the lock forever and block everyone; EX caps how long it can be held.

scenario: worker A 用 Redis 锁处理 order:123：SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000。A 暂停超过 30 秒后锁过期，worker B 又用 tokenB 抢到同一个锁。此时 A 醒来准备释放锁。
q: 锁的 value 放一个随机 token（而不是固定值）的目的是？
options: 对锁的内容做加密
让 key 在集群里分布更均匀
释放时能先验证锁还是不是自己的，避免删掉别人的锁
统计这把锁被持有了多久
why: 随机 token 是这次持锁请求的身份证。A 释放时先看 value 还是不是 tokenA；如果锁已过期并被 B 改成 tokenB，A 就不能 DEL，否则会删掉 B 的锁，让第三个人也进来。
why_en: The random token is the identity of this lock request. When A releases, it first checks the value is still tokenA; if B has reacquired the lock with tokenB, A must not delete it.
codeSample:
SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000
# A pauses for 45s; Redis expires the key.
SET lock:order:123 tokenB NX PX 30000

# A's safe release:
if GET lock:order:123 == tokenA then DEL lock:order:123
# value is tokenB, so A must not delete it.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant R as Redis
  participant B as Worker B
  participant C as Worker C
  A->>R: SET lock tokenA NX PX 30s
  Note over A: pauses 45s
  Note over R: tokenA expires
  B->>R: SET lock tokenB NX PX 30s
  A->>R: safe release checks GET == tokenA
  R-->>A: value is tokenB, do not DEL
  C-->>R: cannot enter while B's lock exists

termDefinitions.meaning: lock value：Redis 锁 key 里存的值，通常是本次加锁请求生成的随机 token，用来释放时确认「这把锁还是我的」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock value is the value stored in the Redis lock key, usually a random token for this acquire attempt, used to verify ownership on release.

termDefinitions.meaning: random token：每次抢锁生成的唯一请求标识；它不是为了加密或分片，而是为了避免旧持有者误删新持有者的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A random token is a unique request id generated for each lock acquisition; it prevents an old holder from deleting a new holder's lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: blind DEL：释放锁时不检查 value，直接删除 lock key；如果锁已过期并被别人重拿，就会删掉别人的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blind DEL deletes the lock key without checking its value, which can remove someone else's lock after the original lock expired.

options_en: To encrypt the lock's contents
To spread the key more evenly across the cluster
So release can first verify the lock is still yours before deleting it
To measure how long the lock was held
q_en: Why store a random token as the lock's value instead of a fixed value?
scenario_en: Worker A processes order:123 with a Redis lock: SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000. A pauses for more than 30 seconds, the lock expires, and worker B acquires the same lock with tokenB. Now A wakes up and tries to release the lock.
optionExplanations: 错：随机 token 不是为了加密内容，它就是一段明文身份标识，用来在释放时比对。
错：token 放在 value 里不影响 key 在集群里怎么分布，key 名才决定落在哪个槽。
对：这段随机值相当于这次持锁发的一张凭证，释放前先核对凭证还是不是自己的，别手滑删掉别人刚抢到的锁。
错：统计持锁时长可以另外记时间戳做，不是 token 本身要解决的问题，token 的作用是身份校验。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the random token isn't for encrypting content — it's a plain identity marker compared at release time.
Wrong: putting a token in the value doesn't change how the key distributes across the cluster — the key name decides that.
Right: the random token is this lock's ID card — on release, check the value is still your token before deleting.
Wrong: timing how long a lock was held is a separate timestamp concern — the token's job is identity verification.

scenario: worker A 用 SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000 抢到锁后暂停 45 秒。锁过期后，worker B 用 tokenB 抢到同一把锁；此时 A 醒来执行 DEL lock:order:123。
scenario_en: Worker A acquires SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000, then pauses for 45 seconds. The lock expires, worker B acquires the same lock with tokenB, and A wakes up and runs DEL lock:order:123.
q: 释放锁时直接盲目 DEL，风险是什么？
options: DEL 本身不是一条原子命令，中途可能被打断
DEL 命令在 Redis 里执行得太慢，拖累性能
你的锁可能已过期并被他人获得，DEL 会删掉他们的锁
被删的 key 会进回收站继续占用内存
why: token 只有被读取并比较时才有保护作用；盲目 DEL 不看 value。A 的 tokenA 已过期，B 写入 tokenB 后，A 再 DEL 会直接删掉 B 的锁。
why_en: The token only helps if release reads and compares it; a blind DEL ignores the value. After tokenA expires and B writes tokenB, A's DEL deletes B's lock.
codeSample:
SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000
# A pauses for 45s; tokenA expires.
SET lock:order:123 tokenB NX PX 30000

# Unsafe: A releases without checking the value.
DEL lock:order:123
# This deletes B's tokenB lock.

# Safe release must compare first:
# if GET lock:order:123 == tokenA then DEL lock:order:123
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant R as Redis
  participant B as Worker B
  participant C as Worker C
  A->>R: SET lock tokenA NX PX 30s
  Note over A: pauses 45s
  Note over R: tokenA expires
  B->>R: SET lock tokenB NX PX 30s
  A->>R: DEL lock without checking value
  Note over R: tokenB is deleted
  C->>R: SET lock tokenC NX PX 30s succeeds
  Note over B,C: B and C can both think they hold the lock

termDefinitions.meaning: blind DEL：释放锁时直接 DEL lock key，不先 GET value 检查 token 是否属于自己。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blind DEL deletes the lock key without first reading the value and checking whether the token belongs to this client.

termDefinitions.meaning: lock token：每次抢锁写入的唯一 value；只有释放时比较 token，才能避免旧持有者删掉新持有者的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock token is the unique value written during acquisition; comparing it on release prevents an old holder from deleting a new holder's lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: mutual exclusion：同一时刻只有一个 worker 应该进入受保护区；误删新锁会破坏这个保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mutual exclusion means only one worker should enter the protected section at a time; deleting a new lock breaks that guarantee.

options_en: DEL itself is not an atomic command and could be interrupted midway
The DEL command executes too slowly in Redis, hurting performance
Your lock may have already expired and been re-acquired, so DEL deletes their lock instead
The deleted key sits in a recycle bin and keeps using memory
q_en: What's the risk of blindly running DEL when releasing a lock?
optionExplanations: 错：DEL 本身是原子命令，不存在「执行到一半被打断」的问题，风险出在没检查 value 就删。
错：DEL 是很快的原语操作，性能不是这个场景的风险点，真正的风险是删错了目标。
对：凭证要被读出来核对才管用；直接 DEL 根本不看 value 是谁的，A 的锁过期后 B 抢到了，A 再删就会把 B 的锁一起删掉。
错：Redis 的 DEL 是真删除，没有回收站，被删的 key 立刻释放内存，不会继续占用。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: DEL itself is atomic — there's no 'interrupted halfway' failure; the real risk is deleting without checking the value first.
Wrong: DEL is a fast primitive; performance isn't the risk here — the risk is deleting the wrong holder's lock.
Right: a token only protects you if you read and compare it; a blind DEL skips that, so it can delete a lock someone else already grabbed.
Wrong: Redis's DEL is a real delete with no recycle bin — the key's memory is freed immediately.

scenario: 释放分布式锁：必须「核对 token 是自己的 → 再删除」，且两步之间不能被其他命令插入。
q: 正确的实现是？
options: 用 Lua 脚本一次执行 GET 比对 + DEL
先 GET 再 DEL 两条独立命令
WATCH 之后直接 DEL
EXPIRE 设为 0
why: Redis 把整个 Lua 脚本当一条命令在单线程上执行，check-and-delete 因此原子；拆成两条命令，中间锁可能易主。
why_en: Redis runs the whole Lua script as one command on its single thread, making the check-and-delete atomic.
whenOtherWins: 单条命令本身已是原子（如 SET NX EX）就不需要 Lua；Lua 用在「多步必须一起发生」的场合。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["SET NX EX token"] --> B["Do work"]
  B --> C["Lua compare token"]
  C --> D["DEL only owner"]
options_en: Run a Lua script that does the GET compare and DEL as one command
Send GET then DEL as two separate commands
WATCH the key, then DEL it directly
Set EXPIRE to 0 on the key
tradeoff: 多步骤原子性 vs 拆成多条命令中途可能易主

termDefinitions.meaning: Lua：Redis 内嵌的脚本语言，整段脚本作为一条命令原子执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lua is the scripting language Redis embeds, and the whole script runs as one atomic command.

termDefinitions.meaning: WATCH：乐观并发控制指令，标记一个 key，若它被改动则后续事务会中止。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WATCH is an optimistic-concurrency command that flags a key so a later transaction aborts if it changed.

q_en: What's the correct implementation?
scenario_en: Releasing a distributed lock must "verify the token is yours, then delete" atomically, with no other command able to slip in between the two steps.
optionExplanations: 对：整段 Lua 脚本会被当成一条命令在单线程里跑完，核对身份和删除这两步因此绑成一个原子操作，插不进别的命令。
错：GET 和 DEL 分成两条命令发，中间给了别的客户端插队改持有者的机会，先核对再删这个逻辑就不再是一个整体动作。
错：WATCH 只对配合 MULTI/EXEC 的事务生效，直接跟着一条 DEL 走并不会让「先核对再删」这两步变成原子。
错：EXPIRE 设为 0 是删除的另一种写法，但同样没有先比对 value 是不是自己的，风险和盲目 DEL 一样。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Redis runs an entire Lua script as one command on its single thread, so check-and-delete is atomic — nothing can slip in.
Wrong: GET and DEL are two separate commands — another client could change the lock's holder in between, breaking atomicity.
Wrong: WATCH only matters paired with MULTI/EXEC; following it with a plain DEL doesn't make check-then-delete atomic.
Wrong: setting a TTL to 0 is just another way to delete — it still skips comparing the value first, same risk as a blind DEL.

scenario: 两个 worker 都想把 stock:item:1 从 10 扣到 9。悲观方案会先抢锁，让别人等；WATCH 方案不阻塞别人，而是在 EXEC 提交时检查 stock:item:1 是否被改过。
q: 「先抢锁再干活」和 Redis 的 WATCH + MULTI/EXEC 分别属于哪种并发控制？
options: 两者都属于乐观并发控制，不阻塞其他客户端
前者悲观；后者乐观——被 WATCH 的 key 中途变了，事务就中止
前者是乐观策略；后者是悲观阻塞式并发控制
两者都属于会阻塞其他客户端的悲观锁
why: 先抢锁是悲观并发控制：先把别人挡在外面。WATCH+MULTI/EXEC 是乐观并发控制：允许别人同时写，但 EXEC 时如果 watched key 已变化，就返回失败并重试。
why_en: Grabbing a lock up front is pessimistic because others must wait. WATCH with MULTI/EXEC is optimistic: other clients can still write, but EXEC aborts if the watched key changed.
codeSample:
# Pessimistic: take the lock before touching the resource.
SET lock:stock:item:1 workerA NX PX 30000
DECR stock:item:1
DEL lock:stock:item:1

# Optimistic: watch, compute, then commit conditionally.
retry:
  WATCH stock:item:1
  old = GET stock:item:1
  if old <= 0:
    UNWATCH
    return sold_out

  MULTI
    SET stock:item:1 old - 1
  ok = EXEC          # nil/null if stock:item:1 changed after WATCH

  if ok == null:
    goto retry       # someone else changed it; reread and recompute
options_en: Both are optimistic concurrency control that never blocks other clients
The first is pessimistic; the second is optimistic and aborts if the watched key changed mid-transaction
The first is optimistic; the second is pessimistic and blocks
Both are pessimistic locks that block other clients
tradeoff: 先占锁的悲观并发 vs WATCH+MULTI/EXEC 的乐观并发
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Client A
  participant R as Redis
  participant B as Client B
  A->>R: WATCH stock:item:1
  A->>R: GET stock:item:1 returns 10
  B->>R: DECR stock:item:1
  A->>R: MULTI
  A->>R: SET stock:item:1 9
  A->>R: EXEC
  R-->>A: abort because watched key changed
  A->>R: retry from WATCH

termDefinitions.term: 悲观并发控制 / pessimistic concurrency
termDefinitions.meaning: 先假设会冲突，所以先抢锁；没拿到锁的人等待或失败。
