termDefinitions.meaningEn: Assume conflicts will happen, so acquire a lock first; clients without the lock wait or fail.

termDefinitions.term: 乐观并发控制 / optimistic concurrency
termDefinitions.meaning: 先假设冲突少，允许并发执行；提交时检查版本或 key 是否变化，冲突再重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Assume conflicts are rare, let work proceed concurrently, and validate at commit time; retry on conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: WATCH 会监视 key；从 WATCH 到 EXEC 之间只要该 key 被别人改过，EXEC 就不会提交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WATCH monitors a key; if another client changes it before EXEC, EXEC does not commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: MULTI 开始排队事务命令，EXEC 尝试一次执行这些命令；配合 WATCH 时，EXEC 变成有条件提交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MULTI queues transaction commands and EXEC attempts to run them; with WATCH, EXEC becomes a conditional commit.

q_en: Which concurrency-control style does 'acquire the lock first' belong to, versus Redis's WATCH with MULTI/EXEC?
scenario_en: Two workers both want to decrement stock:item:1 from 10 to 9. A pessimistic design grabs a lock and makes others wait; a WATCH design does not block others and checks whether stock:item:1 changed when EXEC commits.
optionExplanations: 错：先抢锁本身就是把别人挡在外面等的做法，这是悲观防守，不是乐观。
对：先抢锁属于悲观并发——把别人堵在门外；改用「先观察再提交」的方式，允许大家一起改，只在提交那一刻核对被盯的 key 变没变，变了就失败重试。
错：说反了——先抢锁那种堵别人的做法才是悲观，允许同时写、提交时才检查冲突的那种才是乐观。
错：允许并发写、提交时才判定冲突的这套并不会挡住其他客户端同时操作，它只在最后关头判断冲突，不是靠阻塞实现的。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: grabbing a lock first means blocking everyone else out while you work — that's pessimistic, not optimistic.
Right: grab-lock-first is pessimistic, blocking others out; WATCH+MULTI/EXEC is optimistic, aborting at EXEC if the watched key changed.
Wrong: that's reversed — grabbing a lock first is pessimistic, and WATCH+MULTI/EXEC is the optimistic, non-blocking one.
Wrong: WATCH+MULTI/EXEC doesn't block other clients from writing — it only checks for conflicts at commit time.

scenario: 客户端 C1 在 Redis primary 上用 SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000 抢到锁；primary 已经回 OK，但这条锁记录还没复制到 replica，primary 就崩了。
q: 单节点 Redis 锁在主从 failover 时的经典失效方式是？
options: 主挂时锁还没异步复制到副本，新主把同一把锁再发给别人
锁 key 被迁移到了错误的槽位
锁的 TTL 被意外重置为 0
副本拒绝所有加锁请求
why: 主回 OK 早于副本应用；若主在复制前挂，新主没有 lock key，会再次 SET NX 成功，互斥被打破。
why_en: The primary can reply OK before the replica applies the lock. If the primary dies first, the new primary has no lock key and SET NX can succeed again.
codeSample:
C1 -> primary: SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000
primary -> C1: OK
primary --X--> replica: lock not replicated yet
primary crashes
replica promoted to new primary
C2 -> new primary: SET lock:order:123 tokenB NX PX 30000
new primary -> C2: OK
# C1 and C2 can both believe they hold the lock.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C1 as 客户端1
    participant P as 主节点
    participant R as 副本(将上位)
    participant C2 as 客户端2
    C1->>P: SET lock NX EX (成功)
    Note over P: 崩溃(锁未复制出去)
    R->>R: 被提升为新主
    C2->>R: SET lock NX EX (也成功!)
    Note over C1,C2: 两个客户端同时持锁
options_en: The primary dies before the lock replicates, so the promoted replica grants the same lock again
The lock key gets migrated to the wrong slot
The lock's TTL accidentally resets to zero
The replica refuses every lock request
tradeoff: 单节点 Redis 锁简单低延迟 vs failover 可能破坏互斥

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点先回 OK，副本之后才追复制流；中间有一个丢尾部写入的窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary replies OK first and replicas apply the replication stream later, leaving a window where tail writes can be lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点故障后，把副本提升成新的主节点继续服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover promotes a replica to become the new primary after the old primary fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 加锁常见写法：key 不存在才写入，并给锁设置过期时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A common Redis lock command: set only if the key does not exist, with an expiry time.

q_en: What's the classic way a single-node Redis lock fails during primary-replica failover?
scenario_en: Client C1 acquires a lock on the Redis primary with SET lock:order:123 tokenA NX PX 30000. The primary replies OK, but the lock record has not replicated to the replica before the primary crashes.
optionExplanations: 对：主节点回复确认的时候，副本可能还没收到这条锁记录；它没撑到复制完就挂了的话，新主上没有这个 key，会让第二次抢锁也成功，互斥就破了。
错：这次失效跟槽位路由无关，锁 key 还在原来该在的槽，问题出在异步复制的时间差，不是迁移错了地方。
错：TTL 没有被谁重置，问题是这条锁记录压根没来得及复制到副本，副本上根本不存在这个 key。
错：副本不会主动拒绝加锁请求；被提升成主之后，它会正常处理新的 SET NX，只是「正常处理」恰恰造出了第二把锁。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the primary acks before the replica applies the write; if it dies before replicating the lock record, the new primary lets a second SET NX succeed — breaking mutual exclusion.
Wrong: this failure has nothing to do with slot routing — the lock key is still on its correct slot; it's an async-replication timing gap.
Wrong: nobody resets the TTL — the problem is the lock record never made it to the replica in time.
Wrong: a replica doesn't reject lock requests on its own; once promoted, it processes a new SET NX normally — creating a second lock.

scenario: 你要保护 order:123，同一时间只能一个 worker 处理。注意这不是 Redis Cluster 分片；Redlock 会把同一个 lock key 发给 5 个独立 Redis，至少 3 个同意才算拿到锁。
scenario_en: You need to protect order:123 so only one worker handles it at a time. This is not Redis Cluster sharding; Redlock sends the same lock key to five independent Redis nodes and succeeds only if at least three agree.
q: Redlock 算法的核心思路是？
options: 只是把锁的 TTL 设得比原来更长一些
在多数（quorum）个互不复制的独立 Redis 节点上都拿到锁才算成功
把锁写进 AOF 日志并强制立即刷盘
用 hash tag 把锁强制绑到某个固定槽位
why: Cluster 是 key→一个槽；Redlock 是同一锁 key→多个 Redis。多数 SET NX 成功且未超 TTL 才算拿锁。
why_en: Cluster maps a key to one slot; Redlock sends the same lock key to several independent Redis nodes. The lock is acquired only if a majority SET NX succeeds before TTL expires.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["worker A"] --> R1["Redis 1 OK"]
    C --> R2["Redis 2 OK"]
    C --> R3["Redis 3 OK"]
    C -.timeout.-> R4["Redis 4"]
    C -.down.-> R5["Redis 5"]
    R1 --> Q["3/5 quorum"]
    R2 --> Q
    R3 --> Q
    Q --> OK["lease acquired"]
options_en: Just set the lock's TTL to something longer than before
Acquire the lock on a majority (quorum) of independent, non-replicating Redis nodes
Write the lock into the AOF log and force an immediate fsync
Use a hash tag to pin the lock to one fixed slot

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是多数派；5 个节点至少 3 个，3 个节点至少 2 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is a majority: at least three of five nodes, or two of three nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 分布式锁算法：同一个 lock key 写到多个独立 Redis，拿到多数才成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis distributed lock algorithm that writes the same lock key to several independent Redis nodes and succeeds with a majority.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 key 算 slot，一个 key 只归一个主节点；这是容量分片，不是 Redlock 的多数裁决。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster hashes each key to one slot and one primary; that is capacity sharding, not Redlock quorum voting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有过期时间的锁；只在 TTL 剩余窗口内有效，过期后别人可以重新抢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-limited lock that is valid only within its TTL window; after expiry, another client may acquire it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次抢锁写入的唯一值；释放时先比对 token，避免删掉别人的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A unique value written during acquisition; release compares the token first so it does not delete someone else's lock.

termDefinitions.term: 互不复制的独立 Redis 节点
termDefinitions.meaning: 这些节点不是同一主从组；一个节点丢锁不会变成主从切换丢锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Independent Redis nodes are not replicas, so one node losing a lock is not a replica-failover lock loss.

q_en: What is the core idea behind the Redlock algorithm?
optionExplanations: 错：延长 TTL 只是给单个 Redis 节点更多容错时间，跟 Redlock 要在多个独立节点上都拿锁的核心思路无关。
对：Redlock 把同一个锁 key 发给多个互不复制的独立 Redis 节点，多数（quorum）在未超 TTL 内都 SET NX 成功才算真拿到锁。
错：Redlock 靠多数派节点共识判定拿没拿到锁，不是靠把锁写进 AOF 并强制刷盘。
错：Redlock 讨论的是同一把锁分布到多个独立 Redis 实例，跟 Cluster 里用 hash tag 把 key 绑定到固定槽位是不同的机制。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a longer TTL just buys one node more slack — unrelated to Redlock's core idea of acquiring the lock on multiple independent nodes.
Right: Redlock sends the same lock key to several independent, non-replicating Redis nodes; a quorum majority acquiring it within the TTL counts as a real lock.
Wrong: Redlock decides success by majority-node agreement, not by forcing the lock into AOF and fsyncing it.
Wrong: Redlock spreads one lock across multiple independent Redis instances — different from pinning a key to one Cluster slot via a hash tag.

scenario: worker A 用 Redlock 拿到 order:123 的 30 秒租约后卡住 45 秒；锁过期后 worker B 拿到新锁并写入。A 醒来时，本地还拿着旧锁结果。
q: Kleppmann 对 Redlock 的著名批评指出：即使算法成立，仍会发生什么？
options: N 个节点里多数派永远无法达成，算法根本跑不起来
所有参与节点的时钟必须做到精确同步
客户端 GC 暂停或卡顿后，会拿着已经过期的锁继续操作
获取锁的吞吐量在多节点方案下太低，扛不住并发
why: Redlock 只管“谁拿到租约”；租约过期后，旧持有者可能醒来继续写。资源端若不查 fencing token/版本号，旧写仍能覆盖新写。
why_en: Redlock decides who acquired the lease, but after the lease expires a stale holder can wake up and keep writing. Without a fencing token or version check at the resource, an old write can overwrite a newer one.
codeSample:
A = redlock.acquire("order:123", ttl=30s)
pause(A, 45s)          # GC / scheduler / network delay

B = redlock.acquire("order:123", ttl=30s)
DB.write(order=123, status="paid-by-B")

# A wakes up after its lease expired.
DB.write(order=123, status="paid-by-A")  # unsafe unless DB rejects stale token
options_en: A majority of the N nodes can never be reached, so the algorithm cannot even run
Every participating node's clock must be kept in perfect sync
A paused or slow client can resume acting after its lock has already expired
The lock's acquisition throughput is too low across multiple nodes to handle real concurrency
tradeoff: Redlock 多数派拿锁 vs 资源端 fencing 才能挡旧写
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant L as Redlock
  participant B as Worker B
  participant DB as Database
  A->>L: acquire lease 30s
  Note over A: paused 45s
  B->>L: acquire new lease
  B->>DB: write with new state
  A->>DB: wakes and writes stale state
  Note over DB: reject only if token/version is checked

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 分布式锁算法：向多个独立 Redis 节点抢锁，拿到多数才算成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis distributed lock algorithm that acquires a lock on a majority of independent Redis nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC（垃圾回收）：运行时自动回收内存的过程，期间进程可能暂停一段时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GC, or garbage collection, is the runtime's automatic memory cleanup, which can pause a process for a while.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单调递增的授锁编号；数据库/存储只接受比已记录编号更新的写入，用来挡旧持有者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An increasing lock-grant number; storage accepts only newer tokens to reject stale holders.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有过期时间的锁；过期后别人可以重新获得同一资源的资格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock with an expiry time; after expiry, another client may acquire the same resource.

q_en: Kleppmann's famous critique of Redlock says that even if the algorithm holds, what can still happen?
scenario_en: Worker A acquires a 30-second Redlock lease for order:123, then stalls for 45 seconds. After the lock expires, worker B acquires a new lock and writes. When A wakes up, it still has its old local lock result.
optionExplanations: 错：Kleppmann 的批评不是说 quorum 达不成，而是即使算法本身成立，正确性依然可能被打破。
错：Redlock 确实对时钟敏感，但批评的核心不是「必须精确同步」这个前提要求，而是锁过期后旧持有者仍可能继续写。
对：租约一过，卡住的旧持有者醒过来时根本不知道自己已经掉线，还可能拿着这把没用的锁继续写下去，除非下游会核对递增编号或版本才拦得住。
错：这条批评讲的是正确性漏洞，不是吞吐量或性能问题，Redlock 的吞吐瓶颈不是 Kleppmann 这篇批评的重点。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Kleppmann's critique isn't that quorum can't be reached — it's that correctness can still break even when the algorithm succeeds.
Wrong: Redlock is clock-sensitive, but the core critique isn't 'clocks must sync precisely' — it's a stale holder writing past its lease.
Right: after the lease lapses, a holder that was paused wakes up unaware it's stale and may keep writing, unless the resource checks a fencing token or version.
Wrong: this critique is about a correctness hole, not throughput — acquisition throughput isn't Kleppmann's point here.

scenario: 支付/库存服务用 Redis 锁保护 order:123：worker A 拿到 30 秒锁后开始处理，但因为 GC、网络卡顿或外部 API 慢暂停了 45 秒。锁自动过期后，worker B 又拿到锁并写入了正确的新状态。此时 A 醒来，如果它还直接写数据库，就会用旧判断覆盖 B 的结果。
scenario_en: A payment or inventory service protects order:123 with a Redis lock. Worker A gets a 30-second lock but pauses for 45 seconds because of GC, network delay, or a slow external API. The lock expires, worker B acquires it and writes the correct newer state. If A wakes up and still writes the database, it can overwrite B with stale data.
q: 防止「过期锁的持有者继续写坏数据」的标准手段是？
options: 让持有者每隔几秒就主动给锁续租延长时限
简单粗暴地把锁的 TTL 加大十倍来兜底
同时申请两把互相独立的锁做双重保险来兜底
fencing token：每次授锁附带递增编号，存储层拒绝旧编号的写入
why: 锁过期不会让旧 worker 自动停。每次授锁发递增 fencing token，写 DB 时带 token；B 的 18 写入后，A 的 17 会被存储层拒绝，续租或加长 TTL 只能降概率。
why_en: An expired Redis lock cannot stop the old worker, so each grant needs a higher fencing token and storage must reject stale tokens.
whenOtherWins: 如果过期后最多只是重复做一次幂等小任务，比如重复刷新缓存，Redis 锁加随机 token 通常够用；只要会影响钱、库存、唯一状态、leader 写入，就要让数据层检查 fencing token 或版本号。
options_en: Have the holder proactively renew the lock's lease every few seconds to extend it
Just brute-force the lock's TTL to ten times longer as a safety net
Acquire two mutually independent locks at once as a double safeguard
A fencing token: each grant carries an increasing number, and storage rejects writes stamped with an old one
tradeoff: Redis 锁的简单互斥 vs 数据层 fencing 的真正防旧写能力
codeSample:
SET lock:order:123 request-A NX PX 30000
INCR lock_token:order:123   # returns 17

# Storage, not Redis, rejects stale holders.
UPDATE orders
SET status = :status, last_fencing_token = :token
WHERE id = :order_id
  AND :token > last_fencing_token;
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant R as Redis lock
  participant B as Worker B
  participant DB as Database or storage
  A->>R: SET NX PX succeeds, token 17
  Note over A: pauses longer than TTL
  B->>R: SET NX PX succeeds, token 18
  B->>DB: write with token 18
  DB-->>B: accept and record last_token=18
  A->>DB: stale write with token 17
  DB-->>A: reject

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token：每次授锁都附带的单调递增编号，资源端只接受比已记录编号更新的写入，用来隔离旧持有者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is an increasing number issued with each lock grant that storage uses to reject writes from a stale holder.

termDefinitions.meaning: lock value：Redis 锁里常放的随机 requestId，用来释放锁时确认「这把锁还是我的」。它防误删，不防过期后的旧写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock value is a random requestId stored in the Redis lock so a client deletes only its own lock. It prevents accidental unlocks, not stale writes after expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS：带条件的写入，只有版本号、token 或旧值匹配时才更新；SQL 的 WHERE version/token 条件和 DynamoDB ConditionExpression 都是常见形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAS, or compare-and-set, updates only if a version, token, or previous value condition still matches; SQL conditional updates and DynamoDB ConditionExpression are common forms.

q_en: What's the standard technique to stop an expired lock's holder from corrupting data with a stale write?
optionExplanations: 错：续租能降低锁提前过期的概率，但挡不住已经在写的旧持有者继续写，不是根治手段。
错：TTL 再大也可能被 GC/卡顿超过，只是降低概率、还拖慢故障恢复，不是标准做法。
错：两把独立锁互不知道对方状态，反而增加协调复杂度，解决不了「旧持有者继续写」这个问题。
对：每次授锁发一个递增编号，存储层只认更大的编号、拒绝旧编号的写入，直接挡住过期锁持有者的迟到写。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: renewing the lease lowers the odds of early lapse, but doesn't stop a holder that's already writing from continuing.
Wrong: any TTL can be exceeded by a GC pause or stall; making it huge only lowers the odds and slows recovery.
Wrong: two independent locks don't know about each other, adding coordination complexity without stopping a stale holder.
Right: each grant issues an increasing number; the store accepts only the higher one and rejects older writes — blocking a stale holder's late write.

scenario: 同一张票、同一笔订单、同一个司机派单，同一时刻只能被一个 worker 处理。Redis 锁通常就是一个带 TTL 的 key，例如 SET lock:order:123 worker-A NX PX 30000；A 拿到锁表示 30 秒内别人先别处理 order:123。问题是锁存在 Redis 里，真实业务数据通常在 MySQL/DynamoDB/S3/外部支付系统里，锁过期不会自动让 A 的代码停下来，也不会自动阻止 A 继续写下游。
q: 正确的态度是？
options: 把 TTL 直接加长到 10 分钟
上 Redlock 就万无一失
把 Redis 锁当作正确性的基石
Redis 锁只当效率优化；正确性靠数据层约束或共识系统
why: Redis 锁只能减少并发，不能让过期持有者停手；A 暂停、锁过期、B 写新状态后，A 醒来仍可能写下游。所以钱、库存、唯一状态要由 DB 条件写、版本号或 fencing token 拒绝旧写。
why_en: Use Redis locks as a concurrency throttle, but enforce money, inventory, and uniqueness invariants in storage with conditional writes, versions, or fencing tokens.
whenOtherWins: 若锁失效的后果只是重复做一点幂等工作（如重复刷新缓存、重复预热一个可再生结果），Redis 锁完全够用，不必引入 ZooKeeper 的复杂度。
options_en: Just extend the TTL to ten minutes
Adding Redlock makes it foolproof
Treat the Redis lock as the foundation of correctness
Treat a Redis lock as an efficiency tool; enforce correctness with data-layer constraints or a consensus system
tradeoff: Redis 锁的效率 vs 数据层/共识系统的正确性保证
codeSample:
SET lock:order:123 worker-A NX PX 30000

# Unsafe after the lock expires:
UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid' WHERE id = 123;

# Source of truth checks state/token.
UPDATE orders
SET status = 'paid', fencing_token = :token
WHERE id = 123 AND status = 'reserved'
  AND :token > fencing_token;
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant R as Redis
  participant B as Worker B
  participant DB as Database
  A->>R: SET lock NX PX 30s succeeds
  Note over A: pause / GC / slow API for 45s
  Note over R: lock expires
  B->>R: SET lock NX PX succeeds
  B->>DB: write correct new state
  A->>DB: wakes up and writes stale state
  Note over DB: Redis cannot block this write unless DB checks version/token

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 锁：用 Redis 里的一个 key 表示某个资源暂时被占用，常见写法是 SET lock:resource requestId NX PX ttl。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis lock uses a Redis key to represent temporary ownership of a resource, commonly SET lock:resource requestId NX PX ttl.

termDefinitions.meaning: 过期锁持有者：曾经拿到锁、但锁的 TTL 已经过期的进程；它本地可能还以为自己有资格继续写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An expired lock holder is a process that once acquired the lock but whose TTL has expired; locally it may still believe it can keep writing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 资损：钱、库存、订单状态等业务资产被错误扣减、重复扣减或错误覆盖造成的损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Financial loss means business assets such as money, inventory, or order state are incorrectly decremented, duplicated, or overwritten.

termDefinitions.meaning: invariant：系统必须永远成立的业务规则，例如一张票只能卖一次、一笔订单只能扣款一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a business rule that must always hold, such as one ticket can be sold once or one order can be charged once.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper：基于共识协议的分布式协调服务，可提供强一致的锁语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-based distributed coordination service that can provide strongly consistent locking.

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd：另一个基于 Raft 共识的分布式键值存储，常用来做强一致协调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a Raft-based distributed key-value store commonly used for strongly consistent coordination.

q_en: What's the right attitude to take?
scenario_en: The same ticket, order, or driver dispatch must be handled by only one worker at a time. A Redis lock is usually a TTL key such as SET lock:order:123 worker-A NX PX 30000; A getting the lock means other workers should not process order:123 for 30 seconds. But the lock lives in Redis, while real business data often lives in MySQL, DynamoDB, S3, or an external payment system. Lock expiry does not automatically stop A's code or block A from writing downstream.
optionExplanations: 错：TTL 再长也只是降低过期概率，不能消除卡顿/GC 让旧持有者继续写下游的可能性。
错：Redlock 只解决「多数节点上是否拿到锁」，挡不住租约过期后旧持有者醒来继续写，不是万无一失。
错：把 Redis 锁当正确性基石正是要避免的误区——锁过期不会让代码自动停下来，也不会阻止继续写下游。
对：Redis 锁的作用只是降低并发冲突、提升效率；真要保证不写错，还得靠下游存储自己拒绝掉过时的写入。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a longer TTL only lowers the odds of lapsing early — it can't eliminate a stall letting a stale holder keep writing.
Wrong: Redlock only settles whether a majority of nodes granted the lock — it can't stop a stale holder from still writing after the lease ends.
Wrong: treating a Redis lock as the correctness foundation is exactly the trap — expiry doesn't stop the holder's code.
Right: a Redis lock only reduces concurrency as an efficiency optimization; real correctness comes from downstream conditional writes, version checks, or fencing tokens.

q: 把「Redis 分布式锁」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 代价：failover 或锁过期后，互斥可能被打破
需求：多台服务器并发时，同一资源同时只能一个进程操作
缓解：fencing token，或把不变量放回数据库层强制
选型：Redis SET NX EX——共享、原子、自动过期
why: 需求→选型→代价→缓解：说清楚锁为什么会失效、失效后怎么兜底，才是面试想听的完整回答。
why_en: The chain runs requirement, choice, cost, mitigation: atomic SET NX EX gives mutual exclusion that can break on failover, so back it with fencing or database constraints.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["SET NX EX token"] --> B["Do work"]
  B --> C["Lua compare token"]
  C --> D["DEL only owner"]
q_en: Put the decision chain for a Redis distributed lock in the correct order:

scenario: 关键词帖子榜（搜索 tiger 时按点赞数出 Top 帖）：更新频繁、读延迟要低，这个量级下 SQL 开始吃力。
q: 最合适的 Redis 结构是？
options: Sorted Set：member = 帖子 ID，score = 点赞数
List，靠每次在头部做插入维持顺序
Hash 存 {帖子: 点赞数} 的映射，没有内建排序
Set 存帖子 ID，排序逻辑全靠客户端自己实现
why: 有序集合按 score 维持排序，更新和按名次查询都是对数时间，高写吞吐 + 低读延迟正好接住 SQL 撑不动的规模。
why_en: A sorted set keeps members ordered by score with log-time updates and range queries, a natural leaderboard at scale.
whenOtherWins: 数据量小、读榜不频繁时 SQL 表 ORDER BY 完全够用——别为几千行数据引入新组件。
options_en: A sorted set with the post ID as member and like count as score
A list, keeping order by always inserting at the head
A hash storing a post-to-like-count mapping with no built-in ordering
A set of post IDs, with all sorting logic implemented on the client
tradeoff: 有序集合的对数级排序查询 vs 客户端自排序的线性开销
q_en: What's the most suitable Redis structure?
scenario_en: A keyword post leaderboard (searching "tiger" returns the top posts by like count) updates frequently and needs low read latency, at a scale where SQL starts to struggle.
optionExplanations: 对：分数一变，有序集合自己就把顺序调好了，更新和查名次都是对数级开销，正好扛住这种高频更新又要快速读排名的场景。
点赞数一变名次就要挪位，靠 List 头部插入维持顺序做不到按分数排序，只适合纯时间顺序的场景，不是本题。
Hash 能存「帖子→点赞数」的映射，但取 Top N 得自己把全部取出来再排序，量大了就是本题要避开的瓶颈。
Set 只能判断成员在不在、不带分数，把排序逻辑丢给客户端等于放弃了 Redis 原生的排行榜能力，不划算。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a sorted set auto-maintains order by score, so updates and rank queries are both log-time — fits high-write, low-latency leaderboards.
As likes change, rank has to shift — head inserts on a List only keep chronological order, not score-based ranking; not this case.
A Hash can store the post-to-like-count map, but getting the Top N means pulling everything out to sort client-side — the bottleneck to avoid.
A Set can only tell you membership, no score — pushing ordering to the client throws away Redis's native leaderboard capability.

scenario: tiger_posts 是 sorted set：member=postId，score=点赞数。现在有 7 条帖子，但只想保留点赞最高的 5 条，其余定期清掉省内存。
q: 哪条命令正确？
options: ZPOPMIN tiger_posts 5
DEL tiger_posts
ZREMRANGEBYRANK tiger_posts 0 -6
ZREMRANGEBYSCORE tiger_posts 0 5
why: rank 0 是最低分，-1 是最高分；`0 -6` 表示删掉最低分到“倒数第六名”，因此只留下最后 5 个最高分成员。
why_en: Rank 0 is the lowest score and -1 is the highest. The range 0 to -6 removes the low end through the sixth-from-top member, leaving the final five highest-score members.
whenOtherWins: 已知具体成员名时用 ZREM；要删整个榜单用 DEL；要取出并处理最低分成员用 ZPOPMIN；要按分数阈值删除才用 ZREMRANGEBYSCORE。
codeSample:
ZADD tiger_posts 10 p1 20 p2 30 p3 40 p4 50 p5 60 p6 70 p7
ZRANGE tiger_posts 0 -1 WITHSCORES
# p1 10 ... p7 70  (low score -> high score)

ZREMRANGEBYRANK tiger_posts 0 -6
# remove p1 and p2; keep p3..p7 = Top 5

ZREM tiger_posts p7            # remove this exact member
ZPOPMIN tiger_posts 1          # remove and return current lowest member
ZREMRANGEBYSCORE tiger_posts 0 30  # remove members with score 0..30
DEL tiger_posts                # delete the whole sorted set key
options_en: ZPOPMIN tiger_posts 5
DEL tiger_posts
ZREMRANGEBYRANK tiger_posts 0 -6
ZREMRANGEBYSCORE tiger_posts 0 5
tradeoff: 按名次裁剪集合 vs 弹出并处理最低分成员

termDefinitions.meaning: DEL：删除整个 key；用在这里会把 tiger_posts 榜单整体删掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DEL deletes the entire key; here it would remove the whole tiger_posts leaderboard.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZREM：按 member 名字删除指定成员，例如 ZREM tiger_posts p7。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZREM removes specific members by name, for example ZREM tiger_posts p7.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZREMRANGEBYRANK：按名次区间删除有序集合里的成员，负数从最高分端往回数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZREMRANGEBYRANK deletes sorted-set members within a rank range, where negative indexes count back from the highest score.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZPOPMIN：弹出并返回有序集合里分数最低的成员。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZPOPMIN pops and returns the member with the lowest score in a sorted set.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE：按分数区间删除有序集合里的成员，而不是按名次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE deletes sorted-set members within a score range instead of a rank range.

q_en: Which command is correct?
scenario_en: tiger_posts is a sorted set: member is postId and score is like count. It currently has 7 posts, but you only want to keep the 5 highest-liked posts and periodically trim the rest.
optionExplanations: 错：ZPOPMIN 弹出的是分数最低的成员，5 会把点赞最少的 5 条删掉，正好删反了，留下的反而是低分。
错：DEL 直接删掉整个 sorted set，连要保留的 Top 5 也一起没了，不是「清理多余」的操作。
对：rank 0 是最低分、-1 是最高分，`0 -6` 删掉最低分到倒数第六名（7 条里的最低 2 条），刚好留下点赞最高的 5 条。
错：ZREMRANGEBYSCORE 是按分数区间删除，`0 5` 删的是点赞数在 0-5 分之间的成员，跟「只留 Top 5」的排名逻辑对不上。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: ZPOPMIN pops the lowest-scoring members; popping 5 removes the least-liked posts — the opposite of what's needed.
Wrong: DEL wipes the entire sorted set, taking the top 5 you want to keep with it — not a 'trim the extras' operation.
Right: rank 0 is lowest score, -1 is highest; `0 -6` removes ranks from lowest through 6th-from-top (the bottom 2 of 7), leaving the top 5.
Wrong: ZREMRANGEBYSCORE deletes by a score range; `0 5` removes members with 0-5 likes, not what 'keep only the top 5 by rank' needs.

q: 对有序集合里已存在的成员再次 ZADD，会发生什么？
options: 命令直接报错
追加一个重复的成员
静默忽略这次写入
用新分数覆盖旧分数，成员名次随之移动
why: ZADD 是设置 member 的 score，不是追加一条记录；member 已存在时覆盖旧分数，有序集合会按新分数重新排位。
why_en: ZADD sets a member's score rather than appending a row, so an existing member's score is replaced and its rank moves.
options_en: The command errors out
It appends a duplicate member
The write is silently ignored
It overwrites the old score with the new one, moving the member's rank
codeSample:
ZADD tiger_posts 500 postA   # 首次写入，score=500
ZADD tiger_posts 800 postA   # 已存在，score 更新为 800

termDefinitions.meaning: ZADD 是 Redis Sorted Set 的写命令：给 member 设置 score，并按 score 维护排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZADD is the Redis Sorted Set command that assigns a score to a member and keeps the set ordered by score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有序集合：member 唯一，每个 member 带一个 score，Redis 按 score 做排名和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set stores unique members with scores, letting Redis rank them and query score ranges.

q_en: What happens when you ZADD a member that already exists in a sorted set?
optionExplanations: 错：对已存在成员再 ZADD 不会报错，这是有序集合支持的正常更新操作。
错：有序集合的 member 是唯一的，不会因为再次 ZADD 就出现重复成员。
错：这次写入不会被静默忽略，score 会真的被更新，只是很多人误以为「已存在就不生效」。
对：这条命令本质是「把分数设成这个值」：成员本来就在的话，旧分数直接被新的换掉，排名跟着新点赞数自动挪位。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: ZADD on an existing member doesn't error — updating it is a normal, supported operation for sorted sets.
Wrong: sorted-set members are unique; re-running ZADD doesn't create a duplicate entry.
Wrong: the write isn't silently ignored — the score really does update; a common misconception is that it's a no-op.
Right: ZADD's semantics are 'set the score' — an existing member gets its score replaced, and its rank moves with it.

scenario: 对每个 API key 做固定窗口限流：窗口内最多 N 次请求，超出返回 429 并带 Retry-After 头。
q: 最直接的 Redis 实现是？
options: 每次请求 LPUSH 进列表再 LLEN 计数
用 Pub/Sub 广播请求计数
GET 读出当前值再 SET 回去
对当前窗口的计数 key 执行 INCR，超过 N 就拒绝
why: INCR 原子地自增并返回新值，一条命令完成「计数 + 读数」；配合窗口过期就是固定窗口限流器。
why_en: INCR atomically increments and returns the window's counter, and rejecting when it exceeds N implements a fixed-window limiter.
whenOtherWins: 固定窗口在窗口边界可能被打出双倍突刺；要平滑限速就改用有序集合做滑动窗口。
options_en: LPUSH into a list on every request, then LLEN to count
Broadcast request counts over Pub/Sub
GET the current value, then SET it back
INCR the current window's counter key and reject once it exceeds N
tradeoff: INCR 原子自增 vs GET-then-SET 的竞态窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: INCR：原子地把整数 key 加一并返回新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR atomically increments an integer key and returns the new value.

termDefinitions.meaning: EXPIRE：给 key 设置过期时间，到点后 Redis 自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EXPIRE sets a timeout on a key so Redis deletes it later.

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL：key 距离自动过期还剩多久。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the remaining time before a key expires automatically.

q_en: What's the most direct Redis implementation?
scenario_en: You're rate-limiting each API key with a fixed window: at most N requests per window, returning 429 with a Retry-After header once exceeded.
codeSample:
# Fixed-window key, e.g. one API key per minute.
INCR rate:api-key-42:2026-07-09T12:00
EXPIRE rate:api-key-42:2026-07-09T12:00 60
TTL rate:api-key-42:2026-07-09T12:00

# Reject when the INCR result is greater than N.
optionExplanations: 错：LPUSH 每次都往列表写一整条记录再 LLEN 计数，既浪费内存又比直接自增慢，不是本题要的轻量计数。
错：Pub/Sub 是广播通知机制，不持久计数、也不保证送达，用它数请求次数既不准也不该这么用。
错：GET 再 SET 是两条独立命令，并发请求之间可能读到同一个旧值再各自 +1 覆盖，计数会算少。
对：这条命令一步到位——原子加一并把新值吐回来，配上给这个 key 设过期时间，就是一个现成的固定窗口限流器。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: LPUSH writes a whole new list entry per request just to LLEN-count it — wasteful and slower than a plain increment.
Wrong: Pub/Sub is a broadcast/notify mechanism, not durable counting with delivery guarantees — the wrong tool for this.
Wrong: GET-then-SET is two separate commands — concurrent requests can read the same stale value and each overwrite it, undercounting.
Right: INCR atomically increments and returns the new value in one command; paired with window expiry it's a fixed-window limiter.

scenario: 固定窗口限流：rate:user:42 记录当前 60 秒窗口内的请求数。每个请求都要 INCR 计数，但窗口结束时间应该由第一次请求决定。
scenario_en: Fixed-window rate limiting: rate:user:42 stores the request count for the current 60-second window. Every request increments the counter, but the window's end time should be set by the first request.
q: 限流计数器如果每次请求都调用 EXPIRE，会出什么问题？
options: 持续的请求流不断把过期时间往后推，窗口永远得不到重置
持续调用 EXPIRE 会在 Redis 里造成内存泄漏
会让计数器的过期时间意外变得太快
调用 EXPIRE 会把计数器的值意外清零
why: 每次续期等于把窗口终点不停往后挪；正确做法是只在 INCR 返回 1（窗口的第一个请求）时设置过期。
why_en: Calling EXPIRE on every request keeps pushing the reset forward so a steady stream never gets a fresh window; set it only when INCR returns one.
codeSample:
# Wrong: every request extends the window.
INCR rate:user:42
EXPIRE rate:user:42 60

# Right shape: every request INCRs, only the first request sets TTL.
EVAL "local n=redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1]); if n==1 then redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]); end; return n" 1 rate:user:42 60

termDefinitions.meaning: INCR：原子地把整数 key 加一，并返回加完后的值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR atomically increments an integer key and returns the new value.

termDefinitions.meaning: EXPIRE：现在给 key 设置 TTL；再次调用会重设倒计时，除非使用额外选项限制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EXPIRE sets a TTL on a key now; calling it again resets the countdown unless extra options prevent that.

termDefinitions.meaning: fixed window：固定窗口限流中，窗口从第一次请求开始，到 TTL 到期结束；不能被后续请求不断续期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fixed window starts with the first request and ends when its TTL expires; later requests should not keep extending it.

options_en: A steady stream of requests keeps pushing the reset forward, so the window never refreshes
Repeatedly calling EXPIRE causes a memory leak inside Redis
It makes the counter's expiry unexpectedly trigger too soon
Calling EXPIRE unexpectedly resets the counter's value to zero
q_en: What goes wrong if a rate limiter calls EXPIRE on every single request?
optionExplanations: 对：每来一次请求就续一次命，窗口的终点被不断往后拖，只要流量不断，这扇窗户就永远关不上。
错：反复设置过期时间不会造成内存泄漏，key 只有一个，问题在于「谁决定窗口何时结束」用错了逻辑。
错：不是过期时间变得太快，恰恰相反——它被不断往后推迟，导致窗口迟迟不结束。
错：设置过期时间只影响 TTL，不会把计数器的值清零，清零只会发生在 key 真正过期删除之后。
optionExplanations_en: Right: renewing on every request keeps pushing the window's end further out, so it never naturally lapses and resets.
Wrong: repeatedly setting a TTL doesn't leak memory — there's still just one key; the bug is which event gets to decide when the window ends.
Wrong: it's not that the TTL runs out too fast — the opposite: it keeps getting pushed later, so the window never actually ends.
Wrong: setting a TTL only affects when the key disappears; it doesn't zero the counter's value.

scenario: 简单 60 秒窗口限流：每个用户 60 秒内最多 100 次请求。服务端用 rate:user:42 这个 key 记录当前窗口的请求数；窗口是否重置，完全靠这个 key 的 TTL 到期后自动删除。第一个请求要 INCR 计数，并立刻给 key 设置 60 秒过期时间。
scenario_en: Simple 60-second-window rate limiting: each user can make at most 100 requests per 60 seconds. The service stores the current window's request count in rate:user:42, and the window resets only when the key's TTL expires and Redis deletes it. The first request increments the counter and immediately sets a 60-second expiration on the key.
q: INCR 和 EXPIRE 作为两条独立命令发送，进程恰好崩在两者之间的后果是？
options: 计数器会少加一次
留下一个永不过期的计数器，这个窗口永远不会重置
没有任何实际影响
Redis 会自动回滚那次 INCR
why: EXPIRE 是立刻给 key 装 TTL。若 INCR 成功后进程在 EXPIRE 前崩溃，计数 key 会永久保留；把 INCR 和首次 EXPIRE 放进 Lua 脚本，避免计数和 TTL 断在中间。
why_en: If the process crashes after INCR but before EXPIRE, the counter keeps no TTL, so put the increment and first-expire logic in one Lua script.
options_en: The counter simply undercounts by one
It leaves a counter with no TTL, so that window never resets
There is no real impact at all
Redis automatically rolls back that INCR
tradeoff: 两条命令简单但有崩溃窗口 vs Lua 原子脚本更安全
codeSample:
# Unsafe two-command version.
INCR rate:user:42        # returns 1, key now exists
# process crashes here before EXPIRE
EXPIRE rate:user:42 60   # this command never reaches Redis

# Check the bug:
TTL rate:user:42         # returns -1 = key exists but has no expiry

# Safer Lua version: set TTL only when the counter is first created.
EVAL "local n = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1]); if n == 1 then redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]); end; return n" 1 rate:user:42 60
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App as App process
  participant R as Redis
  App->>R: INCR rate:user:42
  R-->>App: 1
  Note over App: crash before EXPIRE
  App-xR: EXPIRE rate:user:42 60 never sent
  Note over R: key has value 1 but no TTL
  App->>R: TTL rate:user:42
  R-->>App: -1

termDefinitions.meaning: EXPIRE：给一个已有 key 设置过期时间，例如 EXPIRE counter 60 表示 60 秒后自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EXPIRE sets a timeout on an existing key, for example EXPIRE counter 60 deletes it automatically after 60 seconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL：key 还剩多久过期；TTL 返回 -1 表示 key 存在但没有过期时间，-2 表示 key 不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the remaining time before a key expires; TTL returns -1 when the key exists without expiry, and -2 when the key does not exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lua 脚本：Redis 会把脚本里的多条命令作为一个原子单元执行，中间不会被其他客户端命令插入，也不会只执行后一半。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script lets Redis execute multiple commands as one atomic unit, without interleaving other clients' commands in the middle.

q_en: If INCR and EXPIRE are sent as two separate commands and the process crashes right between them, what's the consequence?
optionExplanations: 错：崩溃发生在 EXPIRE 之前，INCR 已经成功执行并生效，计数不会少加，问题出在没设上 TTL。
对：给 key 装上 TTL 是单独的一条命令；如果 INCR 先成功、进程却在下一条命令前就崩了，这个计数 key 就再也没人给它设过期，永远留在那儿。
错：没有 TTL 意味着这个 key 会一直占用内存、计数一直累加下去，绝不是「没有实际影响」。
错：Redis 不会因为后续命令没执行就自动回滚前一条已经成功的命令，INCR 的效果会保留下来。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the crash happens before the TTL command runs; INCR already succeeded, so the count isn't undercounted — the bug is the missing TTL.
Right: setting the TTL is a separate command; if the process crashes after INCR succeeds but before that runs, the counter key sticks around forever and the window never resets.
Wrong: no TTL means the key keeps occupying memory and the count keeps climbing forever — that's very much a real effect.
Wrong: Redis doesn't roll back an already-successful command just because a later one never ran.

why: 有序集合按时间戳存请求，三步「清旧、计数、记新」构成滑动窗口；Lua 保证并发下不会超发。

scenario: 「找我附近 5 公里内的司机」：司机位置频繁更新，查询按坐标 + 半径。
q: 哪组 Redis 命令直接支持这个需求？
options: SETRANGE 改字符串局部片段 + SCAN 遍历全部 key 逐个比对
GEOADD 写入位置；GEOSEARCH FROMLONLAT ... BYRADIUS 按半径查
ZRANGEBYLEX 按字典序区间查询有序集合成员
SINTERCARD 只返回多个集合交集大小，不返回位置信息
why: Redis 原生地理索引：GEOADD 存经纬度、GEOSEARCH 按圆心和半径查询，不需要自己造网格。
why_en: GEOADD stores coordinates and GEOSEARCH queries by center and radius using Redis's native geospatial index.
whenOtherWins: 需要地理围栏、多边形查询或和业务数据 join 时，PostGIS 这类专业地理库更合适。
codeSample:
GEOADD drivers -122.42 37.77 driver:42
GEOSEARCH drivers FROMLONLAT -122.42 37.77 BYRADIUS 5 km ASC
options_en: SETRANGE to patch a string fragment plus SCAN to walk every key and compare manually
GEOADD to write locations; GEOSEARCH FROMLONLAT ... BYRADIUS to query by radius
ZRANGEBYLEX, querying a sorted set's members by lexicographic range
SINTERCARD, returning only the intersection size of several sets, no location data
tradeoff: 内置地理索引的开箱即用 vs 自建网格索引的开发成本

termDefinitions.meaning: GEOADD：把经纬度坐标写入 Redis 的地理空间索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GEOADD writes a longitude-latitude coordinate into a Redis geospatial index.

termDefinitions.meaning: GEOSEARCH：按圆心和半径（或矩形）查询地理空间索引里的成员。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GEOSEARCH queries a geospatial index for members within a radius or box around a point.

termDefinitions.meaning: SINTERCARD：只返回多个集合交集的大小，不返回具体成员。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SINTERCARD returns only the size of the intersection of several sets, not the members.

q_en: Which pair of Redis commands directly supports this requirement?
scenario_en: "Find drivers within 5 km of me": driver locations update frequently, and queries are by coordinate plus radius.
optionExplanations: 错：SETRANGE 改的是字符串片段，SCAN 遍历全部 key 逐个比对坐标，既没有空间索引也没法按半径高效查询。
对：GEOADD 把经纬度写进原生地理索引，GEOSEARCH FROMLONLAT ... BYRADIUS 直接按圆心和半径查，是这个需求的原生支持。
错：ZRANGEBYLEX 按字典序区间查有序集合成员，不理解经纬度和距离，回答不了「5 公里内」这种空间查询。
错：SINTERCARD 只返回多个集合交集的大小，不返回任何位置信息，跟找附近司机的需求对不上。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: SETRANGE edits a string slice and SCAN walks every key comparing coordinates — no spatial index, no efficient radius query.
Right: GEOADD writes coordinates into Redis's native geo index, and GEOSEARCH FROMLONLAT ... BYRADIUS queries directly by center and radius.
Wrong: ZRANGEBYLEX queries sorted-set members by lexicographic range — it has no notion of coordinates or distance.
Wrong: SINTERCARD only returns the size of a set intersection, no position data at all — doesn't fit finding nearby drivers.

q: Redis 地理索引的底层实现是？
options: 按外接矩形层层嵌套组织的 R-tree 空间索引
递归四等分平面区域的四叉树（quadtree）
geohash：经纬度编码成一个可排序的值，存进 sorted set
把平面均匀切分成固定大小格子的网格表
why: Redis GEO 把经纬度编码成 geohash-like score，存进一个 sorted set。它会用 box/radius 找候选，但底层不是 R-tree、quadtree 或 cell bucket 表。
why_en: Redis GEO encodes coordinates into a geohash-like sorted-set score; it may search boxes or radii, but it is not stored as an R-tree, quadtree, or grid table.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["lon,lat"] --> H["encode to geohash-like score"] H --> Z["Redis sorted set
member -> score"] Q["GEOSEARCH radius/box"] --> R["score-range candidate scan"] R --> F["exact distance filter"] Z --> R
options_en: An R-tree spatial index organized by nested bounding rectangles
A quadtree that recursively splits the plane into four quadrants
Geohash: latitude and longitude encoded into one sortable value stored in a sorted set
A grid table that uniformly divides the plane into fixed-size cells

termDefinitions.meaning: geohash 把经纬度交错编码成一维值；Redis 用类似思想生成 sorted set score。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash interleaves longitude and latitude into one-dimensional order; Redis uses a similar idea for the sorted-set score.

termDefinitions.meaning: R-tree：一种按外接矩形组织的空间索引树，Redis 地理索引并不用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree is a spatial index tree organized by bounding rectangles, which is not what Redis's geo index uses.

termDefinitions.meaning: quadtree 把二维平面递归四等分；它是常见地理索引思路，但不是 Redis GEO 的底层结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits a 2D plane into four quadrants; it is common for geo indexes, but not Redis GEO's underlying structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 有序集合，每个 member 对应一个 score，可按 score 范围查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set maps each member to a score and supports range queries by score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用把地图切成 cell，并维护 cellId 到点集合的映射；这是一种可自建的 geo 索引，不是 Redis GEO 的存储形态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fixed grid table maps each cellId to its points. It is a possible custom geo index, but not the storage shape of Redis GEO.

q_en: What's the underlying implementation of Redis's geospatial index?
optionExplanations: 错：R-tree 是按外接矩形层层嵌套的空间索引结构，不是 Redis GEO 的底层实现。
错：四叉树是递归四等分平面区域的结构，Redis GEO 用的不是这一套。
对：底层做法是把经纬度算成一个可排序的类 geohash 数值，直接塞进一个有序集合里，借用它本来就有的排序能力。
错：把平面切成固定大小格子的网格表也不是这里用的方案，真正的底层数据结构其实就是一个 sorted set。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an R-tree is a nested-bounding-box spatial index — not what Redis GEO uses under the hood.
Wrong: a quadtree recursively splits the plane into quarters — not Redis GEO's implementation either.
Right: Redis GEO encodes lat/lon into a sortable geohash-like score and stores it directly in a sorted set.
Wrong: a fixed-size grid cell table isn't Redis GEO's underlying structure — the actual backing structure is a plain sorted set.

q: GEOSEARCH 复杂度 O(N + log M) 里为什么同时出现 N（包围盒内候选数）和 M（半径内命中数）？
options: 两遍过滤：先取网格对齐包围盒里的 N 个候选，再精确筛出半径内的 M 个
因为底层排序算法本身需要跑完整两趟
N 其实指的是 Redis 集群里的节点数量
这是文档笔误，N 和 M 其实是同一个数
why: geohash 的盒子是方形、网格对齐的，无法精确贴合圆形半径，所以先粗筛候选、再逐个精确算距离。
why_en: Geohash boxes are grid-aligned squares, so a first pass grabs candidates inside the boxes and a second pass filters to those within the exact radius.
options_en: Two passes: grab N candidates inside grid-aligned boxes, then precisely filter to the M within radius
Because the underlying sort algorithm itself needs two full passes
N actually refers to the number of nodes in the Redis cluster
It's a documentation typo, and N and M are actually the same number
q_en: Why does GEOSEARCH's O(N + log M) complexity involve both N (candidates in the bounding box) and M (hits within the radius)?
optionExplanations: 对：编码出来的格子是方的、对齐网格的，圆形的搜索半径根本套不进去，所以得先粗筛出一批候选，再挨个精确算距离挑出真正命中的。
错：跑两趟不是排序算法本身的要求，是「先粗筛候选、再精确过滤」这个两阶段查询策略带来的开销。
错：N 指的是包围盒内的候选成员数，跟集群里有多少个节点没有关系。
错：N 和 M 分别对应两个不同阶段筛出的数量（候选数 vs 命中数），不是同一个数，也不是笔误。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a geohash box is square and grid-aligned, so it can't exactly match a circular radius — first coarse-filter N candidates, then precisely check distance for M hits.
Wrong: running two passes isn't a property of the sort algorithm — it comes from the two-stage coarse-then-precise filtering strategy.
Wrong: N refers to candidate members inside the bounding box, unrelated to how many nodes are in the cluster.
Wrong: N and M come from two different filtering stages (candidates vs actual hits) — not the same number, and not a typo.

q: Redis Stream 的本质是？
options: 追加写日志（append-only log），类似 Kafka 的 topic
一个固定大小、写满就自动覆盖旧数据的环形缓冲区
一个按分数排序、支持弹出最小值成员的优先队列
一个不保留任何状态、消息即发即失的广播信道
why: Stream 是追加日志：配合消费组可以做事件溯源和工作队列，是 Redis 里最接近 Kafka 的原语。
why_en: A Redis stream is an append-only log similar to a Kafka topic, and consumer groups coordinate who processes what.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["XADD"] --> B["Stream log"]
  B --> C["Consumer group"]
  C --> D["ACK or pending"]
options_en: An append-only log, similar to a Kafka topic
A fixed-size ring buffer that automatically overwrites old data once full
A score-ordered priority queue that supports popping the lowest-score member
A stateless broadcast channel where messages fire and are gone

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：Apache Kafka，一个支持长期保留、多消费者重放的分布式日志系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is Apache Kafka, a distributed log system built for long retention and replay by many independent consumers.

q_en: What is a Redis Stream, fundamentally?
optionExplanations: 对：它本质是一份只增不减的日志，跟消费组搭配能当事件溯源或任务队列用，是 Redis 里长得最像 Kafka topic 的东西。
错：Stream 不是写满就自动覆盖旧数据的环形缓冲区，它靠 XADD 持续追加，要清理得显式 XTRIM/裁剪。
错：按分数排序、弹出最小值是 sorted set 的能力，Stream 靠 ID 顺序追加，不是分数排序。
错：不留状态、即发即失是 Pub/Sub 的特征，Stream 恰恰相反——它持久保留条目，能被后来的消费者读取历史。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Stream is an append-only log; paired with consumer groups it supports event sourcing and job queues — closest to a Kafka topic.
Wrong: Stream isn't a fixed-size ring buffer that auto-overwrites old data — XADD keeps appending, and trimming needs explicit XTRIM.
Wrong: score-ordered pop-the-minimum describes a sorted set; Stream appends by ID order, not by score.
Wrong: no retained state and fire-and-forget describes Pub/Sub — Stream durably keeps entries so later consumers can read history.

q: 补全 Stream 工作队列的命令分工：
text: 生产者用 {{XADD}} 追加条目；工作者通过消费组用 {{XREADGROUP}} 领取条目；超时未确认的条目可被其他工作者用 {{XCLAIM}}（或 XAUTOCLAIM）抢过来重做。
why: 工作队列链路是：XADD 入流，XREADGROUP 分给 worker，成功后 XACK；没 XACK 会留在 PEL，超时后用 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管。
why_en: The queue loop is XADD to append, XREADGROUP to deliver, XACK to finish, and XCLAIM or XAUTOCLAIM to recover idle pending entries.
codeSample:
XGROUP CREATE jobs workers $ MKSTREAM
XADD jobs * kind email user 42
XREADGROUP GROUP workers worker-1 COUNT 1 STREAMS jobs >
# worker-1 dies before XACK; entry stays in PEL
XCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 {entry-id}
XAUTOCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 0-0 COUNT 10
XACK jobs workers {entry-id}

termDefinitions.meaning: XADD：向 Stream 追加一条新记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XADD appends a new entry to a stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: XREADGROUP：消费组里的 worker 用它领取 Stream 里的新条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XREADGROUP is how a worker in a consumer group reads new entries from a stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: XCLAIM：把一个超时未确认的条目转交给另一个 worker 重新处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XCLAIM transfers a stalled, unacknowledged stream entry to another worker to reprocess.

termDefinitions.meaning: XAUTOCLAIM：从某个起点开始扫描，并批量接管 idle 超时的 pending 条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XAUTOCLAIM scans and claims pending stream entries that have been idle too long.

termDefinitions.meaning: XACK：worker 处理成功后确认条目，Redis 会把它从 PEL 中移除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK acknowledges a processed entry and removes it from the pending list.

termDefinitions.meaning: PEL：消费组记录已投递但还没 XACK 的条目，以及 owner 和 idle 时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The PEL tracks entries that were delivered to a consumer group but not yet acknowledged.

q: Redis Streams 工作队列里，worker 取到任务后崩溃，未确认任务如何恢复？
scenario: 生产者用 XADD 写入任务，worker 用 XREADGROUP 领取任务；只有处理成功并 XACK 后，这条任务才算完成。
options: 未 XACK 的任务永久丢失，不再恢复
Redis 自动重启崩溃 worker，再继续原任务
idle 超时后，用 XCLAIM 转给其他 worker 重做
主节点重新广播任务，让所有 worker 抢处理
why: 未 XACK 的条目会留在 PEL，记录 owner 和 idle。idle 超阈值后，其他 worker 用 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管并重做。
why_en: Unacknowledged stream entries stay in the PEL, so another worker can claim an idle entry with XCLAIM or XAUTOCLAIM and retry it.
tradeoff: 故障恢复与至少一次处理 vs 重复执行风险
whenOtherWins: 若任务不能重复执行，业务层要加去重键或状态机；Redis 重新交付，但不保证只执行一次。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P[Producer XADD] --> S[(Redis Stream)]
    S --> G[Consumer group]
    G --> W1[worker1 XREADGROUP]
    W1 --> PEL[PEL: delivered, not XACKed]
    W1 -. crashes .-> PEL
    PEL -- idle exceeds threshold --> W2[worker2 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM]
    W2 --> R[redo work]
    R --> A[XACK removes from PEL]

rows: 其他 worker 发现超时

options_en: The unacknowledged task is lost forever
Redis restarts the crashed worker and continues the task
After the idle timeout, XCLAIM moves it to another worker
The primary rebroadcasts the task to all workers

q_en: In a Redis Streams work queue, how does an unacknowledged task recover after the worker that claimed it crashes?
scenario_en: A producer writes tasks with XADD and workers claim them with XREADGROUP; a task only counts as done once it's processed successfully and XACKed.
optionExplanations: 错：未 XACK 的条目不会丢失，它会留在 PEL（pending entries list）里等着被接管，不是永久消失。
错：Redis 不会帮你重启崩溃的 worker 进程，它只负责保留和转交消息，恢复业务进程是运维/编排的事。
对：没确认的任务会挂在一个待处理列表里，谁领的、挂了多久都记着；等挂的时间超过阈值，别的 worker 就能把它接过去重做。
错：主节点不会重新广播让所有 worker 一起抢，消费组的分发和接管是按 PEL/idle 逐条精确转交，不是广播抢占。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an un-acked entry isn't lost — it stays in the pending entries list (PEL) waiting to be taken over, not gone forever.
Wrong: Redis doesn't restart a crashed worker process for you — it only retains and hands off messages.
Right: an un-acked entry sits in the PEL tracking its owner and idle time; past a threshold, another worker uses XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM to take it over.
Wrong: the primary doesn't rebroadcast for every worker to race for — handoff is a precise per-entry transfer based on PEL/idle.

q: XCLAIM 接管机制带来的副作用是？
options: 同一条目可能被处理两次——Redis 分不清「慢」和「死」，处理逻辑必须幂等
超时的条目会被 Redis 静默丢弃，不再投递
整个消费组的消费顺序会被完全打乱
接管机制强制一个消费组只能有一个 worker
why: 慢 worker 没死却被判超时的话，条目会被第二个 worker 重做——这是 at-least-once 语义，幂等是消费端的义务。
why_en: Redis cannot tell a slow worker from a dead one, so an entry can occasionally be processed twice and your handler must be idempotent.
options_en: An entry can be processed twice, since Redis cannot tell slow from dead, so handlers must be idempotent
A timed-out entry gets silently dropped by Redis and never redelivered
The entire consumer group's processing order gets completely scrambled
The takeover mechanism forces a consumer group to have only one worker

termDefinitions.meaning: XCLAIM：把 pending 条目从一个消费者转交给另一个消费者重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XCLAIM transfers a pending stream entry to another consumer for retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: XACK：确认 Stream 条目处理完成，并把它从 PEL 中移除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK acknowledges a stream entry as processed and removes it from the PEL.

termDefinitions.meaning: PEL（Pending Entries List）：消费组里已投递但尚未 XACK 的条目列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The PEL is the pending entries list of messages delivered to a consumer group but not yet acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一个操作重复执行多次，结果和只执行一次一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means running the same operation multiple times produces the same result as running it once.

q_en: What side effect comes from the XCLAIM takeover mechanism?
codeSample:
# Worker A reads but does not XACK yet.
XREADGROUP GROUP g A COUNT 1 STREAMS jobs >
XPENDING jobs g

# After A is idle too long, B claims and retries.
XCLAIM jobs g B 60000 1710000000000-0
# If A was only slow, the job may run twice.
XACK jobs g 1710000000000-0
optionExplanations: 对：一个只是慢、并没真死的 worker 也可能被系统当成超时，任务就转给别人重做——这就是至少一次投递，业务逻辑得自己保证幂等。
错：超时的条目不会被静默丢弃，它会被 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管重做，而不是消失。
错：XCLAIM 只是把某条挂起条目的所有权转给另一个 worker，不会打乱整个消费组的处理顺序。
错：接管机制不限制消费组里的 worker 数量，多个 worker 并行消费本来就是消费组的设计初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a worker that's slow but not dead can get timed out anyway, and the entry gets redone by another worker — at-least-once; idempotency is the consumer's job.
Wrong: a timed-out entry isn't silently dropped — it gets taken over and redone via XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM.
Wrong: XCLAIM only transfers ownership of one pending entry to another worker — it doesn't scramble the group's order.
Wrong: the takeover mechanism doesn't cap a consumer group at one worker — parallel consumption is the whole point.

q: 把 Stream 当「可靠日志」用之前必须记住什么？
options: 条目的持久性只取决于你的 RDB/AOF 配置——默认下崩溃可能丢最近的条目
Stream 的写入总是同步落盘，绝不会丢失数据
Stream 会自动把条目复制一份镜像到 Kafka 集群
Stream 里写入的条目永远不可以被删除
why: Stream 再像日志，也逃不过 Redis 的持久化取舍：默认配置下崩溃丢最近写入——和页首的 durability 警告是同一件事。
why_en: Stream entries are only as durable as your persistence settings, so with defaults a crash can lose recent entries.
options_en: Entry durability depends entirely on your RDB/AOF settings, and a crash can lose recent entries under defaults
Stream writes are always synchronously flushed to disk and never lost
Streams automatically mirror a copy of every entry into a Kafka cluster
Once written, entries in a stream can never be deleted
q_en: What must you remember before treating a Stream as a 'reliable log'?
optionExplanations: 对：别看它长得像日志，落盘策略跟 Redis 其他数据一样受同一套取舍约束——默认配置崩溃照样会丢最近那批写入。
错：Stream 不会「总是同步落盘」，它的持久性仍受 RDB 快照间隔或 AOF fsync 频率约束，跟普通 key 一样有丢失窗口。
错：Redis 没有把 Stream 条目自动镜像到 Kafka 集群这种内建功能，这是要自己搭建的跨系统同步。
错：Stream 里的条目可以被删除——XDEL 删单条、XTRIM 按长度或时间裁剪，不是「永远不可删除」。
optionExplanations_en: Right: however log-like it looks, Stream still inherits Redis's persistence trade-offs — a crash under default config can lose the most recent entries.
Wrong: Stream isn't 'always synced to disk' — its durability still depends on RDB snapshot intervals or AOF fsync frequency.
Wrong: Redis has no built-in feature that auto-mirrors Stream entries to a Kafka cluster.
Wrong: entries in a Stream can be deleted — XDEL removes a single entry, XTRIM trims by length or time.

q: 什么时候该把 Redis Streams 换成 Kafka？
options: 只要队列规模比较小，就应该马上换掉
只要系统里已经部署了 Redis，就该顺便换掉
只要用到了消费组（consumer group）机制就该换
需要长期保留、多个独立消费者重放、以及一条都不能丢的持久有序吞吐时
why: Streams 适合已有 Redis、队列规模不大的场景（后台任务、通知扇出、工作分发）；长保留 + 重放 + 不可丢消息才值得付 Kafka 的运维成本。
why_en: Kafka earns its complexity when you need long retention, replay for many independent consumers, and durable ordered throughput where losing a message is unacceptable.
scenario: 你的设计已经在用 Redis Streams 做工作队列（后台任务、通知扇出），眼下数据量和独立消费者的数量都在持续增长。
options_en: You should switch the moment the queue is even moderately small
As soon as Redis happens to already be deployed in the system
As soon as you touch the consumer-group mechanism at all
When you need long retention, replay for many independent consumers, and durable ordered throughput where losing a message is unacceptable
tradeoff: 留在 Redis Streams 的低运维成本 vs 换 Kafka 换来的长保留与可靠重放
q_en: When should you switch from Redis Streams to Kafka?
scenario_en: Your design already uses Redis Streams as a work queue (background jobs, notification fan-out), and both data volume and the number of independent consumers keep growing.
optionExplanations: 错：规模小恰恰是 Streams 更划算的场景，为小队列换 Kafka 只是白白多背运维成本。
错：「已经在用 Redis」不是换 Kafka 的理由，选型要看队列本身的保留/重放/丢失要求，不是图省事。
错：消费组机制 Streams 自己就有（XREADGROUP），不是 Kafka 独有能力，用到消费组不构成换型理由。
对：一旦要求长期留存、好几拨互不相干的消费者各自从头重放、外加一条都不能少的可靠有序吞吐，这份额外的运维投入就值了。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a small queue is exactly where Streams pays off — switching to Kafka for it just adds ops overhead for nothing.
Wrong: 'we already run Redis' isn't a reason to switch — the choice should follow retention/replay/loss requirements, not convenience.
Wrong: consumer groups are a Streams feature too (XREADGROUP), not Kafka-exclusive — using one is no reason to switch.
Right: it's worth Kafka's operational cost once you need long retention, multiple independent consumers replaying history, and durable throughput that can't drop a message.

q: Pub/Sub 和 Streams 的分工，一句话是？
options: Pub/Sub 会把消息持久化落盘，Streams 反而不落盘
Streams 服务「需要补课的消费者」；Pub/Sub 只投递给「此刻在线的听众」
两者的投递语义和可靠性完全等价，可以互换
Pub/Sub 天生持久可靠，更适合做工作队列
why: Streams 有历史可回读；Pub/Sub 即发即失、离线就错过——按「消费者要不要追赶历史」来选。
why_en: Streams serve consumers that must catch up on missed entries, while Pub/Sub only delivers to whoever is listening right now.
options_en: Pub/Sub persists messages to disk while Streams, oddly, does not
Streams serve consumers who need to catch up on history; Pub/Sub only delivers to whoever is listening right now
The two have fully equivalent delivery semantics and reliability, interchangeably
Pub/Sub is inherently durable and reliable, making it the better fit for work queues
tradeoff: Streams 的可回读历史 vs Pub/Sub 的即发即失
q_en: In one line, how do Pub/Sub and Streams divide responsibilities?
optionExplanations: 错：说反了——Pub/Sub 不落盘、即发即失；Streams 才有持久的历史条目可以回读。
对：一个能让消费者回头补看历史，服务的是「需要补课」的场景；另一个发出去就不管了，只送达「这一刻正在听」的人，按这个区别来分工。
错：两者投递语义差别很大——Streams 更接近 at-least-once 可回放，Pub/Sub 是 at-most-once，不能互换。
错：天生持久可靠、适合做工作队列描述的是 Streams，不是 Pub/Sub——Pub/Sub 没有持久化和重放能力。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that's backwards — Pub/Sub doesn't persist, it's fire-and-forget; Streams is the one with durable, replayable history.
Right: Streams keeps replayable history for 'consumers that need to catch up'; Pub/Sub only reaches 'listeners online right now' — pick by that need.
Wrong: their delivery semantics differ a lot — Streams is closer to at-least-once with replay, Pub/Sub is at-most-once.
Wrong: durable and reliable enough for a work queue describes Streams, not Pub/Sub — Pub/Sub has no persistence or replay.

q: Redis Pub/Sub 的投递语义是？
options: 恰好一次投递，Redis 会去重保证不重不漏
至少一次投递，离线消息会重试到送达为止
至多一次：订阅者离线期间发布的消息永久错过
带事务性保证的投递，要么全送达要么全不送
why: 消息不落盘、不可重放：连接断开或不在线就收不到，这就是 at-most-once。
why_en: Redis Pub/Sub is at-most-once delivery, so a subscriber offline at publish time misses the message entirely.
options_en: Exactly-once delivery, with Redis deduplicating so nothing repeats or is missed
At-least-once delivery, retrying offline messages until they land
At-most-once: a subscriber offline at publish time permanently misses the message
Transactional delivery guarantees where messages either all arrive or none do
q_en: What are Redis Pub/Sub's delivery semantics?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 不会去重也不保证恰好一次，Pub/Sub 甚至不保证消息一定能送到，比「恰好一次」弱得多。
错：离线不会有重试——消息不落盘，Redis 不会等订阅者上线后补投递，这不是 at-least-once。
对：消息压根不落盘也没法回放，断线或不在线就是彻底错过，投递上限就是「送到算送到，送不到也不补」。
错：Pub/Sub 没有跨订阅者的事务性保证，它是逐个投递给当前在线订阅者，不是「全送达或全不送」的原子操作。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis doesn't dedupe or guarantee exactly-once — Pub/Sub doesn't even guarantee delivery at all.
Wrong: there's no retry while offline — messages aren't persisted, so Redis won't hold them for a subscriber that comes back later.
Right: messages aren't persisted or replayable — disconnect or be offline and you miss it forever, which is at-most-once.
Wrong: Pub/Sub has no transactional guarantee across subscribers — it delivers to whoever's online individually.

scenario: 你听过一个老说法：Redis Cluster 里的 Pub/Sub 即使加节点也不加容量，因为消息会扩散到全体节点。现在团队准备用 Redis 7+，并且频道数很多、频道名能自然分散。
scenario_en: You have heard the old rule that Pub/Sub in Redis Cluster does not gain capacity when you add nodes because messages spread to every node. The team is now on Redis 7+ with many channels whose names can naturally spread across slots.
q: 「集群 Pub/Sub 加节点不加容量」这个老印象，现在的事实是？
options: 普通 Pub/Sub 仍全局传播；Redis 7+ 的 sharded 版才能按 shard 横向扩展
这个限制至今对所有 Pub/Sub 都成立，Redis 7+ 没有相关改变
只要给 Redis 加 replica，单个频道的发布吞吐就会自动分摊到所有副本
Pub/Sub 已经被 Streams 完全替代，后续 Redis 版本不能再用 Pub/Sub
why: Global Pub/Sub 仍跨节点传播，不能靠加节点扩。Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub 让频道按 slot 落到 shard；多频道可扩，单热频道仍卡单 shard。
why_en: Normal cluster Pub/Sub still propagates across nodes, while Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub routes channels by slot so many spread-out channels can scale, but one hot channel stays shard-bound.
whenOtherWins: 老版本、global/pattern 订阅、单热频道时，仍按“加节点不加容量”回答；新分片模式且频道分散时才说可扩。
options_en: Normal Pub/Sub is still globally propagated; Redis 7+'s sharded version can scale by shard
This limitation still applies to all Pub/Sub, and Redis 7+ made no related change
Adding Redis replicas automatically spreads one channel's publish throughput across all replicas
Pub/Sub has been fully replaced by Streams and cannot be used in later Redis versions
tradeoff: global Pub/Sub 的简单广播 vs sharded Pub/Sub 的可扩展但需按 shard 设计
codeSample:
# Normal/global Pub/Sub: simple, but cluster-wide propagation.
SUBSCRIBE orders.123
PUBLISH orders.123 msg

# Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub: channel hashes to a slot/shard.
SSUBSCRIBE orders.123
SPUBLISH orders.123 msg

# Spread many independent channels across slots/shards.
SPUBLISH chat:1001 msg
SPUBLISH chat:2042 msg

flowchart LR

  G --> N1["node A"]
  G --> N2["node B"]

termDefinitions.meaning: SPUBLISH：Redis 7+ 分片 Pub/Sub 的发布命令，消息按 shard channel 的 slot 路由，只在对应 shard 内传播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SPUBLISH is the Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub publish command; the message is routed by the shard channel's slot and propagated only within that shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSUBSCRIBE：Redis 7+ 分片 Pub/Sub 的订阅命令，订阅一个会像 key 一样哈希到 slot 的 shard channel。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSUBSCRIBE is the sharded Pub/Sub subscribe command, hashing the channel to a slot just like a key.

termDefinitions.meaning: global Pub/Sub：普通 PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE 的集群传播模式，简单但会跨节点传播消息，不适合靠加节点线性扩 Pub/Sub 总线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Global Pub/Sub is the normal PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE cluster propagation mode; it is simple but sends messages across nodes, so it is not linear capacity scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: shard channel：分片 Pub/Sub 的频道名，会按 Redis Cluster 的 slot 算法归属到某个 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard channel is a sharded Pub/Sub channel name that is assigned to a shard using Redis Cluster's slot algorithm.

q_en: The old assumption is 'adding cluster nodes doesn't add Pub/Sub capacity' — what's actually true now?
optionExplanations: 对：得分两种情况——普通的发布订阅照样是全网广播；新版本另外那套按 slot 分片的命令，才真正能把频道摊开到不同分片上扩容。
错：新版本已经加了按分片走的发布订阅，能把很多频道的压力摊到不同分片上，老说法不再对所有情况都成立。
错：单个频道的发布压力不会因为加了 replica 就自动分摊，副本只是复制数据，不参与分担某个频道的 fanout。
错：Pub/Sub 没有被 Streams 完全替代，两者语义不同（即发即失 vs 持久可回放），后续版本仍然可以用 Pub/Sub。
optionExplanations_en: Right: split it in two — plain PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE still broadcasts cluster-wide, while Redis 7+'s SPUBLISH/SSUBSCRIBE lets channels land on one shard and scale horizontally.
Wrong: Redis 7+ introduced sharded Pub/Sub, spreading fanout load for many channels across shards — the old limitation doesn't hold for all Pub/Sub now.
Wrong: adding replicas doesn't auto-spread one channel's publish load — replicas just copy data, they don't share in that fanout.
Wrong: Pub/Sub hasn't been fully replaced by Streams — they have different semantics, and Pub/Sub is still usable in later versions.

q: 使用一个 Pub/Sub 频道之前需要什么创建或配置步骤？
options: 执行 CREATE CHANNEL 命令
在 CONFIG SET 里注册频道
先创建一个 consumer group
什么都不用：有人发布或订阅这个名字，频道就存在了
why: 频道只是个名字：发布者往这个名字上发、订阅者在这个名字上听，不需要任何预先创建。
why_en: A channel is just a name that comes into existence when someone publishes or subscribes; there is nothing to create.
options_en: Run a CREATE CHANNEL command
Register the channel via CONFIG SET
First create a consumer group for it
Nothing: the channel exists the moment someone publishes or subscribes to that name
q_en: What setup or creation step do you need before using a Pub/Sub channel?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 没有 CREATE CHANNEL 这条命令，频道不需要任何显式创建步骤。
错：CONFIG SET 是配置服务器参数的命令，不是用来注册 Pub/Sub 频道的。
错：consumer group 是 Streams 的概念，Pub/Sub 频道不需要消费组，两者是不同的机制。
对：频道说白了就是一个约定好的字符串——谁发谁听全靠对上这个名字，压根不用先注册或声明。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis has no CREATE CHANNEL command — a channel needs no explicit creation step at all.
Wrong: CONFIG SET tunes server parameters; it isn't used to register a Pub/Sub channel.
Wrong: a consumer group is a Streams concept — a Pub/Sub channel doesn't need one.
Right: a channel is just a name — a publisher sends to it and a subscriber listens on it, with no pre-creation step.

scenario: 一台 Chat Server 要订阅很多 Redis sharded Pub/Sub 频道，例如 user:1、user:2、chat:abc 这类频道一共有 100 万个。每个频道名会像 key 一样 hash 到某个 slot，slot 再归属于某个 Redis shard。
q: 一台订阅了 100 万个频道的服务器，需要多少条到 Redis 的连接？
options: 为每个频道单独开一条独立的 TCP 连接，总共 100 万条
严格按每个频道一条连接来计算连接开销
每个持有相关槽位的节点一条——连接开销按节点算，不按频道算
至少要开 16,384 条连接，正好对应哈希槽的数量
why: 频道不是 TCP 连接；一条到某个 Redis shard 的长连接可以承载很多 SSUBSCRIBE。连接数按涉及的节点/shard 算，不按频道数算；但 100 万频道仍会产生订阅状态和 fanout 成本。
why_en: One TCP connection to a Redis shard can carry many SSUBSCRIBE channels, so connections scale with involved shards, while subscription state and fanout still scale with channels.
options_en: Open one dedicated TCP connection per channel, a million separate connections in total
Overhead is counted strictly at one connection per channel, regardless of node
One connection per node holding the relevant slots — the overhead scales with nodes, not channels
At least 16,384 connections, exactly matching the hash slot count
tradeoff: 少量长连接承载大量订阅 vs 每个频道仍有订阅状态和消息 fanout 成本
codeSample:
# One connection to shard/node A can carry many channel subscriptions.
SSUBSCRIBE user:1 user:27 user:8801
SSUBSCRIBE chat:abc chat:def

# A different shard needs a different Redis connection.
# But it is still one connection for many channels on that shard.
SSUBSCRIBE user:42 user:99 chat:west

# Mental model:
# connection_to_node_A.subscriptions = {user:1, user:27, user:8801, chat:abc, chat:def}
# connection_to_node_B.subscriptions = {user:42, user:99, chat:west}

flowchart LR
  CS["Chat Server"] -->|one TCP connection| A["Redis shard A"]
  CS -->|one TCP connection| B["Redis shard B"]
  CS -->|one TCP connection| C["Redis shard C"]
  A --> ASubs["many SSUBSCRIBE channels\nuser:1, user:27, chat:abc..."]
  B --> BSubs["many SSUBSCRIBE channels\nuser:42, user:99..."]
  C --> CSubs["many SSUBSCRIBE channels\nchat:west..."]

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 连接：客户端和 Redis 节点之间的一条长连接，可以承载很多条订阅命令和很多个频道的推送。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TCP connection is one long-lived connection between a client and a Redis node, and it can carry many subscription commands and channel messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: subscription state：Redis 记录某个连接订阅了哪些频道的内存状态；频道多会增加状态，但不等于连接多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Subscription state is Redis's in-memory record of which channels a connection subscribed to; more channels add state, not separate TCP connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: sharded Pub/Sub：Redis 7+ 的分片 Pub/Sub，频道按 slot 归属到 shard，消息只在该 shard 内传播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharded Pub/Sub is Redis 7+'s Pub/Sub mode where channels are assigned to slots/shards and messages propagate only inside the shard.

q_en: How many connections to Redis does a server subscribed to one million channels need?
scenario_en: A Chat Server needs to subscribe to many Redis sharded Pub/Sub channels, for example user:1, user:2, and chat:abc, totaling one million channels. Each channel name hashes to a slot like a key, and the slot belongs to a Redis shard.
optionExplanations: 错：一条连接可以承载很多个 SSUBSCRIBE，不需要为每个频道单独开一条 TCP 连接。
错：连接开销不是按频道数算的，而是按涉及的节点/shard 数算，100 万频道不等于 100 万条连接。
对：一个频道不等于一条连接；一条打到某个分片的长连接底下能挂很多订阅，真正花钱的是连了几个持槽节点，不是订阅了几个频道。
错：连接数跟哈希槽总数 16384 没有固定对应关系，一条连接同样能承载多个 shard 上分布的订阅。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: one connection can carry many SSUBSCRIBEs — you don't need a separate TCP connection per channel.
Wrong: connection overhead isn't billed per channel; it's billed per node/shard involved — 1M channels isn't 1M connections.
Right: a channel isn't a TCP connection; one long-lived connection to a shard can carry many SSUBSCRIBEs, and the cost scales with nodes holding relevant slots.
Wrong: connection count has no fixed relationship to the 16384 hash slots — one connection can carry subscriptions spread across shards.

scenario: 聊天系统用 Pub/Sub 做在线实时投递，但产品要求用户重新上线后能补看离线期间错过的消息。
q: 正确的补法是？
options: 只是把 Pub/Sub 内部的消息缓冲区调得更大一些而已
想尽各种办法保证客户端的连接永远都不会意外断开或掉线
把全部实时投递流程都直接改成客户端定时轮询查询
Pub/Sub 之外再落一份可回放存储：Streams、Kafka/SQS 或 outbox 表
why: Pub/Sub 只通知此刻在线的订阅者；离线补课要从持久化日志/队列或 Message+Inbox 表重读。outbox 表常用来保证「写消息」和「稍后发布事件」不丢。
why_en: Pub/Sub only notifies subscribers that are online right now; offline catch-up must read from a durable log/queue or Message+Inbox tables. An outbox table is often used to make 'write the message' and 'publish the event later' reliable.
whenOtherWins: 若消息只对「此刻在场」的人有意义（光标位置、正在输入提示），纯 Pub/Sub 反而是最省的正确答案；若已用 Kafka 做实时消费，也可以不用 Redis Pub/Sub。
options_en: Just make Pub/Sub's internal message buffer even bigger, nothing else
Find every possible way to guarantee client connections never accidentally drop or disconnect
Replace the entire real-time delivery flow directly with client-side timed polling
Pair Pub/Sub with a replayable store: Streams, Kafka or SQS, or an outbox table
tradeoff: Pub/Sub 的即时低延迟 vs 持久化补课路径的存储/重试成本
codeSample:
# One common chat write path: DB outbox + Pub/Sub notify.
sendMessage(chatId, senderId, body):
  tx.begin()
  msg = Messages.insert(chatId, senderId, body)
  for userId in Participants.of(chatId):
    Inbox.insert(userId=userId, msgId=msg.id, status="PENDING")
  Outbox.insert(type="MessageCreated", msgId=msg.id, chatId=chatId)
  tx.commit()

outboxRelayLoop():
  for event in Outbox.fetchUnsent(limit=100):
    redis.publish("chat:" + event.chatId, { "msgId": event.msgId })
    Outbox.markSent(event.id)

onReconnect(userId, lastSeenMsgId):
  return Inbox.query(userId=userId, after=lastSeenMsgId)

termDefinitions.meaning: Pub/Sub：发布者把消息发到频道，当前在线订阅者立即收到；Redis 不为离线订阅者保存历史。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub sends a message to a channel and current subscribers receive it immediately; Redis does not keep history for offline subscribers.

termDefinitions.meaning: Message/Inbox 表：Message 保存消息正文，Inbox 记录某个用户或设备应该补看的消息指针。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Message/Inbox tables store the message body and per-user or per-device pointers to messages that should be delivered or caught up.

termDefinitions.meaning: outbox 模式：在同一个数据库事务里写业务数据和待发布事件；后台 relay 读 outbox 后再 publish，避免 DB 成功但消息没发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The outbox pattern writes business data and pending events in the same database transaction; a relay later publishes them, avoiding a DB success with a lost publish.

termDefinitions.meaning: outbox relay：轮询或订阅 outbox 表的后台进程，负责把未发布事件发到 Pub/Sub、Streams、Kafka 或 SQS。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An outbox relay is a background process that reads unpublished outbox rows and sends them to Pub/Sub, Streams, Kafka, or SQS.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Streams：Redis 的追加式日志，可保留一段历史并让消费者按 ID 追赶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Streams is an append-only Redis log that can retain history and let consumers catch up by ID.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS（Simple Queue Service）：AWS 的托管消息队列服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, or Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed message queue.

q_en: What's the correct fix?
scenario_en: A chat system uses Pub/Sub for online real-time delivery, but product requires that users coming back online can catch up on messages they missed while offline.
optionExplanations: 错：Pub/Sub 本身就不持久化，缓冲区调再大也没用——离线时消息压根没有落地保存，无从补发。
错：想尽办法不让连接断开不现实，手机切后台、网络抖动都会断线，这不是能靠工程手段消除的前提。
错：把实时投递全改成轮询会牺牲实时性、还加大压力，而且照样解决不了「离线期间的消息去哪查」这个根本问题。
对：广播机制天生只喊得到当下在线的人；想让人下线后还能补看，就得另外找个能持久化、可重读的地方存一份，比如日志/队列或收件箱表。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Pub/Sub itself isn't persistent — a bigger buffer doesn't help, since while offline the message was never stored to resend.
Wrong: guaranteeing a connection never drops isn't realistic — phones backgrounding and flaky networks will disconnect regardless.
Wrong: switching everything to polling sacrifices real-time delivery and adds load, and still doesn't answer where offline messages live.
Right: Pub/Sub only notifies subscribers online right now; catching up offline needs a separate durable log/queue or a Message+Inbox table.

scenario: 你不直接用 Redis 原生 SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH，而是自己在 Redis 里维护一个注册表：topic:room123 -> {chat-server-a:9000, chat-server-b:9000}。原生 Pub/Sub 也有 TCP/TLS，但那是 chat server 到 Redis 的 Redis client 连接；自制方案里，发布者查集合后还要自己逐个 HTTP/TCP/gRPC 直发给订阅者服务器。
q: 「自制 Pub/Sub」（Redis 里存 topic → 订阅者地址集合，发布者自己逐个直发）相比原生 Pub/Sub 的缺点有哪些？（多选）
options: 网络跳数从 2 跳变成 3 跳
发布者要维护到订阅者服务器的连接；没有连接池就要临时建 TCP/TLS
订阅者宕机后要靠心跳/TTL 清理注册表，复杂且啰嗦
发布的消息体大小会受到限制
why: 原生 Pub/Sub 复用 chat server 到 Redis 的 TCP/TLS 连接，Redis 维护订阅并 push。自制只让 Redis 存地址，发布者查表后自己 fanout；连接池、重试、背压和旧地址清理都归应用。
why_en: Native Pub/Sub still uses TCP/TLS, but it reuses established Redis client connections from chat servers to Redis; Redis maintains channel-to-connection state and pushes over those connections. In a homegrown design, Redis only stores addresses, so the publisher fans out itself and owns server-to-server pools, TLS, retries, backpressure, health checks, and stale-address cleanup.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经有一套成熟的 service mesh、长连接池、健康检查和路由层，自制直发可以降低 Redis 数据面压力；但这时你其实是在重建一个消息路由系统，复杂度要算进去。
options_en: The network hop count goes from two hops to three
The publisher must maintain connections to subscriber servers; without a pool it pays TCP/TLS setup
A dead subscriber needs heartbeats or a TTL to clean up the registry, which is complex and chatty
The published message body size becomes limited
tradeoff: 原生 Pub/Sub 复用 Redis 的订阅连接/生命周期管理 vs 自制方案把路由和清理责任推给应用
codeSample:
# Native Pub/Sub: chat server keeps one Redis client connection open.
# The connection may be plain TCP or Redis TLS, depending on config.
SUBSCRIBE room:123
PUBLISH room:123 '{"text":"hi"}'
# Redis pushes to subscribers on their existing Redis connections.

# Homegrown registry: Redis stores addresses, not live Pub/Sub pipes.
SADD topic:room:123:subscribers chat-server-a:9000 chat-server-b:9000
SMEMBERS topic:room:123:subscribers

# Publisher must fan out server-to-server itself.
# rpcPool.send("chat-server-a:9000", message)
# rpcPool.send("chat-server-b:9000", message)

# It must also clean stale subscriber addresses.
SET subscriber:chat-server-a:9000:heartbeat 1 EX 30
SREM topic:room:123:subscribers chat-server-a:9000  # when lease expires

    S2["Subscriber server B"] <-->|"Redis client TCP/TLS"| R1
    P1["Publisher"] -->|PUBLISH room:123| R1
    R1 -->|push on existing connection| S1
