termDefinitions.meaning: 原生 Pub/Sub：Redis 自己维护频道和订阅连接的关系，发布时 Redis 直接把消息推给当前在线订阅者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Native Pub/Sub means Redis maintains the channel-to-subscriber-connection mapping and pushes messages to currently connected subscribers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自制 Pub/Sub：应用自己用 Redis 存 topic 到订阅者地址的注册表，并由发布者自己 fanout 到这些地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Homegrown Pub/Sub stores topic-to-subscriber-address mappings in Redis and makes the publisher fan out to those addresses itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 注册表：记录谁订阅了哪个 topic 的元数据表；自制方案需要维护它的新鲜度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A registry is metadata recording who subscribes to which topic; a homegrown design must keep it fresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 订阅者服务器：这里指订阅某个 topic 的 chat server 实例，不是用户手机；它负责再把消息推给自己连接着的客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A subscriber server here is a chat-server instance subscribed to a topic, not the user's phone; it later pushes messages to its connected clients.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP（传输控制协议）：建立连接后可靠传输字节流的协议，新建连接有握手开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP, or Transmission Control Protocol, is a connection-based reliable byte-stream protocol whose handshake adds setup cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis client connection：应用服务器到 Redis 的已建立连接；SUBSCRIBE 后 Redis 会在这条连接上持续推送消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis client connection is an established connection from the application server to Redis; after SUBSCRIBE, Redis pushes messages over that same connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: TLS：给 TCP 连接加密和校验身份的一层；Redis 可以配置 TLS 端口，但这不改变 Pub/Sub 的订阅模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS encrypts a TCP connection and can authenticate peers; Redis can be configured with a TLS port, but that does not change the Pub/Sub subscription model.

termDefinitions.meaning: heartbeat/TTL：订阅者定期续租自己的注册记录；如果停止续租，系统认为它已死并清理地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat/TTL lease means subscribers periodically refresh their registry entry; if they stop, the system treats them as dead and cleans up the address.

q_en: Compared to native Pub/Sub, what are the drawbacks of a homegrown Pub/Sub built on Redis (storing topic-to-subscriber-address sets, with the publisher fanning out directly)? (multi-select)
scenario_en: Instead of using Redis native SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH, you maintain your own registry in Redis: topic:room123 -> {chat-server-a:9000, chat-server-b:9000}. Native Pub/Sub also uses TCP/TLS, but that is the Redis client connection from a chat server to Redis. In the homegrown design, after reading the set, the publisher must send directly to subscriber servers over HTTP, TCP, or gRPC.
optionExplanations: 对：原生只需 chat server→Redis 这一跳给 Redis 处理；自制多了「查完注册表再逐个直发」这一跳，变成三跳。
对：原生方案蹭的是 chat server 本来就连着 Redis 的那条线；自己搭的话，发布者得给每台订阅者服务器单独握手建连，没有连接池就更慢更重。
对：注册表里的地址不会自动过期，订阅者宕机后要么靠心跳、要么靠 TTL 主动清理，逻辑全部自己写，比原生零维护啰嗦得多。
错：消息体大小限制不是自制方案独有的缺点，原生 Pub/Sub 同样有类似的实现限制，这不是两者的关键差异点。
optionExplanations_en: Right: native only needs one hop, chat-server-to-Redis, and Redis handles delivery; homegrown adds a second hop of registry lookup plus direct fanout — three hops.
Right: native reuses the chat server's existing connection to Redis; homegrown makes the publisher open its own TCP/TLS to every subscriber server.
Right: registry addresses don't lapse on their own — a subscriber's crash needs heartbeats or a TTL to clean it up, all hand-rolled.
Wrong: a message-size limit isn't a homegrown-specific drawback — native Pub/Sub has comparable implementation limits too.

q: 原生 Pub/Sub 里，一个频道的最后一个订阅者断开后会发生什么？
options: 频道会在内存里继续保留 24 小时才清理
频道从内存移除，之后对它的 publish 直接被丢弃
没有订阅者时，消息会开始堆积排队等待
publish 会向发布者返回一个错误提示
why: Redis 只为有活跃订阅者的频道占内存；没人听的频道就不存在，发了也就丢了——零清理成本。
why_en: When the last subscriber disconnects the channel vanishes from memory and later publishes to it are simply dropped.
options_en: The channel stays reserved in memory for 24 hours before cleanup
The channel is removed from memory and later publishes to it are simply dropped
With no subscribers, messages start queuing up waiting to be read
The publish call returns an error back to the publisher
q_en: In native Pub/Sub, what happens when a channel's last subscriber disconnects?
optionExplanations: 错：频道没有「保留 24 小时」这种缓冲期，最后一个订阅者一走，频道立刻不再存在。
对：只有还有人在听的频道才会占一点内存；没人听了它就等于不存在，往上面发东西也是白发——不用你操心清理。
错：Pub/Sub 不落盘也不排队，没有订阅者时消息不会堆积等待，而是直接被丢弃。
错：往一个没人监听的频道 publish 不会报错，Redis 正常处理这次调用，只是没有订阅者能收到而已。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: there's no 24-hour grace period for a channel — the moment the last subscriber leaves, the channel simply stops existing.
Right: Redis only spends memory on channels with active subscribers; an unwatched channel doesn't exist, so a publish to it is just dropped.
Wrong: Pub/Sub doesn't persist or queue — with no subscriber, a message doesn't pile up waiting, it's just discarded.
Wrong: publishing to a channel nobody's listening on doesn't error — Redis processes the call fine, it just has no subscriber to deliver to.

q: 100 节点的 Redis 缓存集群，某个商品突然爆红、流量占到全站一半，会发生什么？
options: 集群检测到热点后会自动触发一次槽再均衡
这份流量会被所有 100 台节点平均分摊
Redis 检测到热点后自动把这个 key 复制到多个节点
拥有这个 key 的那台节点负载暴涨、开始失败，其余 99 台闲着
why: key 哈希决定归属：一个 key 只住一台节点，节点再多也分不走单 key 的流量——这就是 hot key 问题（Memcached、DynamoDB 同样有）。
why_en: A single hot key lives on one node, so that node melts while the other ninety-nine idle, a problem Memcached and DynamoDB share.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Hot key"] --> B["One slot node hot"]
  B --> C["Replicas or key copies"]
  C --> D["Fan out reads"]
options_en: The cluster detects the hot spot and automatically triggers a slot rebalance
That traffic gets evenly shared across all one hundred nodes
Redis detects the hot spot and automatically replicates this key across nodes
The one node owning this key sees load spike and starts failing while the other ninety-nine sit idle
q_en: In a 100-node Redis cache cluster, a single product suddenly goes viral and its traffic hits half the whole site — what happens?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 不会因为检测到某个 key 热就自动触发槽再均衡，槽的归属不会因流量突增而自己变化。
错：一个 key 的哈希结果固定映射到一个槽、一个节点，流量不会因为集群有 100 台节点就自动摊开。
错：Redis 没有内建「检测热点自动复制 key 到多节点」的机制，这是需要应用层自己做的缓解手段。
对：某个 key 归谁管是哈希算出来的、固定住在一台机器上，就算集群再大，这个 key 的流量也只会砸在那一台上，别的全在旁边看戏。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis doesn't auto-trigger slot rebalancing just because it detects a hot key — ownership doesn't shift itself from a traffic spike.
Wrong: a key's hash maps to a single fixed slot and node; traffic doesn't spread out just because the cluster has 100 nodes.
Wrong: Redis has no built-in 'detect hot key, auto-replicate it' mechanism — that's a mitigation you build in the app layer.
Right: key hashing fixes ownership — a key lives on exactly one node, so that one node absorbs the traffic while the rest sit idle.

scenario: 少数几个爆款商品被海量读取，可以容忍秒级陈旧，希望大部分读请求根本不打到 Redis。
q: 最合适的缓解是？
options: 应用服务器进程内缓存这几个最热 key（配短 TTL）
单纯加大拥有热 key 的那台 Redis 节点的内存
把持久化模式从 RDB 换成 AOF
把集群的哈希槽总数从 16384 再调大
why: 应用服务器进程本身有内存，可放一个很小的 TTL map。读路径先查本机内存，miss 才查 Redis/DB；题目要求多数读不碰 Redis，所以本地挡热比 Redis 副本更贴合。
why_en: The app server process has its own memory, so it can keep a tiny TTL map. Reads check local memory first, then Redis/DB on miss; because the prompt wants most reads to avoid Redis entirely, local hot-key caching fits better than Redis replicas.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标只是别打爆 Redis primary，显式副本读或 key 副本也对；如果库存、余额这类不能陈旧，就不要用本地 TTL 缓存做正确性来源。
options_en: Cache the handful of hottest keys in-process on the app servers, with a short TTL
Just give the Redis node that owns the hot key more memory
Switch the persistence mode from RDB to AOF
Increase the cluster's total hash slot count beyond 16384
tradeoff: 本机内存挡住 Redis 热读 vs 每台 app 都有一份短暂旧值
codeSample:
localCache = TTLCache(maxKeys=100, ttl=2s)

getProduct(id):
  if localCache.has(id):
    return localCache.get(id)      # no Redis hop

  v = redis.get("product:" + id)
  if v == nil:
    v = db.queryProduct(id)
    redis.setex("product:" + id, 30s, v)

  localCache.set(id, v)            # per app process memory
  return v
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Req["read product:123"] --> App["App server"]
  App --> L["in-process TTL cache"]
  L -- hit --> Done["return stale-ok value"]
  L -- miss --> R["Redis"]
  R -- miss --> DB["Database"]
  R -- value --> App
  DB -- row --> App
  App --> L

termDefinitions.meaning: in-process cache：缓存存在应用服务器进程自己的内存里；每台 app 实例各有一份，不跨实例自动共享。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-process cache lives in the app server process memory; each app instance has its own copy and it is not automatically shared.

termDefinitions.meaning: local TTL：本机缓存只活几秒，允许少量陈旧，用自动过期换极低延迟和少打 Redis。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A local TTL keeps a value only for a few seconds, accepting slight staleness in exchange for very low latency and fewer Redis hits.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis replica read：把读摊到 Redis 副本，能保护 primary，但请求仍然会进入 Redis。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis replica reads spread traffic across Redis replicas and protect the primary, but requests still hit Redis.

q_en: What's the best mitigation?
scenario_en: A handful of viral products get read at massive volume, second-level staleness is tolerable, and you want most reads to never hit Redis at all.
optionExplanations: 对：应用进程自己就有内存，拿一小块出来做个带过期时间的本地缓存；读的时候先看本机有没有，没有才去问 Redis/DB，大部分请求根本不用出这台机器。
错：加大内存能多存数据，但改变不了「一个 key 只住一台节点」这个事实，热点流量还是全打在那一台上。
错：换持久化模式解决的是数据落盘/丢失问题，跟一个 key 被海量读打爆没有关系。
错：哈希槽总数固定在 16384，调大槽数改变不了某个具体 key 归属哪个节点，热 key 依然集中在一台机器上。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the app server has its own memory — put a tiny TTL map there; reads check local memory first and only hit Redis/DB on a miss.
Wrong: more memory lets that node hold more data, but doesn't change the fact that a key lives on exactly one node.
Wrong: switching persistence mode addresses durability/data loss, unrelated to one key getting hammered by reads.
Wrong: the slot count is fixed at 16384; raising it wouldn't change which single node a given key belongs to.

scenario: 一个读热 key 想横向摊到多台节点上，读方代码可以配合改造。
q: 「key 副本」方案怎么做？
options: 只是把 key 的名字改得更短一点，指望能减少内存占用
同一份数据存成 product:123:1..10 多个 key 散到不同槽，读者随机挑后缀读
用 hash tag 反而把这些数据副本全部绑到同一个槽上
打开集群自带的代理转发模式，指望它来分摊流量
why: 带不同后缀的 key 哈希到不同节点，读流量被随机打散；代价是每次写要扇出到所有副本，读者还得知道哪些 key 被复制过。
why_en: Storing copies under suffixed keys spreads them across nodes and readers pick a random suffix, while every write must fan out to all copies.
whenOtherWins: 写频繁的 key 不适合（写扇出放大）；那种情况优先在数据模型上拆分，或用副本读扛读热。
options_en: Just shorten the key's name a little, hoping that alone uses less memory
Store the data under suffixed keys like product:123:1 through 10 spread across slots, readers pick a random suffix
Use a hash tag to pin all of these data copies onto that very same slot instead
Turn on the cluster's built-in proxy forwarding mode, hoping it spreads the traffic
tradeoff: 读流量摊到多节点 vs 每次写扇出到全部副本的额外成本
q_en: How does the 'key copies' approach work?
scenario_en: You want to spread a read-hot key horizontally across multiple nodes, and the reader code can be changed to cooperate.
optionExplanations: 错：把 key 名字改短只影响内存占用，不会改变它落在哪个槽，热点流量照样集中在同一台节点。
对：带不同后缀的多份同数据（如 product:123:1..10）哈希到不同节点，读者随机挑一个后缀读，流量被摊到多台机器上。
错：hash tag 是故意把相关 key 绑到同一个槽，跟「key 副本」要把流量分散到多个槽的目标正好相反。
错：Redis Cluster 本身没有内建的代理转发模式帮你自动分摊，路由和副本选择要客户端自己实现。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: shortening the key name only affects memory footprint, not which slot it lands on — the hot traffic still concentrates on one node.
Right: storing several copies of the same data under different suffixes (e.g. product:123:1..10) hashes them to different nodes; readers pick a suffix at random.
Wrong: a hash tag deliberately pins related keys to the same slot — the opposite of what key replication is trying to do.
Wrong: Redis Cluster has no built-in proxy-forwarding mode that auto-spreads traffic for you — routing is on the client.

scenario: 一个商品详情 key 读爆了，你给拥有该 slot 的 primary 加了两个 replica，期望读流量自动分摊到副本上。
scenario_en: A product-detail key becomes read-hot. You add two replicas for the primary that owns the slot and expect reads to automatically spread to replicas.
q: 用读副本（read replicas）抗热 key，面试官爱追问的两个坑是？
options: 副本运行成本更贵，读取延迟也比主节点更慢
副本节点根本无法部署到别的机房或可用区
集群客户端默认仍读主节点（须显式配置副本读）；且对写热 key 毫无帮助
只要存在多个副本就会直接导致集群出现脑裂
why: Redis Cluster 客户端默认把 GET 发到 slot primary；副本不会自动分担读流量。要显式启用 replica read/READONLY，且只帮读热 key；SET、INCR 等写热 key 仍打 primary。
why_en: Redis replicas do not automatically serve cluster reads; enable replica reads or READONLY explicitly, and remember this helps read-hot keys, not write-hot keys.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务必须读到刚写入的新值，如库存扣减后的立即校验、支付状态确认，就不要随便读 replica；可以读 primary、做读己之写路由，或用短 TTL 客户端缓存承受可控陈旧。
options_en: Replicas cost more to run and add extra read latency versus the primary
Replica nodes simply cannot be deployed to a different region or availability zone
Cluster clients still read the primary by default (replica reads must be explicit), and replicas do nothing for write-hot keys
The mere existence of multiple replicas directly causes cluster split-brain
tradeoff: 副本读扩展读吞吐 vs 异步复制带来的陈旧读风险
codeSample:
# Cluster protocol idea: a replica can serve reads only after READONLY.
redis-cli -c -h replica-node
READONLY
GET product:123

# Client-library idea: names vary by library.
# Java Lettuce:
connection.setReadFrom(ReadFrom.REPLICA_PREFERRED)

# Node ioredis:
new Redis.Cluster(nodes, { scaleReads: "slave" })  # library name for replica reads
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["Cluster client"] -->|default GET/SET product:123| P["primary for slot 9421"]
  P -->|async replication| R1["replica 1"]
  P -->|async replication| R2["replica 2"]
  C -.explicit replica read / READONLY.-> R1
  C -.explicit replica read / READONLY.-> R2
  W["write-hot traffic"] -->|still primary only| P

termDefinitions.meaning: read preference：客户端的读路由策略，比如只读 primary、优先读 replica、或 primary/replica 混读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read preference is the client's read-routing policy, such as primary-only, replica-preferred, or mixed primary/replica reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: READONLY：Redis Cluster 里发给 replica 连接的命令，允许该连接从 replica 读取它所复制的 slot 数据；读到的值可能落后 primary。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: READONLY is a Redis Cluster command sent on a replica connection to allow reads for the slots it replicates; returned data may lag behind the primary.

termDefinitions.meaning: replication lag：replica 落后 primary 的时间或数据量，是副本读可能读到旧值的根源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication lag is how far a replica trails the primary in time or data, which is why replica reads can be stale.

q_en: When using read replicas to absorb a hot key, what two pitfalls do interviewers love to probe?
optionExplanations: 错：这不是面试官爱追问的坑——真正的坑在于「加了副本流量并不会自动跟着分流」，而不是成本或延迟本身。
错：副本完全可以部署到别的机房/可用区做异地容灾，这不是它抗热 key 时的限制点。
对：默认情况下客户端的读请求照样直奔主节点，副本不会自动接手，得手动打开读副本这个开关；而且这招对写操作扎堆的热 key 完全没用。
错：多个副本本身不会直接导致脑裂，脑裂通常跟 failover/网络分区时的选主逻辑相关，不是「存在副本」这件事本身。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that's not the trap interviewers probe for — the real gotcha is that adding replicas doesn't automatically redirect any traffic to them.
Wrong: replicas can absolutely be deployed to a different region/AZ for disaster recovery — not the limitation for hot-key mitigation.
Right: a Redis Cluster client defaults to sending GET to the slot's primary; replicas need explicit reads enabled, and none of this helps a write-hot key like INCR/SET.
Wrong: having multiple replicas doesn't by itself cause split-brain — that's usually about failover/partition election logic.

q: 把「热 key 应对」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 缓解：客户端缓存 / key 副本 / 副本读，按读热还是写热选择
现象：单个爆款 key 的流量激增
代价：多副本会读到旧值，写入或删除也要同步到更多地方
诊断：key 哈希到唯一节点，单节点过载而集群其余空闲
why: 缓存一致性不是“建集群”，而是同一份值有多份缓存后，更新时如何避免长期读旧值。热 key 多副本能分散读流量，但每次写入、删除或失效都要同步更多地方。
why_en: Cache consistency is not just building a cluster. It is the problem of keeping multiple cached copies of the same value from staying stale after an update. Replicating a hot key spreads reads, but writes, deletes, and invalidations must touch more places.
q_en: Put the decision chain for handling a hot key in the correct order:
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Hot["hot key: product:123"] --> One["one Redis shard overloaded"]
    One --> A["client cache"]
    One --> B["key copies: product:123:0..N"]
    One --> C["replica reads"]
    A --> AC["risk: local stale value"]
    B --> BC["cost: write/delete fanout"]
    C --> CC["risk: replica lag"]

rows: App 本地短 TTL 直接命中
更新后本地副本可能短暂旧
读随机打到 N 份 copy
写入/删除要扇出到 N 份
读 Redis replica 分担主库
复制延迟下可能读旧值

termDefinitions.meaning: 少数 key 承接大量请求，导致它所在的 Redis 分片过载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a key that receives so many requests that the Redis shard owning it becomes overloaded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份数据有多个缓存副本时，更新后如何让读请求别长期读到旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache consistency is the problem of preventing reads from seeing stale cached copies for too long after the data changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次业务写入需要更新、删除或失效多个缓存副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means one logical write has to update, delete, or invalidate multiple cached copies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把读请求打到 Redis replica 来分担主节点压力，但可能受到复制延迟影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replica reads send reads to Redis replicas to reduce primary load, but can observe replication lag.

q: 哪些信号说明这个场景不该用 Redis？（多选）
options: 数据是唯一的真相源，一条都不能丢
工作集大到放内存不经济
需要 join、跨 key 的灵活查询
需要亚毫秒级读取
why: 异步复制 + 持久化窗口意味着已确认写可能消失；内存是最贵的存储位置；Redis 没有 join。亚毫秒读恰恰是「该用 Redis」的理由。
why_en: Avoid Redis as a system of record, for working sets too big for RAM, or when you need joins and cross-key queries; sub-millisecond reads are exactly why you would use it.
options_en: Data is the single source of truth and none of it can be lost
The working set is too big to fit in RAM economically
You need joins or flexible cross-key queries
You need sub-millisecond reads
q_en: Which signals indicate Redis is the wrong choice for this scenario? (multi-select)
optionExplanations: 对：异步复制+持久化窗口意味着已确认写入可能在 failover 时消失，不适合当唯一真相源。
对：内存是最贵的存储位置，工作集一旦大到放内存不经济，就该考虑磁盘型存储而不是硬塞进 Redis。
对：Redis 没有跨 key 的 join 能力，需要灵活关联查询的场景该用支持这类查询的数据库。
错：读取能做到亚毫秒级，正是选它的加分项，不是拒绝它的信号，这个选项说反了方向。
optionExplanations_en: Right: async replication plus a persistence window means a confirmed write can vanish on failover — not a fit as the single source of truth.
Right: memory is the most expensive place to store data — once the working set is too big to fit economically, look at disk-based storage instead.
Right: Redis has no cross-key join capability; a case needing flexible relational queries should use a database built for that.
Wrong: sub-millisecond reads are exactly the reason TO use Redis, not a signal against it — this option points the wrong direction.

scenario: Redis Cluster 把 key 分到 16384 个 hash slot，每个 slot 归一个主节点。你想一条命令同时写两个 key，比如 MSET user:1:name A user:1:age 20，或者用 MULTI/EXEC 把两个 key 一起改掉。
scenario_en: Redis Cluster maps keys into 16,384 hash slots, with each slot owned by one primary node. You want one command to touch two keys, such as MSET user:1:name A user:1:age 20, or a MULTI/EXEC transaction that updates two keys together.
q: 集群模式下多 key 操作（MSET、含多个 key 的 MULTI）的限制是？
options: 所有 key 必须落在同一个槽（hash tag 可以安排到）
集群模式完全不支持任何形式的多 key 命令
跨槽的多 key 操作会自动做两阶段提交协调
跨槽情况下只支持只读的多 key 命令
why: MSET/MULTI 必须在一个节点完成；不同槽归不同主，Redis Cluster 不做跨节点事务协调，会报 CROSSSLOT。用相同 hash tag 可把相关 key 放同槽。
why_en: MSET or a MULTI transaction must execute on one node. If the keys map to different slots, they belong to different primaries, and Redis Cluster does not run a cross-node transaction coordinator; it returns a CROSSSLOT error. Use a shared hash tag when those keys must be operated on together.
options_en: All keys must land in the same slot (a hash tag can arrange this)
Cluster mode does not support any form of multi-key command at all
A cross-slot multi-key operation automatically runs two-phase commit coordination
Across slots, only read-only multi-key commands are supported
codeSample:
# Same hash tag -> same slot -> one node can run the command.
MSET user:{1}:name A user:{1}:age 20

# Likely different slots -> different primaries -> CROSSSLOT.
MSET user:1:name A user:2:name B

# Same rule for MULTI/EXEC: all touched keys must share one slot.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["MSET key1 key2"] --> B{"same hash slot?"}
  B -->|yes| C["one primary executes it"]
  B -->|no| D["different primaries"]
  D --> E["CROSSSLOT, no 2PC"]

termDefinitions.meaning: MSET：一条 Redis 命令里同时设置多个 key-value；在 Cluster 中这些 key 必须同槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSET is a Redis command that sets multiple key-value pairs in one command; in Cluster, those keys must share one slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: MULTI/EXEC：Redis 事务，把多条命令排队后一次执行；在 Cluster 中事务触碰的 key 也必须同槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MULTI/EXEC is a Redis transaction that queues commands and executes them together; in Cluster, the touched keys must share one slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: CROSSSLOT：Redis Cluster 发现一条多 key 请求里的 key 不在同一个槽时返回的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CROSSSLOT is the error Redis Cluster returns when keys in one multi-key request do not hash to the same slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: hash tag：key 名里花括号包住的部分；Redis Cluster 只哈希这段，让相关 key 可以被安排到同槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash tag is the part of a key inside braces; Redis Cluster hashes only that part so related keys can be placed in the same slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: two-phase commit：跨节点事务协调协议；Redis Cluster 不会为跨槽 MSET/MULTI 自动做这件事。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a cross-node transaction coordination protocol; Redis Cluster does not automatically do it for cross-slot MSET or MULTI.

q_en: What's the restriction on multi-key operations (MSET, a MULTI touching several keys) in cluster mode?
optionExplanations: 对：这类多 key 命令得在同一个节点上一口气做完；槽分给了不同的主节点就没法跨节点协调，会直接报错，用同一个 hash tag 能把它们摁进同一个槽。
错：同槽内的多 key 命令是支持的，只是要求这些 key 落在同一个槽，不是完全不支持。
错：集群不会主动帮跨槽的多 key 操作做两阶段提交，槽不一致直接就报错了，不存在自动协调这回事。
错：跨槽限制不区分读写——无论是读还是写，跨槽的多 key 命令都不支持，不是「只放行只读」。
optionExplanations_en: Right: MSET/MULTI must complete on one node; different slots belong to different primaries, so Redis Cluster throws CROSSSLOT — a shared hash tag fixes it.
Wrong: multi-key commands are supported as long as the keys land on the same slot — not a blanket 'no multi-key commands' rule.
Wrong: Redis Cluster doesn't auto-coordinate a two-phase commit across slots — a cross-slot op just throws CROSSSLOT, no help offered.
Wrong: the cross-slot restriction doesn't distinguish read from write — cross-slot multi-key commands fail either way.

scenario: Postgres/MySQL 这类数据库允许你写一条比较抽象的 SQL：查用户、过滤状态、按时间排序、再 join 订单表。数据库会先生成多个可能的执行方案，再选一个预计最便宜的方案。Redis 不走这条路：你要提前把数据放成合适的结构，比如 String、Hash、Set、Sorted Set，然后直接调用 GET/HGET/ZRANGE 这类明确命令。
scenario_en: Databases such as Postgres or MySQL let you write a fairly abstract SQL query: find users, filter by status, sort by time, and join an orders table. The database generates possible execution strategies and chooses the estimated cheapest one. Redis does not work this way: you pre-shape data into structures such as String, Hash, Set, or Sorted Set, then call explicit commands such as GET, HGET, or ZRANGE.
q: 相比自带优化器和查询计划器的数据库，Redis 的取向是？
options: 追求比别人更智能的自动优化
刻意保持简单：只把简单操作做到极快，组合方式留给你
把所有实现细节都藏起来
面向复杂的分析型查询设计
why: Redis 不像 SQL 数据库那样替你规划 join、索引选择和排序路径；GET/HGET/ZRANGE 的访问路径由数据结构决定。好处是性能透明、命令快；代价是复杂查询和二级索引要提前建模。
why_en: Redis favors explicit data-structure access over SQL-style planning, which keeps commands predictable but pushes joins, secondary indexes, and complex queries into your model.
options_en: Chasing smarter automatic optimization than everyone else
Deliberately staying simple: make simple operations very fast and leave composition to you
Hiding every implementation detail from you
Designed around complex analytical queries
tradeoff: 数据库自动规划复杂查询 vs Redis 明确数据结构带来的可预测性能
codeSample:
-- SQL database: declarative query; planner chooses indexes/join/order.
SELECT *
FROM orders o
JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE u.status = 'active'
ORDER BY o.created_at DESC
LIMIT 20;

# Redis: explicit access path chosen by your data model.
ZREVRANGE orders:active_users:by_created_at 0 19
HGETALL order:123
diagram:
flowchart LR
  SQL["SQL: what result do I want?"] --> P["Optimizer / query planner"]
  P --> E["Execution plan: index scan, join order, sort strategy"]
  E --> Rows["Rows returned"]

  RQ["Redis command: exact operation"] --> DS["Chosen data structure"]
  DS --> RR["Predictable command cost"]

termDefinitions.meaning: optimizer：数据库里负责比较多种执行方式并选择预计成本最低方案的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An optimizer compares possible execution strategies and chooses the one with the lowest estimated cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: query planner：把 SQL 变成具体执行计划的组件，例如决定用哪个索引、join 顺序和排序方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A query planner turns SQL into a concrete execution plan, such as index choice, join order, and sorting strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: execution plan：数据库最终采用的查询步骤清单，例如 index scan、table scan、hash join、sort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An execution plan is the list of query steps the database will run, such as index scan, table scan, hash join, or sort.

termDefinitions.meaning: access pattern：应用实际怎么读写数据，例如按用户查订单、按分数取排行榜、按时间取最近消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An access pattern is how the application actually reads or writes data, such as fetching orders by user, leaderboard by score, or recent messages by time.

q_en: Compared to databases with a built-in optimizer and query planner, what's Redis's orientation?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 没有比传统数据库更智能的自动优化器，它反而是刻意不做这层规划，把选择权交给你。
对：它不会像 SQL 数据库那样帮你规划怎么 join、走哪个索引、怎么排序，只把几个基础读写命令做到飞快，怎么拼起来是你的事。
错：Redis 恰恰不藏实现细节——访问路径由你选的数据结构决定，命令直接对应底层操作，是透明的，不是黑盒。
错：面向复杂分析型查询设计的是列式 OLAP 引擎，Redis 的取向正相反，是面向简单高频操作。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis doesn't have a smarter auto-optimizer than traditional databases — it deliberately skips that planning layer.
Right: unlike a SQL database planning joins, indexes, and sort paths for you, Redis just makes simple ops like GET/HGET/ZRANGE extremely fast and leaves composition to you.
Wrong: Redis doesn't hide implementation details — the access path is exactly the data structure you chose, transparent rather than a black box.
Wrong: designing for complex analytical queries describes a columnar OLAP engine — Redis's orientation is the opposite.

scenario: Redis 是纯内存存储，重启会丢数据，靠 RDB 快照或 AOF 日志落盘持久化。
scenario_en: Redis keeps data in memory and loses it on restart, so it persists to disk via either RDB snapshots or the AOF log.
q: 关于 RDB 与 AOF 的对比，下面哪个说法正确？
q_en: Which statement about RDB vs AOF is correct?
options: AOF 丢数据窗口更小，RDB 恢复更快
RDB 记录每条写命令，AOF 存周期性全量二进制快照
两者都只把数据放在内存里、根本不写磁盘
AOF 与 RDB 都靠 SSTable 合并来压缩体积
options_en: AOF loses less data on a crash; RDB restores faster
RDB logs every write command while AOF stores periodic full snapshots
Both keep data only in memory and never write to disk
Both AOF and RDB rely on SSTable compaction to shrink in size
why: RDB = 周期性全量二进制快照，恢复快但会丢上次快照后的写；AOF = 顺序追加每条写命令、重放恢复，就是 Redis 的 WAL，最多丢约 1 秒。二者可同时开：AOF 保命 + RDB 快恢复。
why_en: RDB is a periodic full snapshot that restores fast but loses recent writes, while AOF appends writes for replay and usually shrinks the loss window to about one second.
tradeoff: RDB（恢复快 / 可能丢更多） vs AOF（丢得少 / 文件大、恢复慢）

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 周期性把整个数据集存成一份二进制快照文件
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RDB is a periodic full binary snapshot of the entire Redis dataset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序追加每条写命令的日志，重启时重放恢复，相当于 Redis 的 WAL
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF is an append-only log of every write command, replayed on restart — Redis's write-ahead log.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把写顺序追加到日志再应用，崩溃后靠重放日志恢复
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records each write sequentially before applying it, so a crash recovers by replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSTable 是 LSM 存储常见的不可变有序文件格式，不是 Redis RDB 或 AOF 的压缩机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is an immutable sorted-file format used in LSM storage, not how Redis RDB or AOF is compacted.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 是把写先落日志和内存表，再逐层合并磁盘文件的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree writes to a log and memory table first, then compacts sorted disk files in levels.

optionExplanations: 对：AOF 每秒 fsync、丢数据窗口约 1 秒；RDB 直接载入快照、恢复更快。
错：说反了——RDB 才是周期性全量快照，AOF 才是逐条追加写命令。
错：两者都会落盘（AOF 日志 / RDB 快照文件），不是只放内存。
错：SSTable 合并是 LSM 存储的事，Redis 持久化不用 SSTable。
optionExplanations_en: Right: AOF fsyncs every second (~1s loss window); RDB loads a snapshot directly, so it restores faster.
Wrong: it is reversed — RDB is the periodic full snapshot, AOF is the append-per-write log.
Wrong: both write to disk (AOF log / RDB snapshot file), not memory only.
Wrong: SSTable compaction belongs to LSM storage; Redis persistence does not use SSTables.

scenario: 乘客请求要进消息队列——「崩溃也不能丢单」，还想把不同请求分给不同 matcher worker 并行处理。
scenario_en: Ride requests go through a message queue that must not drop a request even on a crash, and different requests should fan out to different matcher workers in parallel.
q: 用 Redis Streams vs Kafka 做这个队列，哪个说法对？
q_en: For this queue, which statement about Redis Streams vs Kafka is correct?
options: Redis Streams 纯内存、崩溃即全部丢失，这种绝对不能丢单的场景只能选 Kafka 来接收
消费组是 Kafka 独有的能力，Redis Streams 只能单消费者、无法把消息分给多个 worker 并行
两者都有消费组分发多 worker；耐久上 Kafka（磁盘+副本）更抗丢，Redis 内存快但保留有限
Redis 的 XACK 和 Kafka 提交 offset 是毫不相干的两套机制，语义上根本不能类比
options_en: Redis Streams is pure in-memory and loses everything on a crash, so a no-drop case must use Kafka
Consumer groups are Kafka-only; Redis Streams has a single consumer and can't fan out to workers
Both have consumer groups to fan out to workers; on durability Kafka (disk+replicas+long retention) is strongest, Redis is faster but retention is limited
Redis XACK and Kafka offset commit are unrelated mechanisms and can't be compared
optionExplanations: 错：有 AOF 持久化 + PEL 兜住在途消息，不是一崩全丢，只是耐久弱于 Kafka 磁盘+副本。
错：消费组（XREADGROUP GROUP）本就是 Streams 的能力，组内按 worker 负载均衡、能并行。
对：正是本题取舍点——分发能力两者都具备，胜负只在耐久强弱。
错：XACK 和提交 offset 语义相同——都是「标记已完成」，不标就会被重投（at-least-once），能类比。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: AOF persistence + a PEL hold in-flight messages, so it is not a total loss — just less durable than Kafka disk+replicas.
Wrong: consumer groups (XREADGROUP GROUP) are a Streams feature; the group load-balances across workers, so it parallelizes.
Right: this is the trade-off — both can fan out; the only real difference is how durable each is.
Wrong: XACK and committing an offset mean the same thing — "mark done"; skip it and the message is redelivered (at-least-once), so they are analogous.
why: 两者都能用消费组把请求分给多个 worker；真正的分水岭是耐久和回放。Kafka 的磁盘副本日志更适合不能丢单，Redis Streams 更低延迟但受 Redis 持久化和保留策略约束。
why_en: Both can fan out with consumer groups; for no-drop queues, Kafka's replicated disk log is safer, while Redis Streams is faster but bounded by Redis persistence and retention.
tradeoff: Redis Streams（内存·低延迟·保留有限） vs Kafka（磁盘+副本·高耐久·可回放·大吞吐）
codeSample:
# Kafka：处理完再提交 offset，失败会从旧 offset 重投
msg = consumer.poll()
process(msg)
consumer.commit(msg.offset)

# Redis Streams：处理完再 XACK，失败留在 PEL 等接管
id, req = XREADGROUP GROUP matchers w1 STREAMS rides >
process(req)
XACK rides matchers id
XAUTOCLAIM rides matchers w2 60000 0-0  # 接管超时未确认消息

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组 worker 共享一个队列，一条消息只发给组内一个 worker，从而把负载分给多台机器
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group lets a set of workers share a queue so each message goes to just one worker — spreading load.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 消费者在某个 partition 里的读取位置；提交 offset = 记下「读到这了」，重启从这继续
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a Kafka consumer's read position in a partition; committing it records progress so restarts resume there.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Streams 里标记一条消息「已处理完」，从 PEL 移除；作用等价于 Kafka 提交 offset
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK marks a Redis Streams message as processed and removes it from the PEL — analogous to committing a Kafka offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费组里「已投递但还没 XACK」的消息列表；worker 死了这些不丢，可被 XAUTOCLAIM 接管重做
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The PEL holds delivered-but-not-yet-acked messages; if a worker dies they survive and can be taken over via XAUTOCLAIM.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka topic 的分区，组内每个分区被一个消费者独占，是并行度与保序的单位（按 key 分区）
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is a slice of a Kafka topic; each is consumed by one consumer in a group — the unit of parallelism and per-key ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个逻辑事件类型一个 topic/stream（如 ride-requests 一个）；并行/保序靠 Kafka 的 partition 或 Redis 的多 stream/消费组——不是一个事件一条 stream
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model one topic/stream per logical event type (e.g. one ride-requests); parallelism/ordering comes from Kafka partitions or multiple Redis streams — not one stream per event.

termDefinitions.meaning: 至少一次投递：处理完才确认(ack/commit)，没确认就重投——保证不丢，但可能重复，业务要幂等
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery: a message is redelivered until acknowledged, so nothing is lost but handlers must be idempotent.

scenario: 用 Redis TTL 锁保护派单，但锁可能在持有者 GC 卡顿时提前过期，两个 worker 都以为自己还持锁。
scenario_en: A Redis TTL lock guards dispatch, but it can expire during a holder GC pause, leaving two workers both thinking they hold it.
q: 光靠锁不够时，下游怎么保证只有一个写生效？
q_en: When the lock alone is not enough, how does the downstream ensure only one write takes effect?
options: 下游做原子条件写或校验 fencing token，拒掉旧持有者的迟到写
只要把锁 TTL 调得足够长，就永远不会在干活时过期，下游无需再防
让两个 worker 都写下游，用 last-write-wins 让最后写的那个覆盖生效
每个 worker 加锁前先随机 sleep 一段，从时间上错开就不会撞
options_en: The downstream does an atomic conditional write or checks a fencing token, rejecting a stale holder late write
Just make the lock TTL long enough that it never expires mid-work, so no downstream guard is needed
Let both workers write downstream and use last-write-wins so the last writer overwrites
Have each worker sleep a random time before locking so they never collide in time
optionExplanations: 对：这才是正确性的最终保证——CAS 或 fencing 让迟到的旧持有者写不进去。
错：再长的 TTL 也可能被 GC/暂停超过，只降低概率不消除，还拖慢故障恢复。
错：last-write-wins 恰好让旧持有者的过期写覆盖新结果，正是要防的。
错：sleep 只是碰运气错开，并发下照样撞，不是正确性保证。
optionExplanations_en: Right: this is the final correctness guarantee — CAS or fencing keeps a stale holder late write out.
Wrong: any TTL can be exceeded by a GC/pause; a longer TTL only lowers the odds and slows recovery.
Wrong: last-write-wins is exactly what lets the stale holder overwrite the new result — the thing to prevent.
Wrong: sleeping just staggers by luck; under concurrency they still collide — not a guarantee.
why: Redis 锁只是在减少并发竞争；真正的正确性要放到下游条件写里。锁过期后旧 worker 醒来时，CAS/版本检查或 fencing token 会拒绝它的迟到写。
why_en: A Redis lock only reduces contention; the downstream store must use CAS, version checks, or a fencing token to reject a stale holder's late write.
tradeoff: CAS（简单·针对某个状态） vs fencing token（更通用·拒绝一切旧持有者写）
codeSample:
-- CAS / 条件写：只有 pending ride 能被派单
UPDATE rides
SET status = 'assigned', driver_id = 'driverB'
WHERE id = 42 AND status = 'pending';

-- fencing：下游只接受更大的 token
UPDATE rides
SET status = 'assigned', fence_token = 35
WHERE id = 42 AND fence_token < 35;

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL 是 key 的存活时间，到点后 Redis 自动删除；锁靠它避免持有者崩溃后永远不释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL means Time To Live, the time before Redis expires a key; locks use it so a crashed holder does not block forever.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC 是运行时回收内存的过程，暂停过久时持锁进程可能错过锁的过期时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Garbage collection reclaims memory, and a long pause can make a lock holder outlive its lease.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子的条件写：仅当当前值等于预期(如仍是 pending)才更新，否则失败——并发下只有一个赢家
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set: an atomic conditional write that updates only if the value still equals the expected one, so only one racer wins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加锁时发的单调递增编号；下游记住见过的最大值，拒绝编号更小的写，从而挡住锁已过期的旧持有者
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing number issued at lock time; the store remembers the max seen and rejects smaller-token writes, blocking a stale holder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 冲突时让最后写入的覆盖之前的；对锁场景是错的，因为迟到的旧持有者会盖掉新结果
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-write-wins lets the latest write overwrite earlier ones — wrong for locking, since a late stale holder can clobber the new result.

scenario: 派单要保证「同一个 ride 只被处理一次」，在 Redis 分布式锁和数据库锁之间选。
scenario_en: Dispatch must ensure a ride is processed only once; choose between a Redis distributed lock and a database lock.
q: Redis 锁 vs 数据库锁，什么时候用哪个？
q_en: Redis lock vs database lock — when do you use which?
options: 高吞吐低延迟用 Redis 锁+下游 fencing；要和业务写同事务、强一致用 DB 锁
数据库锁在任何并发场景都又慢又弱，任何时候都应该用 Redis 锁去替代掉它
两种锁在性能和一致性上完全等价，随便选哪一个都不会有任何区别
Redis 锁天生和业务的数据库写在同一个事务里，所以一致性比 DB 锁更强
options_en: High throughput/low latency: Redis lock + downstream fencing; need the lock and the business write in one transaction / strong consistency: DB lock
A database lock is always slower and weaker in every case, so you should always replace it with a Redis lock
The two locks are completely equivalent in performance and consistency, so pick either one freely
A Redis lock is inherently in the same transaction as the database write, so it is more consistent than a DB lock
optionExplanations: 对：Redis 锁快但会过期、要下游兜底；DB 锁慢但锁和写同事务、天然一致——按吞吐 vs 强一致选。
错：当「锁+写要原子」时 DB 锁反而更强更简单，不是任何场景都劣。
错：两者差别很大——Redis 快但尽力而为，DB 慢但事务内强一致。
错：Redis 锁和 DB 业务写是两个系统、不在同一事务——这恰恰是它需要 fencing 的原因。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a Redis lock is fast but expires and needs a downstream guard; a DB lock is slower but atomic with the write — choose by throughput vs strong consistency.
Wrong: when the lock and write must be atomic, a DB lock is stronger and simpler — not inferior everywhere.
Wrong: they differ a lot — Redis is fast but best-effort, a DB lock is strongly consistent within its transaction.
Wrong: a Redis lock and the DB write are two systems, not one transaction — which is exactly why it needs fencing.
why: Redis 锁快但会过期，所以高频路径要配 CAS/fencing；数据库锁慢些但和业务写在同一事务，适合强一致的「锁+写原子」场景。
why_en: Use Redis locks for high-throughput coordination only with downstream CAS or fencing; use DB locks when the lock and business write must be one transaction.
tradeoff: Redis 锁（快·尽力而为·需下游兜底） vs 数据库锁（慢·锁写同事务·强一致）

rows: 会 TTL 过期→需兜底
和业务写同事务，天然一致
多一个 Redis 要监控

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库行级锁：在事务里锁住选中的行，直到 COMMIT/ROLLBACK 才释放，无 TTL 过期问题
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE takes a row lock held until the transaction commits or rolls back — no TTL expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 应用级咨询锁(pg_advisory_lock)，由应用自己约定用途、不锁具体行，可当分布式锁用
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Postgres advisory lock (pg_advisory_lock) is an app-defined lock not tied to a row, usable as a distributed lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子条件写：只有当前状态仍等于预期时才更新，用来拒绝并发竞争里的迟到写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set is an atomic conditional write that updates only when the current state still matches the expected one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加锁发的单调递增编号，下游只认更大的、拒绝旧持有者的迟到写——Redis 锁的正确性兜底
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing number; the store rejects smaller-token writes, backstopping a Redis lock.

scenario: Redis Cluster 里某个分片的 master 节点挂了,它有几个 replica。
scenario_en: In a Redis Cluster, a shard's master node dies; it has a few replicas.
q: 怎么选出这个分片的新 master?
q_en: How is a new master chosen for this shard?
options: 挂掉 master 的 replica 发起选举、向其他 master 拉票,得多数票者自升为 master 接管槽(集群内置)
由客户端投票,得票最多的那个 replica 被选为新的 master 节点
必须运维人工登录、手动把某个 replica 提升成 master 才行
由外部的 ZooKeeper / 协调服务来指定哪个 replica 当新 master
options_en: The dead master's replicas hold an election, requesting votes from the other masters; the one with a majority promotes itself and takes over the slots (built into the cluster)
Clients vote, and the replica with the most votes becomes the new master
An operator must manually SSH in and promote a replica by hand
An external ZooKeeper / coordination service designates which replica becomes master
optionExplanations: 对:这是节点内部协议;客户端只在选主结束后刷新槽位路由。
错:客户端不参与选主,只接收 MOVED/槽位表变化后改连新的 master。
错:自动故障转移正常会提升 replica;人工提升只是自动化失效时的运维兜底。
错:ZooKeeper 适合自研协调;这张卡问的是 Redis 自带分片集群。
optionExplanations_en: Right: this is Cluster's built-in shard failover; clients only refresh slot routing after the promotion.
Wrong: clients do not vote; they follow MOVED replies or refreshed slot maps and connect to the new master.
Wrong: normal automatic failover promotes a replica; manual promotion is only an operations fallback.
Wrong: ZooKeeper is useful for custom coordination, but Redis Cluster uses votes from its own masters.
why: 多数主节点先判定旧主 FAIL；它的副本随后竞选，拿到多数主节点授权就接管哈希槽。Sentinel 只用于非分片主从，不参与这里。
why_en: After most masters mark the old master FAIL, one replica wins majority authorization, promotes, and takes the hash slots; Sentinel is for non-sharded setups.
tradeoff: Sentinel(非分片主从·独立哨兵进程) vs Cluster 内置(分片·master 互相投票)
whenOtherWins: 如果是非分片的单主多副本 Redis,用 Sentinel 监控并提升 replica;如果是自研服务选主,才考虑 ZooKeeper/etcd 这类外部协调。
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant M as Other masters
  participant R as Replica
  participant C as Cluster clients
  M->>M: mark old master FAIL by majority
  R->>M: FAILOVER_AUTH_REQUEST(epoch)
  M-->>R: vote once per epoch
  R->>R: promote and take hash slots
  R-->>C: gossip / MOVED updates new route

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片集群内置的自动故障转移:旧 master 被多数 master 标 FAIL 后,它的 replica 竞选并接管哈希槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster failover is built into the sharded cluster: after most masters mark the old master FAIL, one replica is elected and takes the hash slots.

termDefinitions.meaning: Sentinel 是 Redis 随附的独立哨兵进程,用于非分片主从部署的监控、通知和自动提升。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sentinel is a separate Redis process for monitoring, notification, and failover in a non-sharded master-replica deployment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次故障转移递增的版本号:保证每个 epoch、每个 master 只投一票,防止双主/脑裂(和 Raft term、fencing token 一个思路)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version number bumped each failover so each master votes only once per epoch, preventing split-brain — the same idea as a Raft term or a fencing token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集群节点之间定期互相交换心跳和路由信息的协议;靠它发现节点挂、传播新的槽归属
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A protocol where cluster nodes periodically exchange heartbeats and routing info; used to detect failures and spread new slot ownership.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 把 key 映射到 16384 个哈希槽,每个槽归某个 master;新 master 接管的就是这些槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster maps keys to 16,384 hash slots owned by masters; failover moves the dead master's slots to the new master.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是外部协调服务,常用于自研选主、配置和租约,但 Redis Cluster 分片选主不依赖它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is an external coordination service for custom leader election, configuration, and leases, but Redis Cluster failover does not depend on it.
